ideas.title: Water Hammer
ideas.hook: One player holds the pipe network on their phone but can't see a single gauge; the other three each hold one valve and one lever, know nothing about what they're connected to, and will burst the whole system if they shut it too fast.

ideas.title: Step Off
ideas.hook: One player holds the only map and three identical dots that won't say which is which — everyone else is a dot with a secret, private reason they never move the way they're told.

ideas.title: Previous Owner
ideas.hook: The room invents the life story of one imaginary object by each writing a different decade of its history — but every phone can only see the entry immediately before its own, so the truth has to be reconciled blind.

ideas.title: Yours Truly
ideas.hook: The room writes one anonymous, sincere letter to a single player — who gets three cuts to name who wrote which line, and every cut permanently scars the keepsake they're about to keep forever.

ideas.title: Temperature Check
ideas.hook: A tiny language model writes one paragraph live on the TV while each player secretly twists one anonymous dial on the sampler, each of them paid only for the tokens where the model's entropy sat inside their own secret band.

ideas.title: Priced In
ideas.hook: Build one sentence together, one word at a time, where every word's cost is how surprised a tiny GPT-2 is to see it — and you win the slot by being the most boring player at the table while trying to score by being the weirdest.

ideas.title: Dead Hand
ideas.hook: A cursor crawls toward the room's shared goal only while nobody is speaking, and steering is handed to a secretly rotating driver — so the moment you say "no, LEFT," you've stopped the thing you're trying to steer.

ideas.title: Per Word
ideas.hook: Before anyone speaks, every player secretly sets a private tax on every other player's talking — so the only way to get paid is to bait someone into a sentence, and baiting costs you your own money.

ideas.title: Your Next Piece
ideas.hook: A versus block-stacker where you don't pick your own pieces — you privately choose what falls into your neighbour's well, from a hand of three increasingly hostile shapes.

ideas.title: Watch My Dot
ideas.hook: A bullet-hell boss fight where the TV shows only the bullets, your phone shows everyone's hitbox except your own, and surviving means four people screaming steering directions at each other.

ideas.title: Do Not Press
ideas.hook: A proxy that slips a plausible `delete_all_backups` tool into your agent's toolbox and tells you, with a confidence interval, how often it reaches for it.

ideas.title: B Horizon
ideas.hook: Type your address and scroll straight down through the actual soil beneath it — real horizon colors, real textures — then pour water and watch it perch on the clay.

ideas.title: Green Bar
ideas.hook: A test runner for prose: your manuscript gets a red/green bar that goes red the moment chapter 12 changes her eye color.

ideas.title: Open Vowel
ideas.hook: Your phone doesn't listen for words — it listens for consonants, so the room can groan, hum and swoop all it likes, but the instant a hard S or T leaves your mouth your channel fills with static.

ideas.title: Reading Distance
ideas.hook: Your phone is both your private clue feed and the snitch that hears you — the only way to say something loud enough for the room is to walk your screen away and let your clues scroll past unread.

ideas.title: That One's Me
ideas.hook: The map-holder gets a half-second radar flash of three identical white dots and has to figure out which dot is which friend before steering any of them home.

ideas.title: Which One's Blue
ideas.hook: You hold the only map and you are screaming correct directions at people whose phones are privately refusing them for reasons nobody in the room can translate into words.

ideas.title: Full Scan
ideas.hook: A single-player roguelike deckbuilder where you are the query planner and every enemy's HP number on screen is only an *estimate* — stale statistics are how you die.

ideas.title: Press Check
ideas.hook: pytest, but the thing under test is the PDF your pipeline just generated — deterministic geometry assertions for overlap and clipping, plus a handful of cached vision-model assertions for the fuzzy stuff.

ideas.title: Arm's Length
ideas.hook: Your phone hands you a secret rule about who you must be standing nearest to, phones range each other with inaudible chirps, and you have 90 seconds to physically herd four adults into position without ever saying what you need.

ideas.title: Off Camber
ideas.hook: Every phone secretly needs to rest at a different impossible angle somewhere in your living room, all at the same time — and the person still hunting for a slope is the one wobbling everyone else's off.

ideas.title: Reading Glasses
ideas.hook: A ten-word sentence is hidden behind boxes on the TV, and every phone shows you a complete, fluent, confidently wrong version of it — the true words are only the ones your four different hallucinations happen to agree on.

ideas.title: Full Stop
ideas.hook: The room writes one sentence together, but after every word the tiny model rolls a die weighted by how much it wants to put a period there — and each phone is secretly praying the sentence dies at a different length.

ideas.title: Four Hands
ideas.hook: One unbroken ink line on the TV, and each phone owns exactly one degree of freedom of the pen — heading, speed, width, or where the page even is.

ideas.title: Remailer
ideas.hook: Your sentence gets laundered through two other people's phones — it only survives on the final printed page if the room can't tell it was ever yours.

ideas.title: Turkish I
ideas.hook: A live disagreement matrix for Unicode case folding that shows you exactly which strings your signup validator calls distinct while your database calls them the same person.

ideas.title: Peer Dependency
ideas.hook: A single-player deckbuilder where the deck is your actual lockfile — every card is a package you really installed, and the ones with real CVEs shuffle curses into your hand at the worst moment.

ideas.title: Still Wet
ideas.hook: Everyone holds one unlabeled slider on one shared generative image, each phone privately previewing a future only its owner can see — and the picture doesn't dry until every hand lifts at once.

ideas.title: Colophon
ideas.hook: The room co-writes one twelve-line house document, then secretly ballots on who wrote what — and only if the room guesses no better than chance does the broadside print, credited entirely to the wrong people.

ideas.title: Under Embargo
ideas.hook: Everyone watches the same 90-second clip — but before it plays, each phone privately shows you one still frame from later in it, and the only way to say what you saw is to move money on a public tote board.

ideas.title: Call the Ball
ideas.hook: You can see the whole board and your three teammates cannot — but the only thing the game lets you send them is one typed word to one person per turn, plus a single veto to cancel one of the three moves they've already locked in blind.

ideas.title: Running Fix
ideas.hook: One player holds the only map — and it has no dots on it, because the three blind pieces stumbling across it each report terrain through a movement pad that's secretly rotated a different way, so the mapholder has to figure out where everyone is before they can steer anyone.

ideas.title: P-Frame
ideas.hook: Inverts a video codec on your own desktop: it throws away every pixel and keeps only the motion vectors, painting the day's window drags, scrolls, and typing as a slowly decaying flow-field wallpaper.

ideas.title: Strictly Necessary
ideas.hook: A SaaS whose entire success metric is deleting a UI element: it proves your site qualifies for the ePrivacy "strictly necessary" exemption, hands you the diff to get there, and a dated memo your lawyer can sign.

ideas.title: Hold Still
ideas.hook: The map only comes into focus when nobody is moving — so the map-holder spends the whole game screaming "WHO IS STILL MOVING?" at three blind people who have no way of knowing it's them.

ideas.title: Traffic Calming
ideas.hook: You hold the only map, three blind drivers are moving at once, and you can only talk to one of them at a time — so stop giving directions and start building walls in front of them.

ideas.title: Double Text
ideas.hook: Three ghostwriters share the keyboard of one person's group chat, each hoarding private constraint cards — and when two of you lunge at the same incoming message, the double-text lands, both cards burn, and the other end goes cold.

ideas.title: Blown Out
ideas.hook: Three phones blink secret light-codes at one webcam in a dark room, and the camera's single auto-exposure is the resource you're all fighting over — two flashes at once and the whole frame whites out, blinding everybody including the player who stayed quiet.

ideas.title: Here Be Charts
ideas.hook: A navigable map of every chart you could make from one dataset, where the named types are just gravity wells with fuzzy borders — and most of the map is valid, useful charts nobody has bothered to name.

ideas.title: Dye Pack
ideas.hook: Every process that reads your `.env` gets its own uniquely-poisoned copy of the secrets, so when a supply-chain worm phones your credentials home, the callback tells you exactly which package, which version, and which minute.

ideas.title: Skipped Hour
ideas.hook: Your Postgres, your Node containers, and your iOS app each believe a different version of what time it is in Cairo — this sells you the calendar of exact future instants where that disagreement becomes an outage.

ideas.title: Free Rider
ideas.hook: Four words have to be said out loud for you to win — but the only words that cost you anything are the ones you say yourself, so the whole room sits there waiting for someone else to pay.

ideas.title: Mountain Valley
ideas.hook: Four people fold one real paper fortune teller from a diagram split three ways across their phones — nobody ever sees the whole instruction, and the object on the table at the end holds eight fortunes in nobody's name.

ideas.title: Fair Copy
ideas.hook: Four friends write one letter at once, each staring at a private mirror of their own writing tics, because the keepsake only prints unsigned if nobody can tell who wrote what.

ideas.title: Two Panels
ideas.hook: Type your address, drag an arrow off your balcony railing, and find out whether the building across the courtyard eats your €400 solar kit — with your real skyline drawn onto the sun-path chart.

ideas.title: Zone A
ideas.hook: An explorable explanation that walks you through building a webcam "blood glucose monitor" with a gorgeous 96%-accurate Clarke grid, then hands you four toggles that prove it was measuring nothing at all.

ideas.title: Gyroid Choir
ideas.hook: Sculpt a triply periodic minimal surface and hear its own Laplace–Beltrami eigenmodes sing back — then listen to the chord reorganize the instant the surface changes topology.

ideas.title: Title Safe
ideas.hook: Everyone's phone shows the same busy photograph — except one, which is cropped 8% tighter and scaled back up, so its owner sincerely misremembers where everything is.

ideas.title: One Seat Over
ideas.hook: Four people watch the same silent dinner-party crime, but one phone's name key is rotated a single seat — so the traitor's testimony is meticulous, sincere, and consistently about the wrong person.

ideas.title: Splitting Hairs
ideas.hook: Wavelength with no psychic: everyone holds a different secret target zone on the same spectrum, you may only speak in examples, and only the median of three locked dials scores.

ideas.title: Answer Key
ideas.hook: Anomia where only the two duelists know a duel started — everyone else hears two people abruptly screaming toothpaste brands and has to reverse-engineer why.

ideas.title: Once a Year
ideas.hook: Design a lump of plastic whose shadow is meaningless gibberish every day of the year except one, when the sun at your exact address drops it into a legible word.

ideas.title: Credit Memo
ideas.hook: Your cloud vendors owe you SLA credits every quarter and quietly bank on you missing the 30-day claim window — this watches the clock, builds the evidence packet, and takes 25% of what it recovers.

ideas.title: Middle Name
ideas.hook: A daily rap sheet for every free proxy on GitHub — which ones are reading your traffic, and which 400 "independent" IPs are secretly one guy with one TLS-intercepting appliance.

ideas.title: Name Drop
ideas.hook: Anomia where your matching symbol is secret: shapes flip on the TV, exactly one other person is watching for the same one you are, and every time you lunge for the buzzer you permanently hand the room a fact about your card.

ideas.title: Bookends
ideas.hook: Wavelength with the psychic dismantled: one player sees where the target is but not what the scale means, and the two people who each own one end of that scale must define it with a single blind-locked word apiece.

ideas.title: Off Tank
ideas.hook: A 60-second raid boss whose aggro table is invisible: you know your own threat number exactly, nobody else's at all, and the only public signal in the room is which way the boss is facing.

ideas.title: Spectator Mode
ideas.hook: A one-life dungeon crawl where dying is a promotion: dead players' phones flip to the full map, but the dead aren't allowed to speak — they can only drop four unlabeled ping icons into the fog the living are stumbling through.

ideas.title: Long Story
ideas.hook: One friend rambles through an anecdote while everyone else silently trades secret prop bets on it — and the only way to steer the story toward your contract is to ask a question the whole room watches you spend.

ideas.title: Closing Bell
ideas.hook: Everyone's watching the same clip with a private bet window open on their phone — but the market slams shut the instant anyone in the room makes a sound, so the moment you lock in, your best move is to cough.

ideas.title: Plane Change
ideas.hook: A Kerbal-style delta-v subway map for occupational licensing: nodes are states, edges are burn costs in dollars, retraining hours, and calendar months, and you plan a route from your license to the one you want — including the gravity-assist detours that beat going direct.

ideas.title: Serial Number
ideas.hook: A public index that scores every discontinued lab instrument on whether you can still *drive* it today — open-source drivers, open protocols, consumables still made — so a $40k HPLC doesn't get scrapped for want of a Windows 7 DLL.

ideas.title: One Look
ideas.hook: The map is on one phone and it burns as it's read — every tile you reveal is gone forever, so the only surviving copy of the dungeon is whatever the other players managed to scribble into their private, character-limited notebooks.

ideas.title: Symbol Table
ideas.hook: One phone holds a map of unlabeled glyphs and no idea what any of them mean; the other phones each privately hold two entries of the legend — and none of them can see the map.

ideas.title: Blind Bearing
ideas.hook: You answer by laying your phone face-down on the floor like a compass needle aimed at something real in the room — a quarter-turn off, because your phone secretly told you to lie, and the moment it touches the ground the screen goes dark and you can't check.

ideas.title: Free Gyro
ideas.hook: Every phone navigates the room by gyroscope alone, so each player's sense of north silently rots at a different rate — and the only cure is physically pressing two phones together to average your lies.

ideas.title: Stuff the Deck
ideas.hook: A co-op deckbuilder where you never see your own deck — you build the deck of the player on your left, and the only person who knows what's in yours is the rival sitting on your right.

ideas.title: Illusory Wall
ideas.hook: Three players race the same lethal 12-room dungeon at once, and the only map is the anonymous messages the dead leave behind — which are worth points whether they're true or not.

ideas.title: Degree Day
ideas.hook: Upload two years of daily sales and it tells an ice cream shop exactly how many dollars each degree of temperature is worth — then hands them a $180 basket of Kalshi weather contracts that flattens the curve.

ideas.title: Binding Precedent
ideas.hook: Git's rerere already remembers how you resolved that conflict — this turns its secret local cache into shared, citable case law your whole team can audit before it auto-applies.

ideas.title: Slow Push
ideas.hook: Three clinicians, one IV line, and each phone can see exactly one of the patient's three vital signs — any two drugs pushed within six seconds of each other react in the tubing and are destroyed, so the only way to survive is to queue out loud while all three of you are certain yours is the emergency.

ideas.title: Clobber
ideas.hook: Three phones, one system clipboard: you copy a string off the shared screen, and in the second before you paste it, someone else's copy silently overwrites it — so your form gets filled with their word, permanently.

ideas.title: Quad Box
ideas.hook: Four clips play at once on a muted split screen and you spend chips buying the right to actually hear one — then get quizzed on whichever quadrant nobody bothered to pay attention to.

ideas.title: Ad Buy
ideas.hook: Before the video plays, you secretly buy 20-second slots of it at sealed auction — then spend the whole runtime talking the room out of skipping your minutes without ever admitting they're yours.

ideas.title: Would Have Anyway
ideas.hook: Point it at your health and habit data and it grades every self-experiment you've ever run against a null model built from your own noise — most of your wins turn out to be regression to the mean, and it will tell you which ones aren't.

ideas.title: Second Ferment
ideas.hook: A generative art vat that ferments on real-world time — you get one feeding a day, opening it early permanently brands the bottle "young," and a finished batch can be poured as starter into the next one, so images inherit lineage like sourdough.

ideas.title: Last One Wins
ideas.hook: A polyglot JSON differential fuzzer that runs the same payload through seven real parsers in seven languages and hands you a map of every field where your services quietly disagree about what the data says.

ideas.title: Passband
ideas.hook: Three faint sounds hide under the room's noise floor and your phone shows you only one narrow frequency band of them — describe it aloud and your own voice fills the band you were reading.

ideas.title: Shoe Leather
ideas.hook: A co-op errand list where every step, and every wave of your hands while arguing, drains a private fuel gauge nobody else can see — so the loudest volunteer may be the one about to go dark.

ideas.title: Bass Trap
ideas.hook: Three sine tones play at once and each phone hears only one of them, so every player is hunting a quiet spot in a different invisible room — and everyone's advice to everyone else is confidently, hilariously wrong.

ideas.title: Still Warm
ideas.hook: A menubar count of how many daemons, cron jobs, containers, and listening ports on your Mac are still faithfully running for absolutely nobody — an abandoned-factory tour of your own machine, with epitaphs.

ideas.title: Custody Chain
ideas.hook: Git blame tells you who wrote a line; this tells you whether it was typed, pasted, or produced by an agent — and paints the map of your codebase no human has ever actually thought about.

ideas.title: Last Known Good
ideas.hook: Weekly, in your own AWS account, we actually restore your Postgres backup, time it with a stopwatch, run your assertions against it, and hand you a cryptographically signed RTO certificate your cyber-insurer will accept.

ideas.title: Chef's Choice
ideas.hook: Nobody orders their own food — each phone secretly serves someone else, secretly bets on how much they'll hate it, and secretly holds one true fact about one person's palate that they don't know you have.

ideas.title: Matched Book
ideas.hook: Everyone watches the same eight-minute clip, but each phone holds a different sliver of insider information — and no bet pays out unless you can talk someone into taking the other side of it.

ideas.title: Personal Effects
ideas.hook: Split a dead relative's estate by talking it out — except every phone lists the same objects under totally different descriptions, so two people claiming "the tall thing" may or may not be fighting over one lamp, and if they are, the movers drop it.

ideas.title: Black Square
ideas.hook: One crossword grid, but every phone holds clues from a different puzzle filled over it — cross a rival's word with the wrong letter and that square turns black forever, killing both of you.

ideas.title: No Mirror
ideas.hook: Three invisible dots must meet in the middle, and your phone shows you everyone's position except your own.

ideas.title: Dead Key
ideas.hook: Everyone must type the exact same word — but six letters on your keyboard silently do nothing, and nobody's six are the same.

ideas.title: Abuse Desk
ideas.hook: A solo forensics roguelike where you pivot through fake WHOIS, cert logs, and passive DNS to map a phishing campaign — and the automation rules you write to go faster become the false positives that wreck your next shift.

ideas.title: Air Seed
ideas.hook: Clamp a piezo to a houseplant and hear it cavitate — a desktop toy that pitch-shifts the ultrasonic clicks a thirsty plant actually makes down into hearing range, so drought becomes a sound in your room.

ideas.title: Free Time
ideas.hook: Truckers lose detention pay because nobody can prove when they arrived — this app builds a broker-proof evidence packet automatically and, more importantly, nags you to send the notification that makes the claim collectible.

ideas.title: Double Cut
ideas.hook: Seven cards, three players, two silent rounds of simultaneous elimination — you all have to agree on which one survives while never once reaching for the same blade.

ideas.title: Two of Three
ideas.hook: Three players stare at the same sixteen cards, but each phone has one whole sense surgically removed — and the only way to win is for every pair to secretly match on the one channel that pair happens to share.

ideas.title: Bury the Needle
ideas.hook: Your phone's compass lies whenever steel is near, so the room's hidden ironwork becomes a treasure map — except one player has a fridge magnet in their pocket and is walking around forging anomalies that vanish when anyone comes back to check.

ideas.title: Angle of Repose
ideas.hook: Every phone privately demands a different tilt, so you go hunting the room for a slanted surface — a sofa arm, a paperback wedge, a shoe — set the phone down, let go, and walk away, and your own footsteps across the floor are what knock it out of band.

ideas.title: Ink Trap
ideas.hook: Four phones are four ink plates of the same print — you can only ever see your own color, the TV shows the composite so blurred you can argue about balance but not detail, and the round doesn't end until all four of you sign off on a picture none of you has seen.

ideas.title: So Do I
ideas.hook: You write one true thing about yourself, and you are forbidden from protecting it — your confession only makes it into the room's keepsake zine if two other people secretly spend a scarce token to say "so do I."

ideas.title: Lay Flat
ideas.hook: A generative art toy that grows a flat sheet with a random non-Euclidean metric until it buckles into a ruffled surface nobody designed — then exports the cut pattern so you can print it on cardstock and watch real paper fold into the same shape.

ideas.title: As Written
ideas.hook: Prediction markets don't blow up because you were wrong — they blow up because the rules text was ambiguous, so this scores every open Polymarket/Kalshi market on how likely its own resolution language is to get disputed, trained on every UMA dispute ever filed.

ideas.title: Tell Time
ideas.hook: Runs your build twice while lying to it about the clock, the hostname, and the dice — then bisects the lies until it can point at the exact source line that made your artifact non-reproducible.

ideas.title: Rally Point
ideas.hook: Three phones drop a pin on the same map, but each of you can see landmarks the others can't — and the only way to meet is to ignore everything you privately know.

ideas.title: Offcut
ideas.hook: Every card you throw away is the only sentence you're allowed to say — dump seven-eighths of your hand and pray the three of you are all clutching the same word.

ideas.title: Sum of Best
ideas.hook: A four-leg speedrun where only you can see your own split, so calling for the reset means convincing the room you choked without any proof.

ideas.title: Just Frame
ideas.hook: Four phones are four links of one fighting-game combo, and every player knows only their own secret timing window — drop it and the TV names you in milliseconds.

ideas.title: Loose Line
ideas.hook: Hide bits in *which* of a paragraph's near-equally-perfect Knuth-Plass line breaks you chose, so a leaked memo can be traced to its recipient from a phone photo of the printout.

ideas.title: No Quorum
ideas.hook: Feed one JSON payload to twelve real parsers in twelve real runtimes and get a disagreement matrix showing exactly where your pipeline will silently lose a number, a key, or a byte.

ideas.title: Noise Ordinance
ideas.hook: The room co-ops on a puzzle that can only be solved by talking, while every player privately needs the room's total decibels to land inside a secret window — and you cannot tell anyone to shut up without making noise.

ideas.title: Cold Joint
ideas.hook: Three phones each steer one axis of a soldering tip under a microscope, and the room's own voices are the hand tremor — talk above a whisper and the bead smears across a trace.

ideas.title: Out of Sorts
ideas.hook: A cooperative pointing game where each teammate's icon board is missing two-thirds of its symbols — so the obvious clue is silently unavailable and nobody can say so.

ideas.title: Everyone But You
ideas.hook: A speed-blurting game where every player can see all the categories except their own — so you never know which shouted word is the one that fouls you out.

ideas.title: Wheel of Six
ideas.hook: A booster draft where nobody passes anything — the pack rotates on the TV while each phone privately watches a different, partly-lying window into what's already been taken.

ideas.title: Reserve Price
ideas.hook: A live auction where the auctioneer is the room itself — every phone privately owns one hidden clause of the item's description, and the only way to raise the price is to leak your clause out loud.

ideas.title: Export Blame
ideas.hook: `git blame` for environment variables: one command that tells you exactly which file, at which line, set the PATH you are actually running.

ideas.title: Runoff
ideas.hook: Type your home address and play the raindrop that fell on your roof as a roguelike run down the real drainage network to the sea.

ideas.title: Coat Hanger
ideas.hook: A single steel wire on your desktop that you bend with the mouse while it rings — the partials glide because you are literally changing the eigenvalues of the rod.

ideas.title: Nobody's Handwriting
ideas.hook: The room co-writes a single letter one word at a time, but every phone privately renders that word in a different stolen handwriting style and nobody ever learns which hand was theirs — the finished letter is beautiful, signed by no one, and undeletable.

ideas.title: Left in the Frame
ideas.hook: Five phones each hold one strip of a single group photo that no one has taken yet — you pose, shoot, and stitch a portrait of the room that only exists as one exported PNG, and one player is secretly trying to never appear in it.

ideas.title: Common Time
ideas.hook: Every phone silently buzzes a different secret tempo against your palm, and the only way the room can find one shared beat is by watching each other's bodies give it away.

ideas.title: Under Tungsten
ideas.hook: Three players each mix the same color from a different secret set of primaries, on a TV where the swatches are shuffled so nobody knows which one is theirs — and when they finally match, the host changes the light and the match falls apart.

ideas.title: Straight Man
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly holds a different absurd punchline and writes a setup line for the room — but only ONE setup gets used, so the perfect feed for your line is also a gift to three rivals you can't see.

ideas.title: Keystone
ideas.hook: Everyone writes one claim; a tiny local model then yanks each secret fact out of its context one at a time, and whoever's card the room's model misses most loudly wins.

ideas.title: Springback
ideas.hook: Draw the wire hook, spring, or hairpin you want, tell it your spool, and it solves the elastica backwards to hand you the over-bend angles and a printable pegboard jig — because the wire always relaxes past where you bent it and nobody does that math by hand.

ideas.title: Second Reading
ideas.hook: Paste a spec, ticket, or contract clause and it doesn't tell you it's ambiguous — it shows you the four different things forty independent readers actually thought you meant, then highlights the exact sentence where the readings fork.

ideas.title: Glass Miles
ideas.hook: A live map of every host your laptop talks to, each one pinned not where GeoIP claims but at the maximum radius the speed of light in fiber allows — so anycast edges, VPN exits, and stale geolocation snap into view as physically impossible claims.

ideas.title: Aiming Off
ideas.hook: You hold the map but not the pieces — the pieces know only what the ground feels like under them, and describing gravel is the entire game.

ideas.title: Palm Rejection
ideas.hook: One player's phone is the whole maze — but steering a piece means holding a finger on it, and that finger covers exactly the part of the map you needed to see.

ideas.title: Run Hot
ideas.hook: The room co-writes one sentence to land inside a target surprisal band, but each phone is secretly rolling its word choices at a different sampling temperature — so someone at the table is physically incapable of being weird.

ideas.title: Wide Berth
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly forbids one word to the same tiny language model, and the TV shows only the mangled sentence it writes while frantically steering around four landmines it can't mention.

ideas.title: Says Who
ideas.hook: Paste a famous quotation and watch its mutation tree grow across 150 years of newspapers — the decade a word swapped, the year the attribution jumped to Mark Twain, and the single OCR'd page that started it.

ideas.title: Weak Bit
ideas.hook: You are the copy-protection engineer at a 1982 floppy-disk games publisher, and the game is not against pirates — it's against the returns desk, because the scheme that stops the crackers also bricks legit drives.

ideas.title: Hung Jury
ideas.hook: Feed one payload to eight real JSON parsers in eight real runtimes and watch them quietly return eight different values — then fail the build.

ideas.title: Eyes Only
ideas.hook: The TV holds the answer key but stays blacked out — exactly one player at a time may reveal it, and while they look, their own phone goes dark.

ideas.title: Word for It
ideas.hook: Nobody's controls have names — the room has to invent a shared vocabulary out loud, mid-panic, faster than the order queue drains.

ideas.title: Aim Assist
ideas.hook: You are hunting someone in the room through a hot-cold meter and nothing else — and the only real targeting data is the noise they make when you nearly hit them.

ideas.title: Item Box
ideas.hook: Four survival-horror attaché cases, one shared loot crate, ninety seconds — and nobody can see the shape of the hole in your bag but you.

ideas.title: One Megahertz
ideas.hook: An infinite chiptune generator that is a real neural net running on a real 6502 — the whole model, player, and 10,000 hours of unrepeating music fit in a 32KB C64 program with no samples in it.

ideas.title: Print the Key
ideas.hook: Steganography whose entire language model is small enough to print on two sheets of paper as QR codes — because the only way LLM stego actually decodes on someone else's machine is if the model is integer-only and bit-exact.

ideas.title: Punch Ticket
ideas.hook: A tachistoscope lab that breeds dashboard status icons your own eyes can identify in 120 milliseconds, in the idiom of hand-drawn 1940s transit passes designed to be forged-checked at a glance.

ideas.title: Off Limits
ideas.hook: Eight options on the TV, two secretly forbidden to you alone — the room must land on one answer everybody is actually allowed to give, and the only way to signal what you can pick is to pick it and fail.

ideas.title: Blind Sort
ideas.hook: Six items, two unlabeled bins, and nobody can see the whole set — you must silently agree on a rule you can never state, using only cards the other players half-share with you.

ideas.title: Dead Draw
ideas.hook: A co-op deckbuilder where the cards you buy are overlays on your own phone's readout of an unreadable signal — and by wave three your engine is so cluttered you have to start deleting it.

ideas.title: Hit Confirm
ideas.hook: The room shares one fighting-game character, each phone secretly knows a different half of the move list, and you have two seconds to prove you can read the pose your neighbor just left behind.

ideas.title: Crush Load
ideas.hook: A menubar glyph for your one commute that says how packed the next train is *for a Tuesday at 8:10* — and, unlike every transit app, visibly admits when the agency is feeding it nothing.

ideas.title: Take Dictation
ideas.hook: A pre-commit hook that blanks out the few tokens in your LLM-written diff you couldn't have produced yourself and makes you type them from memory — and quietly scores every file by how much of it nobody in the repo can reproduce.

ideas.title: Stage Whisper
ideas.hook: A line of text on your page that humans literally cannot see but AI browsing agents read out loud and obey — so you finally know which of your "users" is a robot driving a real Chrome.

ideas.title: Even Money
ideas.hook: A real takeout menu becomes a betting board where one player is the bookmaker — they know the true price, and their job isn't to be right, it's to set a line that splits the room.

ideas.title: Sandbag
ideas.hook: The model's per-word surprise is drawn as a public skyline across one shared sentence — you secretly own one word, you're forbidden from touching it, and the only way to make it surprising is to make everything around it strange.

ideas.title: Early Exit
ideas.hook: Four phones are each secretly wired to a different layer of the same tiny language model, so every player holds a confidently wrong opinion about the next word — and nobody gets the final layer.

ideas.title: Twelve Gores
ideas.hook: A cartography puzzle game where every level is a real printable papercraft globe — cut the sphere into gores, pick a projection per strip, and endure a client who complains that Australia looks stretched.

ideas.title: Mood Ring
ideas.hook: A docs linter that reads grammatical mood instead of prose style, painting every page as a four-color stripe so you can see at a glance where your tutorial mutated into a reference manual halfway down.

ideas.title: Dev Full
ideas.hook: A conformance harness that drags your CLI through the twelve hostile terminals it will actually meet — piped to `head`, redirected to `/dev/full`, Ctrl-C'd mid-render — and hands back a scorecard of how badly it misbehaves.

ideas.title: Pass the Buck
ideas.hook: Every task on your phone must be dumped on another player to execute, and since everyone dumps on whoever sounds least busy, the room reliably overloads the same person and both senders' tasks die.

ideas.title: Sole Source
ideas.hook: Your phone hands you a secret shopping spec, the room is the only supplier, and if two people type the same object's name into their phones the object is publicly burned and both buyers walk away empty-handed.

ideas.title: Sounds Like You
ideas.hook: You're secretly assigned another player to impersonate, and your phone's only live feedback is a meter screaming how much you still sound like *yourself*.

ideas.title: Stop Words
ideas.hook: One sentence is cut into private bands by information content — you're holding "the of and was," someone else is holding "armadillo," and neither of you can see the other's half.

ideas.title: Heads Down
ideas.hook: Your phone offers you a bet on what's about to happen in the clip, but reading the bet takes your eyes off the clip — and for two chips you can shove your card onto someone else's phone at the exact moment they can't afford to look away.

ideas.title: Quiet Period
ideas.hook: Everyone bets on what happens next in a clip playing on the TV — except one phone was privately shown a still frame from forty seconds in the future, and the only way to cash in is to move a price everyone can see.

ideas.title: Ghost Import
ideas.hook: A continuously-updated census of the package names language models invent, ranked by how many models hallucinate the same one — and whether an attacker has already registered it.

ideas.title: Cold Soak
ideas.hook: Your thermostat has been quietly running a free blower-door test for years — this fits the physics and tells you how many hours your house stays livable when the power dies.

ideas.title: Cast Doubt
ideas.hook: A puzzle game where you are a one-token-lookahead C parser, and the only weapon you have is deciding which words are types.

ideas.title: Ready Check
ideas.hook: An MMO raid boss squeezed into four phones, where the one thing your screen refuses to show you is your own debuff — only your two neighbors can see it, and they're busy.

ideas.title: Mosquito Noise
ideas.hook: A paint program where the document isn't pixels — it's the JPEG's quantized DCT coefficients, so you stamp basis functions and locally crank the quantizer, and the file you save is byte-exactly what you painted.

ideas.title: Not Included
ideas.hook: Your "download all my data" export is legally compliant and quietly lossy — this audits the delivered archive against the live API, field by field, and publishes which services silently drop your revision history.

ideas.title: Trade Paint
ideas.hook: Four invisible cars race around a shared ring where nobody can see anyone else — and every crash paints a permanent public skid mark that tells the whole room exactly where you were.

ideas.title: Type Over
ideas.hook: Everyone types into the same 40-character headline at the same time, and any cell two people touch turns into an unusable black scar — so you must verbally carve up a sentence you can all see being destroyed live.

ideas.title: Latent Image
ideas.hook: Your private clue is a photographic plate that fogs permanently under room noise — and only you know how fragile yours is, so you must beg for silence without speaking.

ideas.title: Silent Partner
ideas.hook: Your phone doesn't listen to you — it watches one other player, and you get paid only for the seconds that person keeps their mouth shut.

ideas.title: All Rise
ideas.hook: Your phone silently knows whether you are sitting or standing, everyone holds a different secret rule about when they're allowed to be up, and the TV only ever tells the room how many people are currently standing.

ideas.title: Sound Proof
ideas.hook: Every phone chirps at itself to measure how buried it is, and each player must stash their own phone somewhere in the room that muffles it to a *different* secret degree — without two phones ending up close enough to hear each other.

ideas.title: Line of Descent
ideas.hook: `git blame` that refuses to tell you "chore: run prettier" — it walks back through reformats, renames, and file moves until it finds the commit where the line's meaning actually entered the codebase.

ideas.title: Last Legs
ideas.hook: Before you turn off TLS 1.2, it tells you the three customers who will break, by name, with a drafted email to each.

ideas.title: Own Words
ideas.hook: A leak-tracing watermark that survives being laundered through "rewrite this in your own words" — because it hides in the choices paraphrase can't touch, not in the wording.

ideas.title: Conditions of Sale
ideas.hook: One lot, three bidders, and three different secret auction rulebooks — so you're not just guessing what they'll pay, you're guessing what game they think they're playing.

ideas.title: Comes Around
ideas.hook: A pick-and-pass draft where you score not for what you take but for secretly calling which card will still be in the pack when it wheels back to you.

ideas.title: Great Minds
ideas.hook: Four players interrogate the same oracle at the same time, and any two questions that mean roughly the same thing are both thrown out and displayed side by side on the TV under the words GREAT MINDS.

ideas.title: Smoke Screen
ideas.hook: You and three friends fire one fireworks show into the same sky, and every shell you launch leaves smoke only YOU know the duration of — so the finale belongs to whoever can lie best about how dirty they burn.

ideas.title: Off Book
ideas.hook: The room sits in total silence while everyone privately types insults that a text-to-speech voice whispers into one chosen rival's earbud — and the first person who makes any sound at all is out.

ideas.title: Billable
ideas.hook: A shared machine on the TV only runs on room noise — but every second of your own voice is billed to you personally, so the fastest way to win is to get someone else to do the talking.

ideas.title: Books and Records
ideas.hook: Regulated firms retain every AI chat transcript and none of the system prompts that produced them — this seals the prompt, tools, and retrieved documents into WORM storage as the regulated communication they legally are.

ideas.title: Involute
ideas.hook: A browser synthesizer made of actual gears, where pitch comes only from tooth counts — so equal temperament is physically unbuildable and every chord you make is forced into pure just intonation.

ideas.title: Carried Forward
ideas.hook: Every Linux and BSD distro secretly maintains a private fork of your favorite library — this mines all their patch directories at once and shows you which packages have been quietly held together by strangers for eleven years.

ideas.title: Shorthand
ideas.hook: You write a sentence ending, one other player secretly tries to finish it from the first two words, and each word they nail is worth exactly as many points as the language model found it shocking.

ideas.title: Nose Blind
ideas.hook: A tiny language model rates how weird everything you type is — and your phone shows you everyone's weirdness meter except your own, so the only way to find yourself is to triangulate off the room.

ideas.title: Understeer
ideas.hook: The map-holder can say "two squares north" all they like — you're holding a private hand of four movement cards, none of which is two squares north, and they have to figure out what you actually have from where their token keeps ending up.

ideas.title: Acetate
ideas.hook: One player's phone is the only map of the maze, but it renders nothing on its own — the walls, the pits, and the exit each live in a different blind player's thumb, and only one of them can hold their layer up at a time.

ideas.title: Rod Break
ideas.hook: Turn your phone into a clinical dark adaptometer: after a 45-second bleach it tracks your night vision coming back in real time, finds the exact minute your rods take over from your cones, and shows you what one glance at a bright screen just cost you.

ideas.title: Left the Building
ideas.hook: Every coding agent on your laptop keeps a full plaintext diary of everything you ever pasted at it — this reads all of them, reconstructs which secrets were actually uploaded to whose servers and when, and hands you a dated revocation checklist.

ideas.title: Scatter Bar
ideas.hook: A browser puzzle game where you're the mask designer at a chip fab: draw a shape, watch 193nm light smear it into unrecognizable blobs, then win by adding serifs and sub-resolution assist bars until the printed resist matches the target across the whole dose-focus window.

ideas.title: Wristband
ideas.hook: Everyone's phone shows the room as four colored wristbands — but on one phone, two people's names are wearing each other's bands, so that player keeps sincerely nominating the wrong human and has to figure out which two friends they've been confusing.

ideas.title: Reads High
ideas.hook: Four phones read the same machine, but one is silently miscalibrated — every number that player shouts is honest, true, and in the wrong units, and they have five minutes to reverse-engineer their own error out loud before the room notices.

ideas.title: Attract Mode
ideas.hook: Your screensaver is a deterministic replay of the last ninety seconds you ever played of a game you abandoned — usually your own death, on loop, until you hit a key and take the controller back on that exact frame.

ideas.title: Burn Three
ideas.hook: A roguelike where luck is a physical tape you can see 24 values ahead — and the whole game is arranging who eats the bad rolls, you or the wolf.

ideas.title: Same Bytes
ideas.hook: The same model on four runtimes sees four different prompts — this range-reads GGUF headers straight off Hugging Face and shows you the exact token IDs where your chat template rotted.

ideas.title: Exit Poll
ideas.hook: Nobody sees how the room actually voted — each phone gets two anonymous secondhand reports, one phone's reports contain a person who doesn't exist, and the arithmetic proves someone's feed is cooked without saying whose.

ideas.title: Rev B
ideas.hook: The room builds a machine to a shop manual on their phones — but one manual is the wrong revision, its holder has no idea, and their defense when the line faults is literally true: 'I did exactly what the book says.'

ideas.title: Sufficient Funds
ideas.hook: Every price is public and every wallet is secret, so the TV keeps a live ledger of what each player has *proven* they can pay versus what they've merely *claimed* — and the gap between those two bars is the whole game.

ideas.title: Backdate
ideas.hook: A habit tracker that lets you rewrite your past — and then shows you the blame view, because how often you edit yesterday says more about you than any streak.

ideas.title: Quit Line
ideas.hook: An explorable that subtracts the gravity of "everyone reads the first paragraph" from millions of public web annotations, so you can finally see which sentences actually earned their ink — and exactly where readers gave up.

ideas.title: Off Spec
ideas.hook: A fleet of sandbox accounts quietly re-runs the same API calls every night so you find out that Stripe changed a response shape before your customers do.

ideas.title: Skyline
ideas.hook: Your sentence is never shown to anyone — only the jagged skyline of how surprised the model was, word by word, and you were secretly assigned the shape you had to draw.

ideas.title: Speak Now
ideas.hook: You must announce every move out loud before you make it, because someone else is privately holding the one rule that says this move will blow the whole thing up.

ideas.title: For Instance
ideas.hook: Nobody is told the rule, everyone gets different examples of it, and the room must silently pick the same one item off the TV.

ideas.title: Spot Me
ideas.hook: You are a color you can never see, and the only controls that can change it are in other people's hands.

ideas.title: Body Tide
ideas.hook: A menubar toy that shows how far the solid ground under your desk has risen since 3am — because the Moon stretches the whole planet, not just the ocean, and you go up and down about 30 cm twice a day without noticing.

ideas.title: First Passage
ideas.hook: A menubar app that models your day as a Markov chain and tells you the real price of opening Slack — not the four minutes you spend there, but the twenty-three expected minutes before you touch your editor again.

ideas.title: Always Green
ideas.hook: Audits your CI suite by how many bits of information each required check actually carries about whether a PR is broken, then prints the dollar cost of the ones that have never once told you anything.

ideas.title: Good for It
ideas.hook: Nobody can bet with their own money — to wager on the game on TV you have to privately borrow from another player at a rate you negotiate face-to-face, so the real market isn't the broadcast, it's whether the room thinks you're good for it.

ideas.title: No Action
ideas.hook: Everyone at the party writes one betting line about the movie playing — and the props you refuse to bet on are the only ones you're allowed to referee, so a line nobody passes on can't be scored at all and dies as 'no action'.

ideas.title: Uncredited
ideas.hook: Three phones build one eight-step drum loop at the same time, hearing only the finished mix out of the TV and never their own part alone — and you win by being the one nobody can pick out when the host solos the lanes.

ideas.title: Split Key
ideas.hook: The room writes one sealed message nobody is allowed to read, splits the key across everyone's phones, and then has to survive ninety seconds of a big red OPEN IT button whose count is public but whose fingers are not.

ideas.title: Hand Me Down
ideas.hook: You never draft for yourself — you draft for the person on your left, you only see one third of what they actually need, and the only way to get fed is to beg out loud to the one person feeding you.

ideas.title: Back Channel
ideas.hook: Every pair in the room negotiates a binding trade at the same time, out loud and in private at once — the TV shows the room exactly WHO you're wired to, never what you just sent them.

ideas.title: Bake Off
ideas.hook: Drop a before-and-after pair and it evolves its way backwards to the actual G'MIC command line that made the look — including a de-bake mode that tries to unwind someone else's edit.

ideas.title: Arch Support
ideas.hook: Prediction markets settle on model-launch announcements, but the launch leaks weeks earlier as a pull request adding a new architecture to vLLM — so watch the plumbing, not the press release.

ideas.title: Total Float
ideas.hook: Critical-path scheduling math turned on your own life, so the app can tell you — with a proof — exactly which obligations you are allowed to ignore today.

ideas.title: Salt the Well
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly slips one sentence into the same shared briefing memo, then the model reads that memo and finishes a public letter — and you score in bits, by how much likelier your own secret word got, while the room hunts for whose sentence was the poison.

ideas.title: Bad Line
ideas.hook: You type a clue for your secret word and watch your own sentence get censored live — because the phone line between you and one other player only passes words the language model finds surprising enough (or boring enough), and nobody told you which.

ideas.title: Set a Pick
ideas.hook: Every phone screams a private ultrasonic tone at every other phone, and the only walls you have are each other's bodies.

ideas.title: Powder Dry
ideas.hook: You get a tiny secret ration of noises for the whole round — and since talking burns them at the same rate as playing, planning the round costs you the round.

ideas.title: Not a Word
ideas.hook: Sound is free and words are not — hum, whistle, or bang the table all you like, but the instant your own phone transcribes a real English word it lands on the TV in 90-point type with your name on it and a price only you can see.

ideas.title: Spectral Test
ideas.hook: Play a broken random number generator like an instrument — patch its output bits to oscillators and hear RANDU's lattice as a buzzing chord while you rotate the point cloud until its 15 hyperplanes snap into view.

ideas.title: Mute the Moon
ideas.hook: A mixing desk for the ocean: pull down the faders for the Moon and the Sun on a real tide-gauge record, and what's left twitching on the master bus is the hurricane.

ideas.title: Ratchet Clause
ideas.hook: Fifteen minutes last August quietly set the floor under every electric bill your shop has paid since — this finds that quarter-hour, names it, and prices exactly what it would have cost to shave it.

ideas.title: Slipstream
ideas.hook: Your phone buzzes points when a word fits your secret category — but one other player is secretly hunting you, waiting to slam right after you do and take it.

ideas.title: Off Axis
ideas.hook: Everyone rates the same eight objects on a secret scale — and the whole room shares that scale except one person, who doesn't know it's them.

ideas.title: Corpsing
ideas.hook: You watch a comedy clip together while secretly buying and selling shares in which of your friends will crack up first — and your own phone is the exchange's laugh sensor.

ideas.title: Second Source
ideas.hook: Every phone shows the same three gauges, but the machine is quietly lying to exactly one of you at a time — and nothing can be committed until two people say the same number out loud.

ideas.title: Sympathetic
ideas.hook: Your phone buzzes a secret rhythm down into the tabletop and listens with its accelerometer for someone else's — find your partner through the furniture, in total silence.

ideas.title: Jostle
ideas.hook: Everyone has to wave their phone around to complete a private motion — but yours takes a sharp quarter-second and theirs takes a slow two seconds, and any overlap jolts the table and breaks a glass, so 'okay, go' is nowhere near precise enough.

ideas.title: Wake the House
ideas.hook: Three siblings creep around a dark house on private errands; when two of you land in the same room the floor creaks — and only the sibling who wasn't there learns where it happened, which is exactly the lie they'll tell you next.

ideas.title: Deadband
ideas.hook: One needle on the TV, everyone's thumb pushing it at once, and each phone privately knows a different narrow window it needs the needle to sit in — so you have to negotiate a shared resting place using nothing but force.

ideas.title: Secret Admirer
ideas.hook: Everyone is secretly assigned one other player to imitate — and since nobody knows who is imitating them, the only way the room scores is if it accidentally collapses onto a single answer.

ideas.title: Point Mutation
ideas.hook: A daily puzzle where you turn one real sentence into another by swapping a single word at a time — and every intermediate has to survive as a sentence a human would actually say.

ideas.title: Orphaned
ideas.hook: A management sim where the map is the real Debian dependency graph, your customers are real popcon install counts, and every week you decide which piece of software the world is allowed to lose.

ideas.title: Meteoric Line
ideas.hook: Every glass of tap water is stamped with the latitude, altitude and storm history of the rain that made it — paint that isotopic fingerprint across a map and let people back-solve where a hair, a bottle, or a beer actually came from.

ideas.title: Swatch Book
ideas.hook: Each phone privately answers a different secret prompt with a photo from its own camera roll — but only five colors ever leave the device, so the group assembles a poster of its year out of images nobody will ever see.

ideas.title: Scrollback
ideas.hook: Four phones privately read the same group-chat thread for 75 seconds — except one phone gets an extra message that never existed, and that player will defend a memory nobody else has.

ideas.title: Runs Fast
ideas.hook: Four phones, one shared task, no clock on the TV — and one player's private countdown ticks at the wrong speed without ever telling them, so the tell isn't what they know, it's how fast they feel.

ideas.title: Below Speech
ideas.hook: Everyone scatters to different rooms of the house, and the only channel that passes through the walls is the sub-100Hz thump of a closing door — so four people must invent a transmission schedule using nothing but doors.

ideas.title: Too Fluent
ideas.hook: One four-word span of this novel excerpt was secretly written by someone in this room, and the only evidence is a surprisal trace that's been sliced four ways so nobody can read it alone — including the liar.

ideas.title: Exact Change
ideas.hook: Your room owes a bill denominated in bits of surprise — four people write simultaneously against one public gauge, clichés cost pennies, weird words cost a fortune, and the total has to land exactly.

ideas.title: Heavy Thumb
ideas.hook: One needle on the TV is the live weighted average of everyone's thumb — you each have a secret target band and a secret pull strength, so the whole round is arguing about where it should go while lying about how hard you're pushing.

ideas.title: Shoulder Surf
ideas.hook: Everyone types their one-word Chameleon clue at the same time — and the hidden Chameleon's phone watches you type it, keystroke by keystroke, exactly two seconds behind.

ideas.title: Talk Over
ideas.hook: Every phone holds loud spoken orders meant for someone else's console — and if two phones talk at once the audio turns to mush, so the humans' only real job is verbally scheduling when the machines get to speak.

ideas.title: Crossfade
ideas.hook: The room must produce 90 seconds of unbroken radio with no silence and no pileup — so you have to start talking while someone else is still talking, and only your phone knows the word that means it's your turn.

ideas.title: Washout
ideas.hook: An n-of-1 trial engine that designs a properly randomized, blinded, carryover-aware self-experiment, pulls the outcome straight off your watch so you can't fudge it, and refuses to show you results until the trial ends.

ideas.title: Never Read
ideas.hook: Wraps your process so every environment variable it actually reads gets logged, then prints a receipt showing that of the 47 secrets you inject, 12 are read, 32 have never been touched, and 3 are read while unset.

ideas.title: Nearest Even
ideas.hook: A browser puzzle game where you crush a real neural network into a shrinking memory budget by choosing each layer's bit width — and watch its actual accuracy, and eventually its actual sentences, fall apart in your hands.

ideas.title: Poison Pill
ideas.hook: You describe a secret word to the room while every listener sits on a different forbidden word they planted themselves — and the word they trapped is usually the one that would have helped them guess.

ideas.title: Table for Two
ideas.hook: Everyone answers the same silly prompt, but your phone secretly tells you how many people you have to match — exactly one, exactly two, exactly four — while a private live meter counts how many others are typing your answer right now.

ideas.title: Sight Read
ideas.hook: A rhythm game with no chart: you're playing the notes the person on your right is tapping out live, while writing the chart for the person on your left — and you can't see their screen.

ideas.title: Liar Ahead
ideas.hook: Everyone speed-runs the same 6-room dungeon at once, and the only way to warn — or sabotage — the players behind you is an anonymous Dark Souls message stuck to a door you've already survived.

ideas.title: Room Tone
ideas.hook: You may talk as much as you like — but only in the flat monotone your phone privately assigned you, while everyone secretly works to make you sound like a human being.

ideas.title: On the Hook
ideas.hook: Every word you say is silently charged to another player's account — you never learn whose, and the only way to find out who's draining you is to make them talk.

ideas.title: Round Up
ideas.hook: An explorable staircase of every lie your allocator tells you: hover any byte count and watch malloc(1025) quietly hand you 1280 bytes, across four allocators at once.

ideas.title: Q Factor
ideas.hook: Every breathing app tells you to breathe six times a minute; this one sweeps your own cardiorespiratory system like a Bode plot and finds the exact frequency where *your* heart rate swings hardest.

ideas.title: Growth Habit
ideas.hook: Every snowflake generator is decorative fiction — this one flies a seed crystal down through the *actual* atmospheric sounding over your house on a real snow day, so the shape it grows is the shape that really fell.

ideas.title: Same Frame
ideas.hook: Every phone becomes a live camera pointed anywhere in the room, and the TV shows the pixel-median of all of them — gray mush until you're all silently aiming at the same object, at which point it snaps into focus.

ideas.title: Letter Perfect
ideas.hook: Everyone types the same word at once and the TV shows only the letters all of you agree on so far — so the shared word grows one character at a time, stalls the instant someone diverges, and nobody may say a thing.

ideas.title: Claim Ticket
ideas.hook: You and everyone else are standing at the same baggage carousel with vague claim tickets, one grab each, and three seconds per bag — and two hands on the same suitcase bursts it open for both of you.

ideas.title: Call Your Shot
ideas.hook: You write one word and simultaneously bet on exactly how surprising it will be relative to everyone else's — and if two of you claim the same rank, you both get nothing.

ideas.title: Scion
ideas.hook: Four players each grow a private sentence they alone can read — until you graft yourself onto the leader's branch sight unseen and must keep writing a sentence you have never seen, steering only by what a tiny language model expects next.

ideas.title: Break Seal
ideas.hook: A $120k-a-gallon certified reference material sits in a lab fridge, its certificate lost in someone's inbox and its expiry two months past — Break Seal is the ampoule-level registry that turns every CRM into a control chart and builds the ISO 17025 audit binder by itself.

ideas.title: Hall Call
ideas.hook: Your CI queue is an elevator bank with a stupid dispatcher — replay 30 days of your real job log through express zones, destination dispatch, and cache-affinity routing, and watch p95 wait time collapse without buying a single runner.

ideas.title: Second Owner
ideas.hook: Package registries tell you who a maintainer *is*, never when the hands on the keyboard silently changed — so fingerprint the build environment baked into every tarball's gzip header, tar uname, and zip timezone offset, and watch a package quietly get a new owner.

ideas.title: In Season
ideas.hook: The model's next-token distribution is literally the deck — you hold six words nobody else can see, watch their probability bars ripen and rot as the room writes a sentence together, and try to cash each one at its peak.

ideas.title: Goes Without Saying
ideas.hook: You write a private clue for your secret word, but before the TV shows it, a tiny language model silently overwrites every word it could have predicted with its own second-favorite word — so only what surprised the machine survives intact.

ideas.title: Circuit Breaker
ideas.hook: A 24/7 bird-feeder cam on the TV is the market, and the only way to trade is to spend a token that pauses the stream for everyone — so buying is a public act of stopping the show.

ideas.title: Still Watching
ideas.hook: The twenty minutes your group wastes scrolling the streaming home screen becomes a hidden-shares market — everyone argues in bad faith, and one player is secretly paid if you never agree.

ideas.title: Slip of the Tongue
ideas.hook: The room drives one robot arm by voice, but certain words come out wrong from certain mouths — and only that mouth knows which, so every command is a two-second casting decision shouted across the couch.

ideas.title: Belay My Last
ideas.hook: You shout an order across the room, then your phone secretly tells you to cancel it — and your only tool is out-talking your teammate's thumb.

ideas.title: Left Up
ideas.hook: A wallpaper that breeds: it never asks whether you like it, it only counts how many hours you tolerated it before hitting the kill switch — and after a year it shows you the phylogeny of your own taste.

ideas.title: Lapse Rate
ideas.hook: A fatigue dispatcher for your own brain: an alertness forecast built from real two-process sleep math, where you drag espressos and naps onto tomorrow's timeline and watch the curve bend.

ideas.title: Trap Table
ideas.hook: An explorable map of every Linux syscall number ever assigned — 30 years, 20 architectures — where the holes, the renumberings, and the `_time64` twins are the story.

ideas.title: Too Many Cooks
ideas.hook: Twelve tiles, four silent cooks, one survivor — but any tile two of you try to cut at the same instant refuses to die and keeps the scar forever.

ideas.title: Late Money
ideas.hook: Four people watch the same 90-second clip paused one beat before the payoff — but each phone was slipped a different true fragment of the ending, and the live odds board quietly tells you which of them the others believe.

ideas.title: Upsell
ideas.hook: Everyone at the table gets the same public threshold for tonight's bill and a secret instruction to push it over or under — and your only lever is the food you actually have to eat.

ideas.title: As Is
ideas.hook: You're auctioning a mystery lot you alone can see, your phone forces you to reveal exactly two of its five true attributes, and the three you hide say more about it than the two you show.

ideas.title: Moving Knife
ideas.hook: A knife sweeps slowly across a shared pile of loot on the TV, and each phone secretly knows what that loot is worth to *you* — tap CLAIM and the piece is yours, but you never learn why anyone else was greedy.

ideas.title: Late Fee
ideas.hook: Turns your bottomless media library back into a 1998 video store: six titles faced out on a shelf, two checkouts at a time, everything else literally invisible until you return them.

ideas.title: Cast Iron
ideas.hook: A deep-zoomable map of all four billion float32 bit patterns, colored by what `(int)f` *actually* does on real hardware — with the compiler and the CPU disagreeing in plain sight.

ideas.title: First Boot
ideas.hook: A Raspberry Pi wiretaps a brand-new gadget's first ten minutes of life — before you tap a single button — and issues it a signed birth certificate you can look up before you buy.

ideas.title: Third Wheel
ideas.hook: Your phone privately tells you who your partner is, and for one player that card is a lie — so they spend the whole game loyally chasing someone who is busy being loyal to someone else.

ideas.title: Wrong Aisle
ideas.hook: Everyone's phone deals five items from the same mystery place — except one phone, which is quietly drawing from the store next door, and its owner has no idea their evidence is wrong.

ideas.title: Sore Subject
ideas.hook: The room must talk to survive, but every word is taxed and each phone privately holds one topic that quietly bleeds its owner dry whenever the conversation drifts near it.

ideas.title: Hands Full
ideas.hook: Your phone's mic is wired to your own buttons — the moment you open your mouth, your controls die, so talking literally costs you your hands.

ideas.title: Rebus
ideas.hook: Two silent builders assemble one pictogram sentence on the TV out of two private icon trays that share nothing, so you're always missing the exact symbol you need and have to imply it instead.

ideas.title: Sigma Weather
ideas.hook: A menubar barometer for scientific disagreement: at a glance, how many sigma apart the world's two best measurements of the neutron lifetime, the Hubble constant, or the muon's magnetic moment are *today*.

ideas.title: Pity Timer
ideas.hook: A drum machine with no step sequencer: you don't place notes, you sculpt the *statistics* — clumpiness, refractory periods, guaranteed-hit pity counters, and cross-voice correlations — and the groove falls out of the randomness.

ideas.title: The New Zero
ideas.hook: The United States is rewriting the definition of "sea level," and your house's official elevation moves by up to a meter overnight — this map shows who silently gains, and who loses, a flood zone.

ideas.title: Free Busy
ideas.hook: Everyone's calendar is public but blurred and six seconds stale, so you politely book a meeting into a gap that closed while you were looking at it — and then all three of you flee into the same new gap.

ideas.title: Whip Pan
ideas.hook: One camera, one scene, three people who each secretly need it pointed somewhere else — and two grabs at the lens at once smears the shot for everybody.

ideas.title: Trace Amounts
ideas.hook: Every phone in the room is quietly screaming a different inaudible tone, and yours is measuring the dose you are getting from exactly one of them — so the party becomes people trying to peel each other off one at a time to find out who they are allergic to.

ideas.title: Relative North
ideas.hook: One player becomes a human protractor, slowly sweeping the room and calling out compass numbers only they can see, while everyone else silently listens for the one private number that tells them where to go stand.

ideas.title: Call Waiting
ideas.hook: Every player is a switchboard with two lines and one mouth — you can shout a secret at someone all you like, but if they're on the other line, your phone is playing them hold music and nothing you said ever happened.

ideas.title: Safe Yield
ideas.hook: A groundwater tycoon sim where the storage meter always reads out of 100% — because the denominator is secretly shrinking every time you overpump, and you can never get it back.

ideas.title: Keep Full
ideas.hook: The propane dealer's paper K-factor card, turned into a change-point detector that quietly catches leaks, theft, and new tenants before it schedules tomorrow's truck.

ideas.title: Short Memory
ideas.hook: The room votes on the next word of a shared sentence, but each phone's private surprisal meter is computed under a different amount of context — so everyone is honestly reading a different, partial truth off the same model.

ideas.title: Soft Spot
ideas.hook: Everyone writes one sentence, then everyone is secretly handed one ugly word to jam into someone else's — and a tiny in-browser LLM scores, in bits, exactly how much damage a single wedge did.

ideas.title: No Card
ideas.hook: You make a small emblem for one secret person out of the same kit everyone else has — it has to be unmistakable to them and untraceable to you.

ideas.title: Long Exposure
ideas.hook: Turn off the lights: the laptop's webcam holds one long exposure while every phone screen becomes a colored brush painting a picture nobody gets to see until the shutter closes.

ideas.title: Group Delay
ideas.hook: A symbol wheel spins on every phone at once and you all have to stop it on the same symbol — except each phone is secretly running a few hundred milliseconds behind, and nobody told you which one is you.

ideas.title: One Too Many
ideas.hook: Everyone's phone shows the same nine answers — except one of your nine is a plant only you can see, it's the best answer on the board, and you have to figure out that you're the one being seduced.

ideas.title: Pure Tin
ideas.hook: Lay out a pretend circuit board, pick your finish, and watch twenty years of spontaneous tin whisker growth in thirty seconds — then read the cause-of-death report.

ideas.title: Burn Hours
ideas.hook: A softsynth whose every voice is a simulated tungsten filament — you hear the light, not the current — and the filaments evaporate, drift, and permanently burn out as you play.

ideas.title: One Pot
ideas.hook: A roguelike deckbuilder where the run *is* a synthesis route — your cards are named reactions, RDKit enforces the rules, and your HP is cumulative yield.

ideas.title: Word of Mouth
ideas.hook: The one person who can read the magic word is the one person whose phone won't let them say it — so you have four minutes to grow that word in somebody else's mouth while they're busy growing one in yours.

ideas.title: Chorus Line
ideas.hook: Every call needs exactly three voices at once — so the hardest part isn't recruiting the third mouth, it's shouting the fourth one away before it ruins your chant.

ideas.title: Minimum Necessary
ideas.hook: You have one sentence you must say out loud, and how loud you're allowed to be is a slider in everybody else's hands, drawn from a shared pot of air that pays out whatever's left.

ideas.title: Retention Policy
ideas.hook: Your phone is a wiretap pointed only at you, and at the end of the round the TV plays your single most damning three seconds with no context whatsoever.

ideas.title: Beam Width
ideas.hook: The model writes the whole story and you are never allowed to type a word — your only power is secretly striking one of its four proposed continuations, while your phone privately whispers which one sounds most like the voice you're hiding.

ideas.title: Two Words Back
ideas.hook: A hidden paragraph advances one word at a time and the room must guess what comes next — but each phone secretly sees a different amount of the past, and nobody is told how blind they are.

ideas.title: Title Search
ideas.hook: Before you drop $4,000 on that perfect expiring domain, get the rap sheet — every blocklist it ever sat on, every phishing kit it ever hosted, and crucially whether all of it belongs to the previous owner.

ideas.title: Romberg Quotient
ideas.hook: Ninety seconds a day of standing still with your phone at your waistband, and a year later you know which of your three balance senses is quietly carrying you — and which one is failing.

ideas.title: Blue Wool
ideas.hook: Your wallpaper photo-fades like a poster in a sunny window — except the sun is your empty desktop and your app windows are the mask, so after a year the bleached ghost of your own workflow is printed into it.

ideas.title: Error Bars
ideas.hook: Wavelength where the hidden target band is split across two phones — one player sees only its left edge, one sees only its right — so how badly their two clue words disagree is the only way the room can tell how wide the target is.

ideas.title: Character Limit
ideas.hook: It's The Chameleon, except your clue is capped at a secret number of letters nobody else knows — so the terse, shifty-looking clue might be an innocent who only had three characters to work with.

ideas.title: Shim Stock
ideas.hook: Every phone privately holds a resting-pose spec — a tilt band, a stillness ceiling — and you must hunt the real room for a surface that satisfies it, set the phone down, and let go of the only thing that was telling you what you needed.

ideas.title: Sheeting Grade
ideas.hook: A phone on your dashboard, a calibration patch taped to the hood, and one night drive turns a $12,000 retroreflectometer into a county-wide traffic sign compliance survey.

ideas.title: Terminal Digit
ideas.hook: Audits your own health-tracking history for rounding lies — finds the real step size of every metric, tests your last digits for human fudging, and redraws your charts with an honest noise band that erases most of your "streaks".

ideas.title: Recommended Value
ideas.hook: Paste any physical constant from an old paper and this thing carbon-dates it — telling you which CODATA vintage the author used, and how many sigmas that number is from today's truth.

ideas.title: Worse Half
ideas.hook: Wavelength with a two-headed psychic: two clue-givers each secretly hold a different target on the same spectrum, must build one clue phrase word by word without talking, and are scored on whichever target the guessers stranded.

ideas.title: Take the Watch
ideas.hook: Exactly one phone in the room shows the live board — and whoever holds it can't move, so the map is a hot potato and everyone else is navigating from a snapshot that's quietly fogging over.

ideas.title: Same Hat
ideas.hook: One phone holds the whole map — but every player's token on it is an identical dot, so the Cartographer can watch you move and still have no idea you're you.

ideas.title: Held Breath
ideas.hook: The room shares one lungful of air: only one person may be making sound at a time, and your phone never tells you whether the slot is free.

ideas.title: Loud Neighbor
ideas.hook: Your phone's mic doesn't police you — it polices the person sitting next to you, and only you can hear the alarm.

ideas.title: Anneal
ideas.hook: A profiler that tells you the smallest set of Python functions you could freeze into static, compilable code — ranked by CPU time, proven monomorphic by watching your program actually run, and handed back as a patch of type annotations.

ideas.title: Probate
ideas.hook: When an employee leaves, their Zapiers, Apps Scripts and Retool apps keep running with prod write access forever — Probate is the estate lawyer that finds every orphaned automation, ranks it by blast radius, and gets it buried or adopted.

ideas.title: Let It Cook
ideas.hook: Your clue only develops while your phone lies face-down and untouched — so reading it stops it, walking blanks it, and the whole room can watch your patience run out.

ideas.title: Double Claim
ideas.hook: Everyone drafts from the same pool at the same instant, and when two of you grab the same card the room stops dead for a five-second sealed bidding war that only the two of you can participate in.

ideas.title: Change Hands
ideas.hook: Twelve numbered bidding chips are dealt in secret and never leave the room — every time you win a lot, your winning chip is silently handed to whoever bid lowest, so the room's power quietly redistributes and nobody but you knows what's in your fist.

ideas.title: Write Only
ideas.hook: Your Mac's own metadata already knows which of the 1,400 things you made last year nobody — including you — has ever opened again.

ideas.title: Kiln Chime
ideas.hook: Fire a virtual tin-glazed tile, then watch and *hear* the glaze craze — every crack propagating under real thin-film fracture physics, each one pinging like cooling pottery.

ideas.title: Backpressure
ideas.hook: A Wavelength riff where three phones drag the same needle at the same time and the TV shows only the resultant — so when your phone secretly turns red because the needle drifted into the one zone you know is wrong, your only voice is how hard you pull.

ideas.title: Dead Level
ideas.hook: Every phone gets a secret slope — like "1.6° downhill, facing roughly north" — and the only way to win is to find the one real sagging surface in the actual house that matches it, then keep everyone's footsteps from ruining your reading.

ideas.title: Open Book
ideas.hook: Your secret only unlocks while your phone lies flat and screaming a tone only other phones can hear — so reading it tells the whole room exactly where you're hiding.

ideas.title: Cosigner
ideas.hook: Every word you say aloud is billed to one specific other player whose name only you know — and if you bankrupt them before they've spoken their word, the whole room loses.

ideas.title: Baud Rate
ideas.hook: Your phones talk to each other in a 14 kHz band you can barely hear — and a whisper is the loudest, most destructive thing in that band, so the room's only working protocol is total silence and pointing.

ideas.title: Shelf Life
ideas.hook: Stolen straight from Project Zomboid: reading a book grants you zero skill points, only an expiring multiplier — so your unpracticed courses rot on the shelf and the tracker won't let you buy another one.

ideas.title: Freeze Line
