ideas.hook: Every Postgres row secretly carries the transaction that wrote it, so your tables already contain a full undocumented audit log — this digs it out and dates it, even for tables with no timestamp column.

ideas.title: Give or Take
ideas.hook: Every ETA your computer shows you is a confident lie; this menubar widget replaces them all with honest, self-calibrating intervals that publicly track their own coverage.

ideas.title: Had to Be There
ideas.hook: Finish the sentence so your friends can guess it word-for-word and a language model never could — clichés score zero because the machine saw them coming.

ideas.title: Cut In
ideas.hook: You bid a secret, unequal purse for a place in line — then the game tells you only who stands directly in front of you and directly behind you, and you have to talk your way into guessing whether that means you're second or last.

ideas.title: Second Lap
ideas.hook: Four card packs circle the room on a 20-second beat, everyone drafting at once — and before you pass, you secretly bet that the card you're leaving behind will still be there when the pack comes back around.

ideas.title: Barge In
ideas.hook: One player is reading aloud, and the only way the round advances is for someone to cut them off at exactly the right word — a word only that listener can see.

ideas.title: Whole Degree
ideas.hook: Kalshi's daily-high-temperature contracts don't resolve on the weather, they resolve on one thermometer's rounded integer — so model the thermometer's personal bias, and trade the buckets whose edges the market prices as if the sensor were unbiased.

ideas.title: Bathtub Mode
ideas.hook: Lake Erie is a 240-mile bathtub that rings like a struck bell for two days after a windstorm — this watches seven NOAA gauges, decomposes the sloshing into its standing modes, and pitches the 14-hour fundamental up into something you can actually hear.

ideas.title: Cube Out
ideas.hook: Point your phone at a pallet and it fits a box to the real thing — overhang and all — then hands you a timestamped 3D scan that is the evidence you need when the carrier's reweigh crew invents 400 extra pounds of freight class.

ideas.title: Ahead of the Tape
ideas.hook: A 90-second clip becomes a three-window betting market — and exactly one person in the room has already seen it, so the real game is spotting whose bet sizes are too confident to be honest.

ideas.title: Wall Bounce
ideas.hook: The room builds one juggle combo on a shared dummy, damage scales down with every hit so everyone wants to go first — and only your phone knows whether your move can actually link right now.

ideas.title: Save Scum
ideas.hook: Every phone gets one silent save and one reload — and when someone rolls the whole room back forty seconds, only their loot comes back with them.

ideas.title: Push Window
ideas.hook: CI queues are quantized like Mario's frame rule, so this CLI learns your pipeline's hidden boundaries and tells you that pushing 90 seconds from now saves you nine minutes — then optionally holds the push until then.

ideas.title: Mother Tongue
ideas.hook: Every phone secretly holds a scrap of real text in a different register and quietly scores everyone's writing against it — you win by writing the line that only your private corpus finds boring.

ideas.title: Headroom
ideas.hook: The room writes one sentence out loud while each phone secretly watches how bored a tiny language model would be by your one smuggled word — and only the blandest submission each turn survives.

ideas.title: Least Common
ideas.hook: Everyone's counter walks the same ring of sixty, but your stride length is a secret — and the TV shows the three positions sorted, so you can see the numbers without knowing whose they are.

ideas.title: Take a Penny
ideas.hook: Three secret hands of tokens must become identical — and the only way to say anything is what you leave in the communal tray.

ideas.title: Never Lift
ideas.hook: One pen, ninety seconds, and it never leaves the paper — the server hands control between phones on a hidden schedule with a crossfade, so the finished line drawing has no seams and no author.

ideas.title: Nem Con
ideas.hook: Four people write a communal poster together, but any line can be silently blocked by anyone — the TV shows only how many hands are up, never whose, so the room must argue itself into something nobody objects to.

ideas.title: Steady Rest
ideas.hook: Your mouse is already a sub-millimeter motion sensor sampling your hand a thousand times a second — this reads the tremor and overshoot hiding in your ordinary cursor movements and shows you, without a wearable, the hour your hands stopped being steady.

ideas.title: Full Charge
ideas.hook: Every time an HVAC tech tops off a leaking system, this quietly computes the EPA-mandated annualized leak rate, starts the 30-day repair clock, and prints the dollar value of the refrigerant that will hiss out of that unit next year — turning a compliance chore into the contractor's best closing argument.

ideas.title: Droop
ideas.hook: A live wallpaper painted by the actual electrical grid your laptop is plugged into — the mains hum sags a few millihertz when the whole city turns on its air conditioning, and your screen sags with it.

ideas.title: Dry Fit
ideas.hook: Everyone rearranges the same tile board at the same time on their own phone — and your beautiful three-tile play is checked last, against a board the cautious players already pulled apart underneath you.

ideas.title: Assemblage
ideas.hook: Five land parcels go up for auction all at once, and the blueprint on your phone only pays if you win two that touch — so every raise is a confession about which corner of the map you actually need.

ideas.title: Clear to Send
ideas.hook: You are a human network buffer holding exactly one packet, you can't see whether the person downstream is full, and the only flow control is your own voice.

ideas.title: Hot Desk
ideas.hook: Spaceteam, except the server keeps silently reassigning your controls to other people's phones and never tells anyone who got what.

ideas.title: Trickle Charge
ideas.hook: A shared battery fills only while the room is silent, everyone's phone privately forbids them to cash out below a different secret level, and the only way to stop the greedy player is to make a noise your own phone will snitch about.

ideas.title: Safelight
ideas.hook: Your private briefing is photographic paper that only develops in silence — every word you say fogs your page and every page within earshot, permanently.

ideas.title: Bait Bucket
ideas.hook: A fish can only reach a lake by swimming there — so every occurrence record in a hydrologically disconnected basin is a signed confession that somebody carried it.

ideas.title: Shovel Ready
ideas.hook: Backup-generator air permits are filed a year before anyone announces a data center — so you can tell a county's electricians they're about to get poached before their boss knows.

ideas.title: Wrong Fount
ideas.hook: Your great-grandfather is in 20 million newspaper pages, but the scanner spelled him "Ohas. Muclieil" — so search for the typo instead of the name.

ideas.title: Wrong Number
ideas.hook: Every phone privately holds a different scrambled keypad, and the room must silently converge on dialing the same seven digits when nobody can see anybody's screen and no two thumbs travel the same path.

ideas.title: Strange Track
ideas.hook: A bubble chamber simulator where the game never tells you what particle you saw — you measure the curvature yourself, do the kinematics, and defend your identification.

ideas.title: Dirty Set
ideas.hook: Treat your portfolio like an incremental compiler: write each position's thesis as a graph of premises, and when a premise is falsified by real data the tool marks every dependent holding STALE and hands you a rebuild queue.

ideas.title: Felt Report
ideas.hook: Your keyboard and mouse are ground motion: a drum-paper wallpaper that runs a real seismic trigger algorithm over your input stream and publishes a nightly earthquake catalog of your own working day.

ideas.title: Market Price
ideas.hook: Everyone at the table is secretly betting over/under on tonight's bill — but each phone was handed a *different* line, orders lock in simultaneously and blind, and whatever you bet, you have to eat it.

ideas.title: Tipped Off
ideas.hook: Everyone watches the same four-minute clip, but each phone holds a different piece of inside information about it — and the only way to cash in is to trade, which prints your secret onto the public tape.

ideas.title: One Size
ideas.hook: Everyone writes one sentence at the same time, but each phone is secretly running the same model against a different hidden voice — and the sentence that wins is the one whose *worst* secret fit is best.

ideas.title: Surge Pricing
ideas.hook: A shared sentence grows word by word while a tiny language model quotes every player a different, constantly-moving price for the one secret word they're stuck holding — and the room's bit budget is draining.

ideas.title: Tracking
ideas.hook: Fingerprint every copy of a document in the microscopic gaps between its words, so a leaked page photographed on someone's phone still names the recipient it came from — and a reverse mode that tells you whether the PDF *you* just received is marked.

ideas.title: Torn Write
ideas.hook: A drop-in SQLite VFS that lies to your app the way a real disk does — torn sectors, fsync that didn't, power loss mid-checkpoint — then shrinks the exact fault schedule that corrupted you down to a three-line repro.

ideas.title: Named Peril
ideas.hook: Stop scoring your dependency risk out of 10 and start quoting it in dollars — an underwriting engine that turns your lockfile into an actual insurance premium, because a number you'd have to pay out on is a number you can't fudge.

ideas.title: First Refusal
ideas.hook: A Dutch auction where every bidder gets their own secret clock — the price falls from 12 to 1, but your four-second window might only ever offer you nine.

ideas.title: Meet Order
ideas.hook: Three dispatchers share one single-track railroad, and every phone's clock is secretly running on a different town's local time — so when you shout "I'm clear of Ferndale at 8:15," you are lying without knowing it.

ideas.title: Lazy S
ideas.hook: Three ranchers draw cattle brands on their phones at the same time, and the registry rejects any two brands that look alike when rotated or flipped — so you can see you're colliding, but never with whom.

ideas.title: Rated Load
ideas.hook: Upload your G-code and we'll tell you the exact force that snaps the part, which layer line it fails at, and how to rotate it on the plate to triple its strength.

ideas.title: As of Right
ideas.hook: Fly through the ghost city that zoning already permits — every unbuilt-but-legal floor in New York rendered as translucent volume hovering above the real buildings.

ideas.title: Off Nominal
ideas.hook: Your wallpaper is a year-long cardiogram of the continent's power grid, measured by your own machine — and it can timestamp any recording you drop on it.

ideas.title: Peremptory
ideas.hook: Nine jurors on the TV, each phone judging them through a different private lens, and every player must strike six — the room wins only if exactly one candidate survives all three secret strike lists.

ideas.title: Muster Point
ideas.hook: Three identical dots drift on the TV, one is secretly yours, your swipe direction is secretly rotated, and the room has ninety seconds to silently agree on a place to meet.

ideas.title: Someone Keep Talking
ideas.hook: Two valves are held open by the sound of a human voice, only the person not talking is allowed to touch anything, and the instructions get dealt exclusively to whoever can't stop mid-sentence to read them.

ideas.title: Dual Key
ideas.hook: Two people must shout the same secret phrase at the exact same instant — and if either one says it alone, even by accident, that order is dead forever.

ideas.title: Bad Merge
ideas.hook: The room has to sort itself by a real, embarrassing number using ten privately-dealt comparisons — one of which the server quietly reversed, and its holder knows they're poisoned but not where.

ideas.title: True Up
ideas.hook: Property-based testing pointed at your Stripe account: it replays every invoice against an independent model of proration and hands you a dollar-quantified list of the money your billing code quietly loses.

ideas.title: Tempco
ideas.hook: A browser toy where resistance fights temperature: build circuits out of real alloys and watch the coupled electro-thermal feedback loop settle, oscillate, or scream into runaway — sonified.

ideas.title: Crowd Cover
ideas.hook: Your phone will only submit your secret while at least one other body in the room is facing the same direction you are — so confessing means quietly convincing someone to turn and stand with you.

ideas.title: Valet Key
ideas.hook: You read your phone's secret objective, hand the phone to the player on your left, and now they hold the only feedback meter for a goal only you know — while three other pairs shout their own contradictory instructions across the same room.

ideas.title: Hold That Thought
ideas.hook: Every player must read a private list aloud without losing their place, while their phone secretly orders them to break into a specific teammate's sentence and drag a specific word out of them.

ideas.title: Wake Word
ideas.hook: Every phone in the room is a smart speaker with a private wake word and a private set of skills — and none of them will take orders from their own owner, so clearing the chore queue means four people shouting near-identical vegetable names at each other's hands.

ideas.title: Gang Run
ideas.hook: You're print shops ganged onto one shared press sheet, each dragging a job you can see and nobody else can — and if two jobs overlap by a single cell the press prints ink over ink and ruins them both.

ideas.title: Mutual Aid
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly pledges to have one other player's back — and any two people who pledge to each other both die on the spot, so the only deal that pays is a ring of three or more that has to be negotiated out loud without a single handshake.

ideas.title: Mean Time
ideas.hook: Scans your Grafana and Prometheus for statistical malpractice, then queries the real data to prove it — "your API latency panel shows 240ms, a value your system produces roughly never."

ideas.title: Cooling Off
ideas.hook: Replays your entire brokerage history with every single order delayed — one day, one week, one month — and draws the curve of how much richer you'd be if you'd just sat on your hands.

ideas.title: Paid As
ideas.hook: Stop phoning insurance companies for a benefits breakdown — reconstruct each payer's real behavior from the thousands of claims they've already adjudicated for you, and quote patients a range instead of a lie.

ideas.title: Nightingale Floor
ideas.hook: Everyone plants their phone somewhere in the room as a listening post, then has ninety seconds to run a private errand across that floor without any of the four microphones chirping — and a single spoken sentence costs five times a dropped spoon.

ideas.title: Splash Zone
ideas.hook: Every phone bills its owner for the decibels it hears, so your pocket taxes you for talking and taxes everyone who leans in to listen — and the only way to trade your secret is out loud.

ideas.title: Ring Test
ideas.hook: Knock on the furniture: each phone privately holds a different secret target timbre, and the room has to find the one real object in it that sounds right to everyone at once — without ever being able to say what "right" means.

ideas.title: Lubber Line
ideas.hook: Every phone secretly rotates the room's 360° answer wheel by a different amount — so you vote by physically turning your body, in full view of everyone, and the two players whose wheels match must find each other before the clock runs out.

ideas.title: Saw It Coming
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly needs to land their own word in one shared sentence, but any word you add that makes the model too confident about what comes next is rejected out loud — so the moment your intent becomes predictable, you're locked out.

ideas.title: Mixed Company
ideas.hook: Every phone secretly primes the same tiny language model with a different world, and you win by writing one sentence that reads as perfectly native to your model and completely alien to everyone else's.

ideas.title: Snowfall Line
ideas.hook: A scrubbable map of the elevation at which rain turned to snow, every hour, for the last forty years — so you can watch the freezing level migrate up your own mountain across your lifetime.

ideas.title: Sniff Test
ideas.hook: A local forensic scope that shows you what your phone is *actually* saying about you on your own wifi, ranked not by bytes but by how weird the traffic is compared to the same app on everyone else's network.

ideas.title: Bisect Cassette
ideas.hook: Every test run you do all day is silently recorded as a (commit, test, pass/fail) tape, so when a bug finally surfaces `git bisect` is already over before you type it.

ideas.title: Upstage
ideas.hook: Lights off, the TV is the only light in the room, and your phone's camera is quietly hunting for your secret color — while the person standing in front of you eclipses it.

ideas.title: Hammer Price
ideas.hook: A sealed-bid auction where your bid is a punch — everyone sees the size of your swing, only your phone knows how hard it actually landed.

ideas.title: Band Pass
ideas.hook: Talk normally for ninety seconds while your phone secretly measures how surprising you are in bits per word — and your secret quota is to be dull, or to be strange, and the person speaking before you controls how hard that is.

ideas.title: Room Temperature
ideas.hook: Every phone runs the same tiny language model fed a different secret paragraph, and the room must build one sentence that bores all of them at once.

ideas.title: Fill or Kill
ideas.hook: Trade with all three people at once, back every offer with the same cubes you only own once, and let the server publicly execute you for the promises you couldn't keep.

ideas.title: Last Thumb
ideas.hook: One mystery lot, four thumbs pressed to four screens, a price ladder climbing — and every finger that lifts tells you something about what you're bidding on.

ideas.title: Racemize
ideas.hook: A browser toy where you watch a flask of molecules spontaneously choose a handedness — the same symmetry break that decided every amino acid in your body is left-handed, and you can tilt the odds and lose.

ideas.title: Blame Blind
ideas.hook: A git subcommand that answers "who last touched this line" when the line has been reformatted, moved between files, and renamed twice — by tracking the AST node instead of the byte offset.

ideas.title: Bench Depth
ideas.hook: A menubar toy that turns your CPU's power-management telemetry into a live rowing crew — cores that boost hard, sag, and get benched, so you can see thermal throttling as a shell losing its stroke rate.

ideas.title: Clapper
ideas.hook: Three phones scrub through the same silent twelve-second clip — but one is mirrored, one is tinted, and each holds a different slice of the timeline — and you all have to park on the exact same instant with nothing to go on but which flicker you think the others found interesting.

ideas.title: Monitor Mix
ideas.hook: Three people must all talk nonstop at once to keep the show running — but no phone shows you your own levels, only your neighbor's, so the only way to hit your target is for someone to shout it at you while you're mid-sentence.

ideas.title: Tongue Tied
ideas.hook: One sentence scrolls on the TV and the room must read it aloud without a gap — except each player is secretly forbidden from voicing certain words, so the sentence has to be handed mouth-to-mouth mid-clause while everyone shouts logistics over each other.

ideas.title: Cheap Talk
ideas.hook: Every word you write costs bits of surprisal under a tiny LLM, deducted from a private wallet — so the only way to afford your secret word is to get other people to make it predictable first.

ideas.title: Tip of Tongue
ideas.hook: You write a hidden prompt; the only thing the room ever sees is the tiny LLM's top-5 next-word bar chart — and if your secret word shows up in it, you score zero.

ideas.title: Fair Weather
ideas.hook: A menubar barometer for your own dependency tree that reads the *maintenance weather* over each package — not vulnerabilities, but the slow atmospheric signs a maintainer is drifting away.

ideas.title: Enforcement Gap
ideas.hook: An explorable map of the internet's unlocked front doors — every domain's DMARC posture rendered as a city where buildings without door locks are the ones anyone can send mail as, and you can walk your own street.

ideas.title: Boiling Point
ideas.hook: A single-player extremophile roguelike where you don't shoot anything — you allocate a fixed protein budget across heat-shock chaperones, membrane lipid saturation, and DNA repair, then watch a real Arrhenius-curve hot spring cook your lineage over 200 generations.

ideas.title: In Stock
ideas.hook: Twelve items on the TV, but your phone's shelf is quietly missing three of them — and the only way to learn what everyone else can see is to fail together, out loud, on the big screen.

ideas.title: Circle of Confusion
ideas.hook: The TV shows one badly blurred photo; every phone shows it a little sharper, and exactly one phone shows it sharper still — so the person who can actually see it has to learn to sound as lost as everyone else.

ideas.title: Remit To
ideas.hook: Your DMARC protects your outbound mail; nobody checks whether the 300 *suppliers* who email you invoices are trivially spoofable — this watches their DNS every night and pings your AP team when a vendor becomes impersonable the week their payment is due.

ideas.title: Catchment
ideas.hook: Every transit isochrone map draws one crisp 30-minute blob and lies to you; this one runs the trip from every departure minute of the morning and shows nested probability bands — where you can *reliably* get, versus where you get only if you're lucky.

ideas.title: Secondhand
ideas.hook: A writing tool that shades every phrase in your draft by how many other people already wrote it — your prose comes back looking like a worn leather chair, and it tells you which sentence peaked in 1987.

ideas.title: Stack Marker
ideas.hook: An MMO raid boss with no MMO: the TV shows everyone's position publicly while your phone privately tells you that you're the bomb, or the chain, or that your legend for reading the boss's telegraph went stale one cast ago — and the wipe replay reveals every hidden card so the room can find out exactly who killed it.

ideas.title: Try Jumping
ideas.hook: Everyone plays their own private text roguelike at the same time, and the only thing you can send each other is a Dark Souls message assembled from eighteen canned words — except the dungeon quietly reseeds itself per player, so the most honest advice in the room is also the most lethal.

ideas.title: Fair Coin
ideas.hook: Every phone privately flips a coin that decides whether you must answer honestly or answer whatever the coin says — so the room ends up with a true, printable map of who trusts whom that no one can ever be pinned to.

ideas.title: Hard Out
ideas.hook: Everyone listens to the same three-minute interview, but each phone is privately hunting a different moment, your stake bleeds away one point per second, and you have to bail before your moment fires.

ideas.title: Grantee
ideas.hook: Sells honest electronics importers the one thing they can't assemble themselves: a court-ready evidence packet showing the $19 competitor's FCC ID belongs to somebody else's product.

ideas.title: Dicing
ideas.hook: A WebGPU sandbox where you design the tempering profile of a sheet of safety glass, then smash it and see whether the fragments actually pass the EN 12150 dice-count test.

ideas.title: Crib Sheet
ideas.hook: A roguelike where the only thing that carries between runs is one 3×5 index card you write yourself — and the game literally refuses to show you any tooltip you didn't bother to record.

ideas.title: Cognate
ideas.hook: Nobody holds the same cards, so you can't play the same card — you have to play the same *idea*, and the idea is never named out loud or on screen.

ideas.title: Last Seen
ideas.hook: You can only see one neighbor, one tick late, in a closed ring — so if everyone copies what they saw, the room rotates forever and never agrees.

ideas.title: Clean Copy
ideas.hook: Everyone's phone holds the same nine evidence cards — except one player's copy is the uncorrupted original, so the only person in the room reading the truth is also the only person who sounds completely insane.

ideas.title: Street Name
ideas.hook: You're a search party splitting up a neighborhood by radio, except every phone shows the same map with completely different names for every corner — so the two of you who confidently agreed to cover different places are about to walk into each other.

ideas.title: Nobody Else
ideas.hook: Everyone gets the same private prompt and 60 seconds to point their camera at something in the room that satisfies it — and if two of you framed the same lamp, you both get nothing.

ideas.title: Known Issue
ideas.hook: Describe your car's weird noise in plain English and get back the exact failure cluster from two million public NHTSA complaints — plus the odometer reading where it usually breaks.

ideas.title: Trap Line
ideas.hook: You must say your word aloud to find who holds its other half — but any player can arm a silent 8-second snare that punishes the next voice in the room, at the cost of going blind and possibly trapping their own partner.

ideas.title: Reading Room
ideas.hook: Your private page only develops while the room is silent — and the first person to finish reading is suddenly free to talk, burning everyone else's text off the screen.

ideas.title: Getting Warm
ideas.hook: You describe a secret word out loud while two opponents have quietly buried semantic landmines around it — and you're the only person in the room who can feel the heat rising.

ideas.title: Sealed Until
ideas.hook: The room writes a time capsule of predictions about each other, and every line survives into the final artifact only if the group fails to guess who wrote it.

ideas.title: Squash Fold
ideas.hook: Six people fold one sheet of paper into an object none of them can see coming, because each phone holds exactly one secret step and nobody is told whose turn it is.

ideas.title: Yield to Scrap
ideas.hook: Prices used GPUs the way a bond desk would: rental income is the coupon, depreciation is the pull-to-par, and the result is an actual yield curve across silicon generations telling you which cards are trading rich.

ideas.title: Almost Every
ideas.hook: A zoomable microscope on the number line that shows you which points have names — zoom far enough and the screen goes empty, because you have finally arrived somewhere no expression can reach.

ideas.title: Third Row
ideas.hook: A route planner that optimizes for not throwing up: it scores every candidate route by frequency-weighted motion-sickness dose, so you can pick the boring highway over the pretty switchbacks before your kid decides for you.

ideas.title: Asked and Answered
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly writes one yes/no question about the hidden subject at the same time — and any two questions that mean the same thing are struck from the record unanswered, so the obvious question your private clue is screaming at you to ask is the one most likely to get you nothing.

ideas.title: Drumhead
ideas.hook: Every phone lies face-down on one hard table, buzzing private rhythms through the wood to claim slots — and while you're transmitting, your own accelerometer is deaf, so you never learn who else was buzzing at the same instant until the table has already swallowed both your claims.

ideas.title: Yardstick
ideas.hook: Everyone drafts from the same sixteen face-up cards, but each phone privately scores the whole table under a different secret rule — so your screen is a live leaderboard of a game nobody else is playing.

ideas.title: Standing Order
ideas.hook: Your hand isn't a hand, it's a line you can never reorder — and every card a rival gives you gets wedged in at a slot they choose, so your next play is always partly someone else's decision.

ideas.title: Cross-Date
ideas.hook: Photograph a stump in your backyard, trace one line from pith to bark, and get back the exact calendar year that tree was born — plus the droughts and fire scars written into its rings.

ideas.title: Hour Meter
ideas.hook: A $9 diagnostic that reads a used GPU's actual wear — memory retention errors, fan bearing coast-down time, thermal paste pump-out — and issues a signed condition report buyers can verify before they wire money.

ideas.title: Peel Ply
ideas.hook: Debug scaffolding that bonds hard to your working tree and never, ever commits — one command peels it off, another lays it back down after a rebase.

ideas.title: Under the Table
ideas.hook: Phones lie face-down on one wooden table thumping 55 Hz pulses through it, and you get exactly three pulses out — but if two of you fire in the same slot the table turns to mush and both messages die, so the whole game is felt in your fingertips.

ideas.title: Type Ahead
ideas.hook: Everyone types an answer at the same time, and the instant two of you are typing the same first three letters, that prefix burns for both of you — so you spend the round frantically swerving away from words you can't see anyone else writing.

ideas.title: On the Book
ideas.hook: Nobody bids live — everyone secretly writes a two-rule bidding bot, and then the whole room watches your bots bankrupt each other over a worthless lot.

ideas.title: Net Out
ideas.hook: Everyone posts secret barter rates, and the server finds the four-way trade ring nobody at the table could ever have negotiated out loud.

ideas.title: Column Inch
ideas.hook: A cheat sheet that shrinks 3% every week, forcing you to keep evicting facts — and anything you can still recall from memory after eviction stays gone forever, so the page physically contracts as you actually learn.

ideas.title: Native Speaker
ideas.hook: It quietly harvests the diff between what you dictated and what you finally typed, builds a phrasebook of your own two registers, and can then run the translation backwards — turning your stiff written prose back into the way you actually talk.

ideas.title: Fat Finger
ideas.hook: A linter for identifier schemes that shoves your whole ID corpus through the lossy channels real IDs actually travel — handwriting, dictation, OCR, autocorrect, Unicode normalization, case-insensitive collation — and hands you the exact pairs that are one plausible human error apart.

ideas.title: Backlog
ideas.hook: A booster draft where packs never wait for you — you can hoard as many open packs as you dare on your phone, but every held pack rots, and you choose which neighbor eats the mess.

ideas.title: Still Holding
ideas.hook: A silent all-pay auction bid with your thumb: hold the button as long as you dare, pay every second you held whether you win or lose, and watch the TV count fingers still down without ever telling you whose.

ideas.title: By Omission
ideas.hook: Everyone holds a secret hand of seven cards and must end up holding the same one as somebody else — and the only way to say anything is to visibly throw the wrong cards away.

ideas.title: Push Poll
ideas.hook: Everyone answers the same poll question — except each phone was privately handed a differently rigged version of it, and the round ends when the TV finally shows you what everyone else was actually asked.

ideas.title: Pinch Hit
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly writes one brutal category as a trap for somebody else — and when two symbols collide on the TV, your phone hands you the stranger's category and ten seconds to blurt.

ideas.title: Dutch Book
ideas.hook: A scanner that hunts for sets of prediction markets whose prices are mathematically incoherent — not identical markets on two venues, but markets that logically imply each other and don't know it.

ideas.title: Seek Time
ideas.hook: A menubar toy that re-sonifies your silent SSD as a 2003 desktop hard drive, deriving head-seek distance from the inode numbers of the files you actually touch.

ideas.title: Rolls Downhill
ideas.hook: Drop a virtual marble on any doorstep and watch which street corner in your city everything — rainwater, litter, runaway shopping carts — eventually ends up at.

ideas.title: Green Light
ideas.hook: The forty-minute argument about what to watch becomes a live anonymous price chart of the room's indecision — and every person shilling a title is secretly long on it.

ideas.title: Bump Steer
ideas.hook: You can see the whole yard but you have no hands; they have hands but can only shove each other, and nobody can move themselves an inch.

ideas.title: Quitclaim
ideas.hook: The one player who can see the map is forbidden to speak, and the only way they can tell you anything is by permanently cutting a tile out of their own screen and deeding it to yours.

ideas.title: Out of True
ideas.hook: Every phone becomes a spirit level, the party surveys the real slopes of your actual crooked apartment, and the whole thing detonates when two people unknowingly measured the same coffee table and got different answers.

ideas.title: Zero Beat
ideas.hook: The TV screams a 19kHz tone you can't hear, and every phone reads the Doppler shift of its own owner's body — so you can sprint sideways for free, but creeping one inch toward the screen charges a bust meter only you can see.

ideas.title: Skeleton Track
ideas.hook: A logging-railroad puzzle-tycoon where you never have enough rail, so the only way forward is to tear up the line behind you and lay it again — a little more worn each time.

ideas.title: High Water
ideas.hook: Plots your parser as a seismograph — input position against step count — so exponential backtracking shows up as a visible sawtooth cliff instead of a mystery hang.

ideas.title: Double Delta
ideas.hook: A rhythm machine descended from Colossus: nothing triggers on a note, everything triggers when two punched paper-tape loops statistically agree more than they should.

ideas.title: Estate Sale
ideas.hook: The house map lives on the Realtor's phone and updates as they walk; the buyers wander blind through rooms that only exist on someone else's screen, and the Realtor is quietly lying about at least one of them.

ideas.title: Cartographer's Hands
ideas.hook: One player's phone holds the only map of a dark maze, but they may never speak — they can only squeeze, tilt, and tap their phone to send haptic pulses that arrive on the walkers' phones as a private felt language nobody agreed on in advance.

ideas.title: Tween
ideas.hook: Four people simultaneously draw four frames of one looping animation, each phone showing a live ghost of the frame ahead of you being drawn *right now* — so you're all chasing each other around a ring that has to close.

ideas.title: Heads You Lie
ideas.hook: Every phone secretly flips a weighted coin that decides whether you must answer a personal question truthfully or lie on command — so the room ends the night holding an honest statistical census of itself that can never be pinned on anyone.

ideas.title: Live End
ideas.hook: Your phone chirps and listens to its own echo, and the private number on your screen sends you diving into the coat closet while someone else stands in the tile doorway — and if you both crowd the same hard corner, your bodies absorb each other's reading.

ideas.title: Still Life
ideas.hook: Four phones rest on four different surfaces in your living room — a palm, a couch arm, a hardwood floor — and one of you must whisper a three-beat code into the furniture without the room figuring out which twitching body owns which spiking line on the TV.

ideas.title: Fake Crawler
ideas.hook: An explorable map of everyone pretending to be Googlebot in your access logs — reverse-DNS every claimed crawler, plot the liars by ASN and hunting pattern, and watch which parts of your site the impostors care about that the real bots don't.

ideas.title: Panel Wash
ideas.hook: A dashboard that watches your rooftop solar quietly lose money to dust and tells you the one thing no monitoring app will: the exact dollar day on which washing the panels stops being a waste of a Saturday.

ideas.title: Shay Grade
ideas.hook: A single-player logging-railroad tycoon where you don't lay track on a map — you lay it on a real USGS elevation raster, and the geared Shay locomotive's brutal physics decides whether your greedy shortcut up the ridge is a route or a runaway.

ideas.title: Plane Table
ideas.hook: The Plotter's phone shows three live dots on a blank white sheet with no walls drawn; the three blind players drag on featureless black pads and feel the walls by flash and buzz — the actual map exists nowhere except in what the room shouts at each other.

ideas.title: Grid North
ideas.hook: One player's phone holds the maze and three anonymous dots; the other three hold D-pads whose "up" is secretly rotated, and nobody can win until the room jointly works out both who is which dot and which way each person's north actually points.

ideas.title: Dinner Theater
ideas.hook: Everyone reads the same restaurant menu, but each phone secretly holds a different diner's hidden appetite — you bet on what the table will actually order, and the winner is whoever read the room, not the menu.

ideas.title: Minor Edit
ideas.hook: One sentence sits on the TV and everyone edits it at the same time toward a different secret agenda — but two commits landing on the same word merge-conflict, revert, and weld that word shut permanently.

ideas.title: Typebar
ideas.hook: The host TV is one mechanical typewriter and every phone is a fistful of its typebars — the room must strike a word letter by letter, and any two bars that swing at the same instant lock together and kill that letter forever.

ideas.title: Locked Groove
ideas.hook: A year of your health data becomes a physically playable 3D-printed record — one revolution per day, eleven minutes of lo-fi drone — and the last day is cut as a locked groove so it repeats forever.

ideas.title: Index Case
ideas.hook: Stop asking which test is flaky and start running an outbreak investigation: pull odds ratios over runners, shards, and execution predecessors until your CI names the shared resource that's actually the pathogen.

ideas.title: Certificate Holder
ideas.hook: Compile the insurance exhibit buried in your subcontract into machine-checkable rules, then red-line every ACORD 25 a broker faxes you against it — so you find out a sub is uninsured before the crane falls, not after.

ideas.title: Sidetone
ideas.hook: Your own voice comes back into your earbud a half-second late so speaking makes you stutter like a broken record — and the delay is a weapon your silent rivals buy with the seconds they didn't spend talking.

ideas.title: Half Duplex
ideas.hook: The TV whispers a secret list exactly once, and your phone's live captions freeze dead the instant you make a sound — so every word you say is a hole punched in your own copy.

ideas.title: Two Piles
ideas.hook: Eight objects, two unlabeled piles, three phones — split them however you like, but the room only wins if all three splits are the same set, and nobody may say a word about why.

ideas.title: Blink Twice
ideas.hook: Three phones in a dark room tap out silent flashes, but each player can only see one other player's light — the room has to reach unison through a chain nobody can see the whole of.

ideas.title: Not It
ideas.hook: Eight jobs are melting down and only the phone holding a job knows how much it actually costs — so the entire game is four people yelling half-truths about their workload to shove the worst task onto somebody else.

ideas.title: Throw Your Voice
ideas.hook: Every phone is a mailbox and your voice is the parcel — you have to physically walk over and speak into the right person's handset, because the phones compare loudness to decide whose inbox your sentence actually landed in.

ideas.title: Pocket Knot
ideas.hook: Tumble a virtual cord in a virtual box and watch it tie itself, then have the app compute the Alexander polynomial and tell you it's a 5₁ — the earbud-tangle experiment, playable.

ideas.title: Natural Long
ideas.hook: Your bank statement is a leveraged commodities book you never opened — this tool prints your real position in gallons, therms, and euros, then quotes the smallest hedge that flattens it.

ideas.title: Below the Line
ideas.hook: The TV crawls a real end-credits roll while everyone secretly owns shares in things like "any line containing ASSISTANT" — dividends fire line by line, and the only public signal is an anonymous tape of who just panic-sold.

ideas.title: Maker's Mark
ideas.hook: You secretly craft a tiny charm for one person in the room out of materials you don't have — and asking for what you need is how you sign your work.

ideas.title: Return Address
ideas.hook: Your group writes one letter to itself a year out — and it only gets sent if none of you can tell who wrote which line.

ideas.title: Since Last Run
ideas.hook: A CLI wrapper that reruns your command and shows only what actually changed since the last time — after learning which tokens in your output are just timestamps, durations, and PIDs pretending to be news.

ideas.title: Cross Slope
ideas.hook: Cities are legally required to inventory every non-compliant sidewalk and currently do it by walking miles with a digital level — so measure it from public LiDAR instead and sell them the prioritized repair list.

ideas.title: Greedy Star
ideas.hook: A generative music instrument where the score is a regular expression and the performance is its catastrophic backtracking — forty bytes of pattern unfolding into a ninety-second self-similar piece.

ideas.title: Plus on Block
ideas.hook: Four phones each hold two moves' secret frame data, and the room has to yell startup and advantage numbers at each other fast enough to keep one shared combo alive as the hitstun bar drains.

ideas.title: Zip Tie
ideas.hook: Match someone else's answer and you don't lose points — you get cable-tied to them for the rest of the game, sharing one answer slot, one shrinking menu, and one split score, while the untied players watch you argue.

ideas.title: Overprint
ideas.hook: Four people draw at the same time on one shared canvas they can't see themselves in — every cell two brushes touch turns to permanent mud, and the TV renders all ink in identical flat black so you slowly lose track of which marks are yours.

ideas.title: Fine Motor
ideas.hook: A menubar app that never records what you type, only how — turning your keyboard into a passive neurological instrument that scores your motor steadiness every day for years.

ideas.title: Time Error
ideas.hook: A menubar clock that runs on grid time instead of atomic time, drifting seconds behind whenever a continent is short of power — and notching a mark when it hears a power plant fall over.

ideas.title: Underwater Fill
ideas.hook: A Wednesday-morning email that tells an independent pharmacist exactly which prescriptions will lose them money this week — and which A-rated equivalent NDC to stock instead.

ideas.title: Turnstile
ideas.hook: Five gates, one last train, and every phone holds a different sliver of who can go where — walk into a gate someone else picked and it jams welded-shut for the rest of the night.

ideas.title: Slapback
ideas.hook: The TV fires a chirp, every phone records how the room echoes back at it, and three seekers crawl under tables trying to find the one spot in the house that *sounds* like their secret target.

ideas.title: Speed Trap
ideas.hook: The TV screams an 18kHz tone, your phone reads the Doppler shift off your own walking, and everyone in the room is racing to the screen under a different secret speed limit.

ideas.title: Toss-Up
ideas.hook: Write a sentence fragment the model finds maximally undecided — then get punished for every pair of humans in the room who fill the blank with the same word.

ideas.title: Print Through
ideas.hook: A menubar cassette deck for your own music library where tapes physically wear out with every play, and taping over an old mixtape leaves the erased songs bleeding through as ghostly pre-echo.

ideas.title: Last Flight
ideas.hook: An API that scores the last thirty meters of a delivery address — stoop steps, walk-up floors, sidewalk grade, door width — so movers stop quoting curbside prices for fourth-floor walk-ups.

ideas.title: Hygral Fatigue
ideas.hook: A salon roguelike where the hair is an actual physics simulation — every wash irreversibly damages a hidden strand state you can only probe with a loupe and a stretch test.

ideas.title: Cut Through
ideas.hook: Three drivers silently plan the same route across one city map — except each phone secretly shows only YOUR tolls, and the delivery van stalls dead at the first junction where your routes disagree.

ideas.title: Namespace
ideas.hook: Everyone types a word for the same category at the same time, and the TV lights up the exact letter where two of you are about to collide — swerve now, or you both score nothing.

ideas.title: Party Favor
ideas.hook: Four cards circulate through four phones at once, each phone writing blind on someone else's card and never its own, so everybody goes home holding a small printed thing about them that nobody will ever admit to writing.

ideas.title: Wet Ink
ideas.hook: Four phones type into one paragraph on the TV at the same time, every keystroke surfaces after a random delay so no one can tell who wrote what, and the group leaves with a signed-by-nobody note they actually keep.

ideas.title: Negative Space
ideas.hook: The anti-recommender: it embeds everything you've read, finds the holes — regions dense in the world's corpus and empty in yours — and each morning hands you one thing from your largest adjacent blind spot.

ideas.title: Toile
ideas.hook: A single-player pattern-cutting puzzle: slash darts and seams into a 3D garment until its curvature can lie flat, then nest the pieces on a bolt of striped fabric where every stripe has to match across every seam.

ideas.title: Same Camera
ideas.hook: Drop in the photo you're about to post anonymously and it plays hostile analyst — proving your metadata scrub left the sensor's fingerprint, the camera's quantization signature, and the sun's angle intact.

ideas.title: Bloom
ideas.hook: In a dark living room, every phone is a signal lamp blinking a private codeword at the laptop's webcam — and when two of you flash in the same 700ms slot, the camera whites out and both messages die.

ideas.title: Tailwind
ideas.hook: Two strangers write about the same card in separate rooms, and the model measures how much each sentence made the other one cheaper to say — convergence you can't negotiate for.

ideas.title: Trade Dress
ideas.hook: You're secretly assigned a genre, and you win by writing one sentence that the little language model finds obvious in YOUR genre and baffling in everyone else's.

ideas.title: Iso Cam
ideas.hook: The TV plays the clip smeared into unreadable blocks while your phone alone holds a sharp keyhole onto one corner of the frame — bet parimutuel on what's about to happen, knowing your edge only pays if everyone else is blind to it.

ideas.title: Trade Deficit
ideas.hook: The mischievous opposite of a keep-in-touch app: it reads your message history, works out who actually breaks the silences, and hands you a ledger of the friendships you have been quietly subsidizing for years.

ideas.title: Stepped On
ideas.hook: A CLI that asks the uncomfortable question about that suspiciously cheap OpenAI-compatible endpoint you're routing through: is this actually the model you're paying for, or has it been cut with a 4-bit knockoff and a hidden system prompt?

ideas.title: Mark to Myth
ideas.hook: Mutual funds are legally required to publish their own private-market fair-value marks every quarter, so you can reconstruct a live, unofficial price chart for SpaceX or Stripe out of nothing but SEC filings — and watch Fidelity and T. Rowe disagree with each other by 40%.

ideas.title: Bogey
ideas.hook: Ground Control's phone is a radar scope showing three identical unlabeled blips, three blind pilots know who they are but not where, and one of them is flying for the other side.

ideas.title: Declination
ideas.hook: One player holds the only map — on their own phone — and must talk three blind teammates across a flooding grid whose d-pads are each secretly rotated by an unknown quarter-turn.

ideas.title: Steerage
ideas.hook: A story writes itself one token at a time on the TV, and you spend a private wallet of bits to shove it toward your secret word — but bending the model costs exactly what it costs, so the whole game is waiting until your word gets cheap.

ideas.title: Small Bills
ideas.hook: A sealed-bid auction paid in indivisible bills from a wallet only you can see — no change is given, so you lose not because you're poor but because you can't make 14 — and every bill the winner spends is dealt straight into a loser's pocket.

ideas.title: Dwell Time
ideas.hook: Twelve face-down lots on the TV: tap and hold to flip one privately on your phone — but the room sees exactly whose eyes are on which slot, and the card you stared at longest is the one you'll lose the tie for.

ideas.title: Retrace
ideas.hook: Every time you SSH in and poke at a broken box, your fingers write an acceptance test — this mines your shell history for the read-only commands you ran to confirm the fix, learns which parts of their output are stable, and compiles them into a real health-check suite.

ideas.title: In Scope
ideas.hook: Companies quietly add domains to their bug bounty scope before they announce owning them — this backtests eight years of hourly scope diffs against acquirers' stock returns to find out how often the security team leaks the deal.

ideas.title: Rule of Six
ideas.hook: A soap foam coarsens on your screen for eight minutes and plays itself: every bubble with fewer than six sides is doomed, and each death is a note in a piece that starts as a hiss of thousands and ends with three lonely low tones.

ideas.title: Common Hand
ideas.hook: Three phones hand-draw one shared alphabet, but you only ever glimpse a letter from one secret neighbor for four seconds — and never your own again — so a single coherent handwriting has to survive around a hidden ring.

ideas.title: Envy Free
ideas.hook: Three phones simultaneously paint claims onto one shared image, each guided by a private map of what it's secretly worth to them — and nobody takes a piece home unless the partition is envy-free.

ideas.title: Second Printing
ideas.hook: Everyone's phone greys out the illegal moves — but one player's rulebook has a single clause quietly misprinted, so they play honestly, look like a cheater, and become convinced everyone else is cheating.

ideas.title: Dowsing
ideas.hook: One player hides a virtual object by physically walking to a spot; everyone else's phone becomes a compass needle that lies — it points true only when you're facing the wrong way.

ideas.title: Plumb Line
ideas.hook: Every phone is a private spirit level for a different invisible plane, and the only way to find the room's true horizon is to tilt your body until four strangers' bubbles agree without anyone seeing anyone else's bubble.

ideas.title: Harmless Instrument
ideas.hook: A menubar widget that watches the weather balloons descending over your county and taps you on the shoulder only when one is about to land somewhere you could actually walk to and pick it up.

ideas.title: Why Stopped
ideas.hook: An obituary column for drugs: every terminated clinical trial in ClinicalTrials.gov, given a headstone, a cause of death, and a warning label for the next team about to try the same target.

ideas.title: Slow Mover
ideas.hook: A single-player air-defense duty shift where you never learn the truth in time: a slow, cold, non-squawking track is either a lost Cessna, a decoy, or a Geran, and your job is to hold a probability — not a trigger.

ideas.title: Rider
ideas.hook: Everyone answers the same three innocent categories on the TV — but each phone is secretly holding a different weird contract clause every one of your answers must obey, and the round is won by reading everyone else's.

ideas.title: Over the Shoulder
ideas.hook: Cooperative one-word clue-giving where your phone secretly live-mirrors one other player's half-typed clue — and someone you can't identify is watching yours the same way.

ideas.title: Light Lag
ideas.hook: The pilot's viewport — and the TV everyone is watching — runs four seconds behind reality, so the only live truth in the room lives on two other phones, and the pilot has to fly on voice alone while their own eyes lie to them.

ideas.title: All Hands
ideas.hook: Every job on this sinking ship needs an exact number of thumbs held down on different phones at the same instant — so the room spends sixty seconds screaming about who has the winch and how many hands are already on it.

ideas.title: Cargo Cult
ideas.hook: Mines your own shell history for the incantations you actually perform after a command fails, so the next time it fails it hands the fix straight back to you — deadpan about the fact that neither of you knows why it works.

ideas.title: Data Collapse
ideas.hook: A puzzle game where you are handed ten ugly scattered experimental curves and a deck of physical quantities, and you win by inventing the dimensionless group that snaps them all onto one master curve.

ideas.title: Magic Comma
ideas.hook: A covert channel hidden in the one formatting choice Black refuses to normalize — the magic trailing comma — so a project can stamp an invisible, reformat-proof watermark into Python source and later prove who (or what) wrote it.

ideas.title: Point Shave
ideas.hook: The room yells answers at a game-show clip like always — except each phone secretly holds an over/under on the room's own score, and somebody in here is being paid for you to fail.

ideas.title: Reaction Shot
ideas.hook: Everyone watches the same horror trailer, but the real market is on each other — your phone holds shares in your friends' gasps plus a secret directive about your own.

ideas.title: Carry-On Only
ideas.hook: Your sentence has to fit in 24 bits of luggage, and the price of every word is exactly how surprised a language model is to see it — so keeping "marzipan" costs more than keeping six whole clauses, and a stranger's phone has to unpack whatever survived.

ideas.title: Proximity Effect
ideas.hook: To be heard, the phone must be at your lips — which means you can't see the screen, so every word you bank is muttered blind from memory, and reading the screen loudly is rejected as a shout.

ideas.title: Noise Floor
ideas.hook: Your phone whispers one digit of the vault code at a volume only you can hear — and any cough, laugh or "sorry, what?" buries somebody's digit forever, which is exactly why one of you is secretly being paid to cough.

ideas.title: Marching Orders
ideas.hook: Your coding agent obeys thousands of words you never wrote and have never read — this reconstructs the full text of its instructions from every source, hashes it, and tells you exactly what changed since yesterday and who changed it.

ideas.title: Never Moved
ideas.hook: You've lived at the same address for thirty years and been redistricted eleven times — here's the scrolling timeline of every political boundary that has ever quietly closed around your kitchen table.

ideas.title: Minutes
ideas.hook: Everyone watched the same five people answer the same four questions — then one phone hands you the official minutes with two cells quietly flipped, and nobody, including you, knows whose copy is the doctored one.

ideas.title: Spell Out
ideas.hook: Every phone shows everyone's secret letter but your own, so the only way to learn what you are is to watch other people spell words around the hole where you're standing.

ideas.title: Composite Sketch
ideas.hook: Two witnesses privately hold two different suspects in the same 12-card police lineup, and every card one of them rules out might be the other's suspect walking free.

ideas.title: Clear Cut
ideas.hook: Sixty words stand on the TV like a forest, and every single word any phone hears you say is felled forever for everybody — so the whole room is racing to harvest a vocabulary they are simultaneously destroying.

ideas.title: Part 15
ideas.hook: A solo pirate-radio roguelike on a real elevation map: pick a rooftop, pick a frequency, and let terrain physics decide your audience while listener complaints — not scanners — slowly draw the FCC's direction-finding cone toward your transmitter.

ideas.title: Grandfathered
ideas.hook: You granted Screen Recording to an app in 2022; the app was sold, resigned by a new company, and still has it — this tool diffs the code-signing requirement stored in TCC.db against the binary sitting on disk today and shows you every grant that has quietly changed hands.

ideas.title: Elbows Out
ideas.hook: A real-time draft with no turns and no passing: claim a card by holding it for 2.5 seconds, during which your phone blacks out the entire rest of the board — commitment literally costs you your eyes.

ideas.title: Inch of Candle
ideas.hook: A 17th-century candle auction: hold your thumb down to push your bid up, and the flame dies at a moment only the server knows — though each phone was whispered one true, partial clue about when.

ideas.title: Ration Card
ideas.hook: Every word you're allowed to say is a coupon with a punch count, and the switch on your friend's panel stays dead until somebody spends the coupon for its name.

ideas.title: Do Not Combine
ideas.hook: A Spaceteam where the hard part isn't learning what your panel says — it's that the warning you shouted eight seconds ago silently expired and became a lie.

ideas.title: Blur Radius
ideas.hook: Everyone privately types one true, specific, mortifying thing — then blurs it, word by word, until it stops being about you and starts being about at least one other person in the room.

ideas.title: Leather Hard
ideas.hook: Three phones become three hands on one potter's wheel — one spins, one slides up the wall, one leans in — and the wobbling vase you somehow make together is the only thing you take home.

ideas.title: Free Lunch
ideas.hook: A scanner that treats those "free V2Ray servers, updated every 15 minutes" lists as what they probably are — and scores each node for TLS interception, DNS lying, and content injection before you route your life through a stranger's box.

ideas.title: Deferral
ideas.hook: A blood donor's private pharmacokinetic model of their own iron — because the 56-day rule was written for the blood supply, not for your marrow.

ideas.title: Firm Price
ideas.hook: A quoting sidecar for small system integrators that watches real distributor prices and tells you exactly how many days your quote can stay firm before the DRAM market eats your margin.

ideas.title: Beat the Bounds
ideas.hook: Three phones each drag one stake of a shared triangle across a neighborhood map, each obeying an ordinance only that phone can see, until all three lamps glow green — and the room walks away with a dated poster and a GPX of a route it just invented.

ideas.title: Wheel Bid
ideas.hook: A rotating draft where you never pick from a pack — you privately rank the whole pack once, and the server resolves everyone's rankings into simultaneous picks, so the wheel spins in a single second instead of ten minutes.

ideas.title: Sealed Nickel
ideas.hook: A blind auction where the only currency is the cards you already drafted — bid one of your own cards face-down, and the loser's bid is what the winner actually takes home.

ideas.title: Duty Cycle
ideas.hook: Small SaaS that reads a cold-storage warehouse's meter data and tells the owner exactly what their compressor's ability to pause is worth in dollars per year — then files the paperwork.

ideas.title: Bias Point
ideas.hook: A browser synthesizer with no oscillator module — you breadboard actual transistors, and if you bias one wrong it sounds wrong, for the real reason.

ideas.title: Unblockable
ideas.hook: Import a year of your own bank statement and fight it as a Sekiro boss, where every expense's telegraph length is derived from how predictable it actually was.

ideas.title: Tine
ideas.hook: Three phones each own five tines of a hand-crank music box and can only see their own five lanes, while the TV scrolls the strip past a playhead and forgets it — so the tune exists whole only in the room, until you all punch it and take the paper home.

ideas.title: Siphon
ideas.hook: Your score grows only while you're talking and drains only while your secret, unknown parasite is talking — so the only way to work out who's robbing you is to shut up and stop earning.

ideas.title: Near Field
ideas.hook: Four phones lie flat on the table as a listening array, and how loudly you speak decides who receives your message — a whisper delivers to exactly one device, a normal voice broadcasts to the whole room and everyone gets to steal it.

ideas.title: Under Oath
ideas.hook: A GPS stamp on a photo proves nothing, so this cross-examines your own field photo against the barometric pressure, the visible cell towers, and the direction of its own shadows before it lets you swear to it.

ideas.title: Whistle Print
ideas.hook: Whistle a photograph across the room: one laptop screeches it out as 30-line mechanical-television audio, another listens with its microphone, and the reverb, the fridge hum, and the two machines' disagreeing clocks become the print.

ideas.title: Right of Way
ideas.hook: A wildlife-crossing puzzle where placing one canopy bridge is literally a rank-one update to the landscape's Laplacian, so you watch gene flow re-light across a severed forest in real time.

ideas.title: Both Modified
ideas.hook: Everyone edits the same paragraph at once, blind — and any two edits that touch overlapping words annihilate each other and scar those words permanently unusable.

ideas.title: Cold Weld
ideas.hook: Every time two of you slam the same button at the same instant, your phones are permanently welded into a single pair of hands — and half of each panel disappears.

ideas.title: Slow Play
ideas.hook: Skull & Roses where your disc stays secret but your hesitation doesn't — the TV publishes exactly how long each player agonized before committing, so the only tell in the room is a truthful bar chart.

ideas.title: Structure Borne
ideas.hook: Phones go face-down on real furniture and knocking is the only network — find your secret partner by getting both your phones onto the same table, and make sure nobody else's phone is on it.

ideas.title: Hard Iron
ideas.hook: Hide-and-seek where the hidden thing isn't an object but a spot on your floor, and the only clue is how badly that spot bends a phone compass.

ideas.title: Tenured
ideas.hook: A desktop terrarium where every object your program allocates is a critter in a pond, the garbage collector is the tide that drowns most of them, and the survivors who reach tenure get engraved nameplates — which is to say, your memory leak becomes a visible aristocracy.

ideas.title: Stand Dev
ideas.hook: A wallpaper that develops one photograph a day in a physically simulated darkroom — and it only advances while you leave the computer alone, because every keystroke sloshes the tray and leaves surge marks in the print.

ideas.title: Prestige
ideas.hook: An idle-game economy for the whole room: the TV shows one shared bank exploding upward, every phone privately owns a generator and a shop, spending is anonymous, and the target is only reachable if somebody volunteers to hit the button that wipes everyone's progress.

ideas.title: Soak
ideas.hook: The TV is an MMO raid boss with an eight-second cast bar, the room's three corners are the arena, and each phone privately holds one debuff whose survival rule references debuffs it cannot see — so the only way to live is to start shouting raid callouts.

ideas.title: Pay Grade
ideas.hook: The machine only obeys an order given by someone who outranks you — and nobody in the room knows the whole org chart.

ideas.title: Pidgin
ideas.hook: Every phone's buttons are labeled in its own private industrial dialect, and the only glossary that can translate your words is sitting in someone else's pocket.

ideas.title: Misprint
ideas.hook: A cooperative tile-chain game where every phone quietly refuses to let you make an illegal move — except one player's rulebook has a single clause swapped, so they play flawlessly by rules nobody else has.

ideas.title: Adverse Possession
ideas.hook: A menubar keyboard map that shows which of your key combinations have been quietly squatted by background apps — you press ⌥Space, it lights up occupied, and names the tenant that took it without asking.

ideas.title: In District
ideas.hook: Small advocacy orgs upload their member list and get back the only thing a congressional staffer actually cares about — which districts they have real constituents in, ranked by whether that representative is pivotal on the bill they're fighting.

ideas.title: Trace Paper
ideas.hook: One town map, torn into three transparent layers — one per phone — and you all must drop a pin on the single landmark you believe everyone else can also see.

ideas.title: Odd Lot
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly carves the same six goods into three lots at once, the server enacts whichever division looks fairest by public weight, and then all phones blind-grab a lot — where any two hands reaching for the same pile leave both empty.

ideas.title: Step Response
ideas.hook: Your slow CI doesn't just slow the team down — it makes the team oscillate, and this fits a control-theory model to your GitHub history so you can report the damping ratio in the runner-budget meeting.

ideas.title: Legal Tender
ideas.hook: A menubar central bank that strikes one engraved banknote per day — guilloche spun from your hourly activity, an intaglio portrait in wavy-line halftone, microtext of the day's longest sentence — until a year of them tiles into an uncut printer's sheet you can hang.

ideas.title: Walk-In
ideas.hook: Recall notices arrive as press releases full of lot codes nobody reads — this quietly cross-matches every federal food recall against the invoices your distributor already emailed you and tells you exactly which case in your walk-in to pull.

ideas.title: Carrier Sense
ideas.hook: Eight icons on the TV, a secret list of ones you're forbidden to pick, and the only way to talk to the room is one shared lamp that lights the same way no matter who pressed — so you have to invent Morse code in ninety seconds.

ideas.title: Convoy
ideas.hook: Three phones, three cars in a hidden ring, and no speedometer anywhere — the only thing you can see is the gap to the car ahead, so the room has to silently agree on a cruising speed nobody can name.

ideas.title: Make a Market
ideas.hook: One player is secretly the bookmaker, privately pricing both sides of a prop about the show you're all watching — too greedy and nobody bets, too generous and the room eats their bank.

ideas.title: Wall Crossed
ideas.hook: Everyone bets private chips on what the clip will do next — but one of you was quietly handed a spoiler beforehand, and the only tell is the shape of the money.

ideas.title: Cursed Item
ideas.hook: A roguelike where the loot is real: every item you equip grants a power on the TV and a private curse that quietly corrupts what YOUR phone is allowed to show you — and the party has to finish the dungeon without ever seeing each other's screens.

ideas.title: Iron Manual
ideas.hook: A fighting-game boss telegraphs one attack per beat, but each phone privately holds only two of the six frame-data pages needed to know what actually punishes it — so the block call has to be shouted across the room before the startup frames run out.

ideas.title: Craze
ideas.hook: Type in a glaze recipe and watch the crackle network actually grow — thermal-expansion mismatch simulated crack by crack into a pattern no one has ever seen before.

ideas.title: Hold Tag
ideas.hook: Forwards your food distributor's invoice PDFs into a live FDA recall feed, tells you exactly which case on your shelf is poison, and chases the credit.

ideas.title: Gnomon
ideas.hook: Click one pole and its shadow in a photo, and the sun tells you whether the timestamp is lying.

ideas.title: Sharp Money
ideas.hook: The room bets on a 90-second clip while one player has already seen it — and the only way to catch the insider is to read the anonymous line movement they leave behind.

ideas.title: Prepaid Minutes
ideas.hook: Every phone has a private balance of talk-seconds that its own mic burns down, and the player who can see the problem was issued ten seconds while the players holding the tools were issued forty-five.

ideas.title: Split Band
ideas.hook: A spoken repair order is diced into 120ms slices and dealt across the room's phones, so the message only becomes intelligible in the air between them — and everybody hears a slightly different version.

ideas.title: Tectonic
ideas.hook: The Cartographer's phone is the only place the marble and its maze exist; the other players can't see any of it and each secretly owns exactly one way to rotate, mirror, or shove the entire world.

ideas.title: You Are Here
ideas.hook: One player's phone holds the whole maze — but the dots on it are anonymous, so the three blind pieces have to figure out which dot they are before they can follow a single instruction.

ideas.title: Trabecula
ideas.hook: Topology-optimize a bracket into a beautiful bone-like lattice, then watch the game load it from an angle you weren't told about and snap it — a puzzle game about overfitting to your load case.

ideas.title: River
ideas.hook: Every reviewer gets a visually identical PDF whose justified line breaks are secretly a different valid Knuth-Plass solution — so when a page photo leaks, the whitespace rivers name the leaker.

ideas.title: Nap
ideas.hook: Your phone's microphone is a texture reader: rub a finger on carpet, oak, or glass and it knows which — so the board is every surface in your apartment, and somewhere in the room another player is secretly hunting the exact same one.

ideas.title: Cold Shoulder
ideas.hook: The TV tells the whole room to point at the oldest thing in it — but your phone has secretly forbidden one 60° wedge of the room, so you must pick a worse answer and hope nobody notices which direction you keep avoiding.

ideas.title: Weak Link
ideas.hook: Five phones each secretly fill a different blank in one sentence, one of you was privately told to wreck it, and the only evidence is the model's per-player blame chart.

ideas.title: Dead End
ideas.hook: You privately write an innocent-looking half-sentence engineered to strand whoever inherits it — while simultaneously fighting your way out of the cul-de-sac someone else built for you.

ideas.title: Bycatch
ideas.hook: A menubar aquarium stocked with the Wi-Fi networks around you — each neighbor's SSID is a fish whose size is its signal and whose depth is its band, and after a week it can tell you which ones are residents and which are just passing through.

ideas.title: Test Card
ideas.hook: A screensaver that renders a live broadcast test card built entirely from the death rate of the world's free public IPTV streams — it never shows a single frame of video, only the decay.

ideas.title: Grainline
ideas.hook: A Zachtronics-style solo puzzle where you cut seams and place darts on a 3D form, then watch it flatten into sewing-pattern pieces — scored on how much you tortured the fabric and how much you wasted.

ideas.title: Stall
ideas.hook: A train only moves while the room is silent, and the only brake is your own voice — which stops it, taxes you, and tells everyone you were hoping to get off early.

ideas.title: Personal Space
ideas.hook: Every phone screams a private ultrasonic tone nobody can hear; you must drift close to your secret mark for five seconds without letting the stranger who's hunting you get equally close — and no one is allowed to say a word about it.

ideas.title: Joist
ideas.hook: Every phone lies flat on a different piece of furniture; you knock on wood and discover the room's hidden vibration network — which surfaces are secretly connected, and which of you are structurally alone.

ideas.title: Bump
ideas.hook: A roguelike run where the whole party shares one character, but each phone privately holds a different item that only reveals its true effect when someone else triggers it — so every choice is a bet on a stranger's inventory.

ideas.title: Iframe
ideas.hook: A fighting-game combo is split limb-by-limb across four phones — each player owns one body part of a single shared fighter, and the combo only lands if every limb's input arrives inside the same three-frame window.

ideas.title: Dead Time
ideas.hook: Control-theory lab for your own body: it measures how many days lie between pulling a lever and seeing the result, then tells you you're oscillating because you keep correcting daily on a four-day delay.

ideas.title: Stale Frame
ideas.hook: Your prod crash points at payments/charge.py:412 from a release three months old — Stale Frame walks that exact line forward through history and tells you where it lives now, and whether someone already fixed it.

ideas.title: Ragged Right
ideas.hook: Typeset your year of bills like a paragraph — Knuth-Plass line-breaking decides which bill goes in which paycheck, and an overdraft prints as an Overfull \hbox warning.

ideas.title: Finder's Fee
ideas.hook: The only map is on the Fixer's phone, the Fixer is on nobody's team, and every hint has a price the Fixer makes up on the spot.

ideas.title: Ground Truth
ideas.hook: Three blind scouts each have one useless sense; the fourth player holds the only map in the room, and it starts blank.

ideas.title: Drone
ideas.hook: Everyone types at once and the only rule is: never surprise the model — until the host privately shoves a rare word into your hands and gives you six words to make it feel obvious.

ideas.title: Elide
ideas.hook: Delete as many words as you dare from a shared sentence — you get paid in bits for every word a tiny language model can put back, and fined in bits for every one it guesses wrong.

ideas.title: Follow Suit
ideas.hook: A silent cooperative trick-taking hand where your goal card is secret even from your teammates, and the only thing you may ever say out loud is one true sentence about one card.

ideas.title: Freight Elevator
ideas.hook: A single-player tycoon where you run a commercial building's freight elevator as a scarce contested resource — every tenant move-in, caterer, and drywall delivery bids for a booking slot, and your whole business is the schedule.

ideas.title: Blast Freeze
ideas.hook: A CI-repo watchdog that treats your git history like a cold-chain: it flags the exact commit where a repository's clone weight crossed the line from "code" to "landfill" and prices the ongoing carrying cost in CI-minutes and bandwidth for every downstream consumer.

ideas.title: Coxswain
ideas.hook: The rowers face backward and can't see the river — each phone is one oar — while the single Cartographer up front holds the only chart of the rapids and can only steer them with their voice.

ideas.title: Shoal
ideas.hook: One player's phone is the only chart of a drowning tidal flat — everyone else is a blind fish they must herd onto shrinking high ground before the water swallows the last safe cell.

ideas.title: Nightcap
ideas.hook: Each phone is secretly handed one slot of a cocktail — base, sour, sweet, wildcard, garnish — and fills it blind, so the shaker reveal is a Frankenstein drink nobody saw coming, printed as a recipe card you now have to actually make.

ideas.title: Flourish
ideas.hook: Given one abstract prompt, everyone secretly draws a single freehand squiggle on their phone — and you win only if all three strokes turn out to be the same shape.

ideas.title: Ladder
ideas.hook: Everyone silently drags the same five cards into a ranked order and prays the whole room landed on the exact same list — with no way to see anyone else's hand.

ideas.title: Sandhi
ideas.hook: A daily wordgame about the seams between words — you're shown a target hidden word and must find a natural everyday phrase that secretly contains it across the spaces, like the 'nitrate' buried in 'the night rate.'

ideas.title: Beacon Frame
ideas.hook: A menubar generative-music toy that turns the invisible RF around you into an ever-shifting ambient soundscape — every nearby WiFi network becomes a voice, its signal strength the volume, so the room's radio weather composes a piece that's never the same twice.

ideas.title: Flam
ideas.hook: Everyone drums into the same 8-slot loop, but two hits on the same beat clash into an ugly flam — so the room must silently carve up the groove into non-overlapping pieces.

ideas.title: Swap Meet
ideas.hook: Everyone haggles at once in dead silence — your phone quietly floats secret 'I give X, I want Y' offers onto a trading floor and the server snaps compatible ones into instant, atomic trades before you complete your hidden recipe.

ideas.title: Float
ideas.hook: A silent heist where every quiet second banks loot for the crew — until the vault privately taps ONE of you to whisper a keycode, and everyone else must figure out, without speaking, that it isn't their turn.

ideas.title: Day Field
ideas.hook: Every morning your desktop wallpaper becomes an abstract Rothko-style color-field painting of the day ahead — dense and agitated where you're back-to-back, soft and open where you're free — art you can't quite read but can always feel.

ideas.title: Second Run
ideas.hook: Independent and repertory cinemas just lost the free box-office data they lived on — this gives them a booking brain that tells them which title to play next weekend and whether the terms will pencil out.

ideas.title: Register
ideas.hook: Write one sentence that reads as flawless nursery rhyme yet total gibberish when the model rereads it as a legal contract — the bigger the perplexity gap between the two hats, the better.

ideas.title: Forgery
ideas.hook: The room draws one secret object stroke-by-stroke onto the TV, but one player never learned the word — and every spectator privately logs live suspicion the instant each stroke lands, building a secret dossier instead of one end-vote.

ideas.title: Cutthroat
ideas.hook: A row of loot on the TV, everyone secretly grabs one at the exact same instant — and if two of you grab the same thing it shatters and nobody gets it.

ideas.title: Tilt
ideas.hook: Import your real brokerage trade history and it reconstructs your worst year as a boss-rush roguelike where each behavioral bias — holding losers, selling winners, revenge-sizing — is a monster you learn to beat.

ideas.title: Left Behind
