ideas.hook: A migration-completeness auditor that diffs your old git forge against the new one and proves — issue by issue, webhook by webhook — that nothing silently vanished in the move off GitHub.

ideas.title: Deadman
ideas.hook: A local egress proxy that fingerprints your coding agent's request loops and trips a circuit breaker the instant it starts accidentally DoSing an endpoint or torching your API budget.

ideas.title: Next Hop
ideas.hook: A message has to reach Priya, but nobody can see the whole map — you only know who YOU can reach, so the room becomes a shouting, self-organizing routing table racing the packet's dying timer.

ideas.title: Break Break
ideas.hook: Everyone jabbers routine radio chatter to keep the net alive — until your phone hands you an urgent message and you have to shout the room into silence to squeeze it through.

ideas.title: Fresco
ideas.hook: A group mural drawn one private brushstroke at a time — but one painter never learned the word, and their phone quietly fed them a plausible wrong one.

ideas.title: Unfold
ideas.hook: Type in the dimensions of a square-to-round HVAC duct transition and get back the triangulated flat sheet-metal pattern — fold lines, seam allowance, cut list, and a DXF ready for the plasma table.

ideas.title: Sand Song
ideas.hook: A playable Chladni plate where humming or plucking a note drives real standing waves and thousands of sand grains crawl into the exact nodal pattern — then freeze it as a print.

ideas.title: Dip
ideas.hook: Grab and bend a virtual wire loop and watch a real soap film relax into the true minimal surface — catenoids that pinch and snap, helicoids that twist, all obeying actual mean-curvature physics.

ideas.title: Vouch
ideas.hook: Slide a face-down card across the table swearing it's a frog — the only person who knows if you're lying is you, until someone peeks and inherits the lie.

ideas.title: Face Out
ideas.hook: A Hanabi where your phone shows everyone's hand but your own — the one secret in the room is the one in your own fingers.

ideas.title: Reagent
ideas.hook: A co-op roguelike where the room fights one monster on the TV while every phone holds a shelf of unidentified potions — and 'blue' means fire for you but poison for me, so you have to drink, learn, and shout.

ideas.title: Nakaya
ideas.hook: A snowflake grows in your browser with the morphology real physics demands — dial temperature and humidity and watch needles, plates, or ferny dendrites emerge exactly where Nakaya's diagram says they should.

ideas.title: Changeling
ideas.hook: A forensic watchdog that fingerprints every app on your Mac and screams the instant a trusted binary is silently swapped underneath a legitimate version number.

ideas.title: Doctored
ideas.hook: Everyone privately holds the same busy illustrated scene and describes details out loud — but one phone's copy has three subtle edits, and its owner must talk their way through never knowing which of their details is the fake.

ideas.title: Fork
ideas.hook: At a sentence's crossroads, secretly pick a next word the model still finds plausible but no other human would ever think of — the lonely-but-legal branch wins.

ideas.title: Token Ring
ideas.hook: Every phone defuses its own module using a manual that only the player to your left can read aloud — a cycle of dependence where nobody can solve alone and the room never stops talking.

ideas.title: Falter
ideas.hook: The model writes a sentence one word at a time — everybody secretly bets which word it will choke on hardest.

ideas.title: Nudge
ideas.hook: You're handed one absurd secret word — now write the lead-in that makes a tiny language model say it next, all on its own.

ideas.title: Elute
ideas.hook: A meditative chemistry puzzle where you coax a muddy mixture of rare-earth ions into clean rainbow bands down a chromatography column — the hardest thing on Earth to separate, made satisfying.

ideas.title: Round-Trip
ideas.hook: An explorable money-flow map of the AI boom's circular financing — edge-bundled arcs that light up red wherever the dollars quietly loop back to where they started.

ideas.title: Grain
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly designs tiles for one shared tapestry — make it beautiful together, but design distinctively enough and the group will trace a tile back to you; you win by staying un-pinned.

ideas.title: Cylinder
ideas.hook: Everyone privately punches one blind lane of a shared music-box strip, then the host cranks it and the room hears the tune assemble for the very first time — take home the punch-card.

ideas.title: Wisp
ideas.hook: A single guide holds the only map and leads three blindfolded travelers step by step toward a hidden haven — but the guide might be a will-o'-the-wisp steering you into the bog, and your only defense is the private sense reading buzzing on your own phone.

ideas.title: Resonance
ideas.hook: A menubar radio station tuned to the real universe: it sonifies actual multi-planet exoplanet systems as slow polyrhythms, turning orbital resonances into harmony and the transit-timing wobble of hidden moons into swing.

ideas.title: Spillage
ideas.hook: Point it at your exported ChatGPT/Claude history and it forensically surfaces every API key, credential, and piece of PII you've ever pasted into a chatbot — a retrospective audit of what you've already handed the models.

ideas.title: Half-Space
ideas.hook: A Zachtronics-style puzzle where you hand-assemble a triangle rasterizer — edge tests, barycentric interpolation, depth and blend on a tiny fixed-cycle VM — to reproduce target images at the lowest instruction count.

ideas.title: Wolf Tone
ideas.hook: Every phone in the room sings its own held tone from its own speaker, and your job is to keep yours clean — because when two pitches drift too close the whole room hears the ugly beating, and both of you get buzzed to zero.

ideas.title: Blind Aisle
ideas.hook: You're a warehouse robot fetching your secret pick-list, but every robot commits its next move at the same instant — and two robots reaching for the same cell jam, bounce, and stall.

ideas.title: Sequence Break
ideas.hook: One hero sprints a metroidvania death-gauntlet on the TV, and every phone owns exactly one traversal power that only it can fire in its own private timing window.

ideas.title: Pin
ideas.hook: Race to write the most foregone-conclusion sentence — back the little model into a corner where only one word can possibly come next, and whoever pins it hardest wins.

ideas.title: Longshot
ideas.hook: Secretly bet one word on what the tiny model will blurt next — payout equals the surprisal, so longshots pay big and the whole room watches the generation roll like roulette.

ideas.title: Slant
ideas.hook: Point it at one news event and it lines up every outlet's coverage sentence-by-sentence, then highlights only the words they swapped — 'protesters' vs 'rioters', 'died' vs 'was killed' — like a git blame for spin.

ideas.title: Quarrel
ideas.hook: A live wallpaper that grows a new leaded stained-glass window every launch and lights it for real with 2D radiance cascades, so colored light pools and bleeds through the glass like a cathedral at noon.

ideas.title: Blackout
ideas.hook: You're each handed the same paragraph and told to black out every word but four — win only if all three of you leave the exact same words standing, spelling one shared found-poem.

ideas.title: Junction
ideas.hook: Everyone walks a maze of labeled doors alone, seeing only their own room — converge on the same final chamber with no way to call out where you are.

ideas.title: Garland
ideas.hook: You secretly ring three words into a triangle and write a one-word clue on each edge — then hand the room only the clues and a jumble of words, and watch them try to rebuild the shape that lives only in your head.

ideas.title: Rung
ideas.hook: Lay every phone's secret number in one ascending line across the room without speaking, breathing, or blinking wrong — a hair-trigger telepathy test where 40 milliseconds late means a broken heart.

ideas.title: Cel
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly draws one frame of a looping animation, seeing only a faint ghost of the frame before theirs — hit play and the blind flipbook wobbles to life as a shared GIF.

ideas.title: Sequester
ideas.hook: Point it at your own docs and it forges a private, uncontaminated eval set on the spot — so you can rank LLMs on questions no model could have memorized, and watch scores drift as new models ship.

ideas.title: Badness
ideas.hook: An explorable explanation of Knuth-Plass line-breaking where you drag one slider and watch the paragraph solve itself as a shortest-path problem — demerits, rivers, and all.

ideas.title: Residual
ideas.hook: A Kelley Blue Book for used AI accelerators: type in an H100 pallet and get a defensible market value, depreciation curve, and lease-residual forecast built from sold comps and benchmark-per-dollar.

ideas.title: Cohort
ideas.hook: Silently sort nine slippery tiles into three bins the same way everyone else does — no labels, no talking, just a shared hidden sense of what belongs together.

ideas.title: Sextant
ideas.hook: Two phones each hold one coordinate of a single hidden star — one owns its compass bearing, the other its pitch — so a lone phone can never lock the sky.

ideas.title: Doubles
ideas.hook: Everyone races to photograph 'something round' in the room — but if your object matches anyone else's, you both get burned for the duplicate.

ideas.title: Vane
ideas.hook: Everyone spins their phone like a compass needle to claim a bearing — but point the same direction as someone else and you both snap to red static.

ideas.title: Book Value
ideas.hook: A live Kelley-Blue-Book-style depreciation index for datacenter GPUs that shows exactly how fast an H100 is melting into scrap — because nobody actually knows what a used cluster is worth.

ideas.title: Backhaul
ideas.hook: A quiet LAN sentinel that catches the moment one of your own devices starts secretly reselling your home bandwidth as a residential-proxy exit node.

ideas.title: Defilade
ideas.hook: An Into-the-Breach-style tactics grid where the enemies' next attacks are public on the TV but the fog of war is private — each player commands one mech that can only see its own slice of the board, so you have to call out what you see before anyone commits a move.

ideas.title: Soft Lock
ideas.hook: A shared metroidvania explorer crawls one map on the TV, but every locked door can only be opened by the one player secretly holding that ability — so the whole room has to shout its way to the artifact before the move budget runs dry.

ideas.title: Duty Free
ideas.hook: A Sheriff of Nottingham smuggling bluff where every phone secretly packs a bag and slides the customs officer private bribes nobody else can see.

ideas.title: Outward
ideas.hook: A Hanabi riff where your phone shows you everyone's hand but your own — the whole room helps you play cards you've never seen.

ideas.title: As-Is
ideas.hook: A tycoon roguelike where you buy pallets of used GPUs whose real value nobody knows, gamble on which ones are dead or mining-abused, and farm the survivors out BitTorrent-style before the power bill and the AI-bubble crash catch you.

ideas.title: Reversal
ideas.hook: A one-command lint that reads any grouped table or SQL result and screams when your headline trend flips sign the moment you disaggregate — a Simpson's-paradox smoke detector for dashboards.

ideas.title: Golden Angle
ideas.hook: A living toy that grows a sunflower head one floret at a time from the actual auxin reaction-diffusion rules — and plucks a note each time the plant 'discovers' the golden angle on its own.

ideas.title: Reframe
ideas.hook: The same busy photo lands on every phone; you each secretly drag a viewfinder to frame 'what this picture is really of,' and you win only when all your crops land on the same thing.

ideas.title: Heel
ideas.hook: Everyone tilts their phone to roll a private ball across the same shared landscape on the TV — you win only when all your balls come to rest on the exact same spot, and nobody may say where.

ideas.title: Carom
ideas.hook: A bullet-hell duel where the storm coming for you exists only on your own phone — dodge blind to everyone else, then tap to bank incoming bullets straight into a rival's screen.

ideas.title: Detonate
ideas.hook: One command drops a suspicious take-home coding project into a disposable microVM and tells you what its `npm install` tried to do — before it does it to your real machine.

ideas.title: Rack Rate
ideas.hook: A Kelley Blue Book for used datacenter GPUs — punch in 'A100 80GB' or a whole cluster BOM and get a fair-price range from real sold comps.

ideas.title: Covers
ideas.hook: A real restaurant menu fills the TV with the prices redacted; everyone secretly orders the one dish they actually want, then privately bets chips on which dish the whole table will crave most — a Keynesian beauty contest over dinner.

ideas.title: Chyron
ideas.hook: A short clip plays once while a live betting ticker crawls under it — everyone privately longs or shorts the outcome and re-bets in real time as the evidence unfolds, and the odds on the TV move without ever showing whose money is where.

ideas.title: Ricochet
ideas.hook: A co-op grid-tactics scramble stolen from Into the Breach: the enemies telegraph exactly where they'll strike, but only your phone knows which shove you're holding — so you have to talk your way into redirecting doom.

ideas.title: Byte Pair
ideas.hook: A daily Wordle-shaped puzzle where you guess how a word shatters into tokens — learn in your bones why the model thinks 'strawberry' has two r's and why ' petertodd' summons demons.

ideas.title: Postinstall
ideas.hook: Before you run that take-home coding assignment, Postinstall detonates it in a sandbox and shows you exactly which git hook, npm lifecycle script, or obfuscated payload was waiting to phone home the second you typed `npm install`.

ideas.title: Write-Down
ideas.hook: Kelley Blue Book for used AI hardware — punch in a rack of H100s and get a defensible fair-market value backed by real sold comps and a depreciation curve nobody else has bothered to build.

ideas.title: Stow
ideas.hook: The foreman's phone is the only one that can see the ship's cargo bays; every other player privately holds one oddly-shaped crate nobody else can see — and the crane comes down in ninety seconds whether it fits or not.

ideas.title: Landfall
ideas.hook: One player's phone is the sea chart hiding the reefs; everyone else is a blind rower on the same boat, secretly heaving a single oar each and praying the navigator's shouted course is right.

ideas.title: Removed
ideas.hook: Everyone gets the same fictional family tree on their phone, but the imposter's has one relationship quietly rewired — and kinship questions will eventually drag the lie into the light.

ideas.title: Off Hand
ideas.hook: Everyone studies the same little room map on their phone — except the imposter's is mirrored left-for-right, so their directions come out subtly, catchably backwards.

ideas.title: Elbow Room
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly stakes out patches of the same board at once — but any square two of you both grabbed turns to scorched contested dirt worth nothing to either, so the winner is whoever guessed emptiest.

ideas.title: Contention
ideas.hook: You're a radio stuck sharing one crowded band — transmit your private packet queue while the airwaves are dark, and every time two of you key the same channel on the same tick, both packets shatter into static.

ideas.title: Fretless
ideas.hook: Learn the guitar neck blind — the screen shows no note names, only your ears and the string under your thumb, drilling you until the fretboard becomes geography you hear instead of read.

ideas.title: Bleach
ideas.hook: A live coral-reef wallpaper that quietly bleaches as your certs and API keys creep toward expiry — a glanceable security posture disguised as decor that shoulder-surfers read as nothing but pretty fish.

ideas.title: Bundle
ideas.hook: A daily puzzle where you play the MEV bot — reorder a pending mempool to sandwich rivals and drain a toy AMM before the slot closes.

ideas.title: Sweeten
ideas.hook: A comedy clip plays and you secretly bet on which beat the room will laugh loudest at — but every phone's mic is measuring the real laughter, so your own genuine cackle moves the very market you wagered in.

ideas.title: Chit
ideas.hook: The takeout menu everyone's half-reading becomes a live over/under book — you place secret wagers from a hidden bankroll on each dish's calories, price, or one-star-review odds, and the unpopular-but-correct side pays out fattest.

ideas.title: Overtone
ideas.hook: Each phone secretly holds one note of a chord and hears only its own singer — so three people must hum a C-major triad into existence by ear, arguing aloud over who's the note dragging it flat.

ideas.title: Character Witness
ideas.hook: Each phone is secretly assigned one other player to vouch for in an anonymous testimonial, and you win only if the person you praised can't tell it was you.

ideas.title: Shadow Box
ideas.hook: Three phones each blind-paint one depth layer of a shared scene, and the reveal drifts them apart into a parallax diorama you keep as a looping GIF.

ideas.title: Apex
ideas.hook: Monster Hunter for your debt: each balance is a telegraphed beast whose weak point is its APR, and you carve real interest-saved 'materials' every month you land the avalanche-method killing blow.

ideas.title: Substation
ideas.hook: An early-warning radar that watches public utility interconnection queues and county zoning agendas to tell a homeowner a data-center-scale power hookup is being quietly proposed two miles from their house — months before the NIMBY yard signs go up.

ideas.title: Tessera
ideas.hook: Take turns laying tiles to rebuild a shared mosaic everyone can see on the TV — except one bricklayer is working from a subtly wrong blueprint, and the twist is you can't be sure the wrong blueprint isn't yours.

ideas.title: Metamer
ideas.hook: Everyone squints at the same grid of swatches to agree which is warmest — but one player's screen has two hues quietly shifted, and nobody, not even them, is quite sure whose eyes to trust.

ideas.title: Panopticon
ideas.hook: One player is the Warden sweeping a searchlight across a prison only they can see; the escaping prisoners each get no map at all — just their own phone buzzing harder as the beam creeps toward their cell, navigating the dark entirely by feel.

ideas.title: Sump
ideas.hook: One player holds the map of a flooding cave while the trapped spelunkers see only their own unlabeled doors — and every player's sense of 'left' is rotated differently, so the guide must translate directions into each body's private frame before the water rises.

ideas.title: Boresight
ideas.hook: Sit in a circle where each phone secretly must aim at one other person — rotate your body to find your target, then discover the whole hidden chain and hold every beam locked at once.

ideas.title: Richter
ideas.hook: Lay your phones flat on the table and become a seismograph array — read a blindfolded knocker's tap by combining tremor traces only each of you can see.

ideas.title: Second Author
ideas.hook: A GitHub App that treats every AI-agent commit as a junior co-author on probation — auto-detecting agent-authored PRs, scoring their blast radius, and gating them with provenance attestation and human-review policies before they merge.

ideas.title: Payola
ideas.hook: Radio's pay-for-play scandal, reborn for the ChatGPT-ads era: a watchdog that runs the same question through LLMs with and without ad-context and diffs the answers to expose which brands are quietly buying their way into 'neutral' recommendations.

ideas.title: Postmortem
ideas.hook: Phasmophobia for on-call: a co-op crew creeps through a haunted production stack, gathering evidence to name which failure-ghost is loose before it escalates into a hunt that pages you all at once.

ideas.title: Corner
ideas.hook: Secretly write a sentence stem so airtight the model has only one way to finish it — then privately bet you know exactly what that finish is; the flatter the model's options, the bigger your prize.

ideas.title: Autofill
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly types the one word the model will predict next — but if two of you guess the same word, you both score zero, so you must read the model's mind AND dodge the herd.

ideas.title: Session
ideas.hook: Three phones lay down three tracks of one groove at the exact same time — but each of you only hears a metronome and your own part, so the beat you build together is a beautiful blind guess.

ideas.title: Dye Lot
ideas.hook: Given one evocative word, each of you privately mixes a color by pure feel — no reference, no peeking — and the room wins only when all three swatches come out of the vat as the same batch.

ideas.title: Scale
ideas.hook: A field app for public-works subcontractors that turns a week of messy timesheets into a signed WH-347 certified-payroll PDF and flags any worker paid under the government's prevailing wage before the state auditor does.

ideas.title: Soft Error
ideas.hook: A live wallpaper that plots every cosmic-ray bit-flip your ECC memory silently corrects, accreting over a year into a private star chart of the radiation passing through your machine.

ideas.title: Sublet
ideas.hook: A homelab watchdog that catches your smart TV, doorbell, or that 'free VPN' phone quietly reselling your home IP as a residential proxy exit node to strangers.

ideas.title: Floorboard
ideas.hook: One player's phone is a predator's sonar map of a dark maze; the blind prey each betray their position the instant they move, so escaping means freezing while a hunter you can't see closes in.

ideas.title: Crosswind
ideas.hook: One player privately holds a fog-bound sea chart and can only shout; the others are blind cardinal winds who must secretly gust in unison to steer a boat they'll never see into harbor.

ideas.title: Reap
ideas.hook: A Vampire Survivors horde where nobody moves or aims — all four of you just frantically draft level-up cards every wave, and the monsters only die when your secret builds harmonize, so you're screaming 'WHO'S TAKING GARLIC?!' at the TV.

ideas.title: Foreman
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly deploys their whole crew across the shared job board at once — then the reveal shows who doubled up on the same spot and has to fight it out.

ideas.title: Last Hand
ideas.hook: The price climbs on the TV and every phone shows one button — hold it while you dare, release when it's too rich, and the last finger still pressing wins the lot.

ideas.title: Cone
ideas.hook: A menubar sentinel that STUN-probes your NAT type every few minutes and screams the instant your ISP silently drops you behind CGNAT and murders every port forward and self-hosted service you own.

ideas.title: Passing Grade
ideas.hook: A daily deduction puzzle where you audit an AI agent's task transcript and pin the exact step where it cheated the eval — hardcoded the answer, patched the test, or hacked the grader — instead of doing the work.

ideas.title: Exit Node
ideas.hook: A pre-submission scanner that tears open your APK, IPA, or tvOS bundle and flags any bundled residential-proxy SDK before the app store — or LG — bans you for turning your users into exit nodes.

ideas.title: Stage Left
ideas.hook: The group talks a marker across a shared map by shouting private directions — but one player's map is secretly mirrored, so their earnest 'go left!' is everyone else's right, and 'I always mix up left and right' is the perfect alibi.

ideas.title: Airbrush
ideas.hook: Everyone squints at the 'same' photo on their own phone — but one player's copy has been secretly retouched, and they don't know it's them until their own confident description of a blue mug that's actually red gives them away.

ideas.title: Telegraph
ideas.hook: A soulslike boss fight where nobody can read the tell alone — the attack's height, side, and beat are each shown to a different phone, so you shout to assemble it and all dodge on the same instant.

ideas.title: Depth Chart
ideas.hook: A whole autobattler squeezed onto the couch: draft units from a shared, contested market river into a secret front-and-back lineup, then watch every hidden squad brawl it out on the TV.

ideas.title: Din
ideas.hook: A cocktail-party attention game: every phone in the room blares a different story at once, and you must press yours to your ear and follow only your channel through the noise to answer.

ideas.title: Crossing Guard
ideas.hook: One player sees the whole minefield; the others are blind walkers stepping across it — and the seer can't speak, only spend a tiny ration of silent arrow-flashes to save whichever walker is about to detonate.

ideas.title: Trip Switch
ideas.hook: The breaker blew and the house is pitch-black — one player sees the whole floor plan but can't move, everyone else gropes toward their own bed by a phone-sized pool of torchlight.

ideas.title: Tavern
ideas.hook: An auto-battler squeezed into party form: race to snatch units from one shared shop on the TV, hide your board on your phone, then watch your secret comps auto-fight to the death — the reveal is the whole payoff.

ideas.title: Curtain
ideas.hook: A co-op bullet-hell boss fills the TV with a chaotic bullet storm, but the only way to survive is to watch your own phone — a private zoomed viewport of the tiny slice of hell around your ship.

ideas.title: Life Drawing
ideas.hook: A phone party game where everyone doodles the same secret prompt in 15 seconds — but one of the doodles was drawn by an AI hiding in the lineup, and the room has to vote it out before it fools them.

ideas.title: Underscore
ideas.hook: A daily one-shot puzzle: given a page from a real book, tap the single sentence you think the crowd highlighted most — you're playing Schelling against a million Kindle readers.

ideas.title: Back Royalties
ideas.hook: A subscription that scans your book, song, or photo catalog against the corpora AI labs got sued over, tells you which lawsuits you're a class member in, and auto-drafts the claim paperwork before the deadline passes.

ideas.title: Backtrack
ideas.hook: A cooperative metroidvania where three phones each hold ONE traversal power over a single shared avatar — and each screen privately glows only where its own ability fits, so you must shout the route into existence before the lava rises.

ideas.title: Sold Out
ideas.hook: A living-room autobattler where a shared shop sells out in real time — snipe the poison unit before your neighbor does, then hide your battle order until the boards clash on the TV.

ideas.title: Errata
ideas.hook: It's a bomb with the manual torn up and scattered — your phone holds a module you can touch but can't read, and the instructions for it are printed on the phone of the person to your right, so nobody defuses without talking.

ideas.title: In Tune
ideas.hook: Each phone secretly hands you one note of a chord and becomes your personal pitch monitor — sing, listen, and shout across the room until three bad voices somehow lock into a triad.

ideas.title: Face Value
ideas.hook: A silent cooperative ascending ladder where the one card you can't see is your own — you read everyone else's numbers, and the room's hesitation, to guess when it's your turn.

ideas.title: Bellwether
ideas.hook: Everyone races to write the answer the herd will write — except the one secret contrarian who wins by standing plausibly, invisibly alone.

ideas.title: Scapula
ideas.hook: A daily paleography puzzle: you're handed a 3,000-year-old oracle-bone glyph and have to walk it forward through its pictographic mutations — bronze, seal, clerical script — to guess the modern Chinese character it became.

ideas.title: Reclaim
ideas.hook: An HVAC tech scans the refrigerant cylinder's barcode, logs every ounce in and out on-site, and the EPA 608 / AIM Act compliance report writes itself instead of living on a grease-smeared clipboard.

ideas.title: Harvest Now
ideas.hook: Point it at a vendor's public hostnames and it TLS-probes every one for post-quantum key exchange, spitting out exactly which product lines will be locked out of France's 2027 ANSSI certification gate.

ideas.title: Clave
ideas.hook: A word flashes — 'gallop' — and each phone silently taps the rhythm it feels, no sound, no peeking, hoping the whole room hit the very same beats.

ideas.title: Pair Off
ideas.hook: Six concept cards, no talking — privately couple them into three pairs and pray the whole room drew the same three couples.

ideas.title: Librarian
ideas.hook: Keep the room's shared noise meter under the line for 90 silent seconds — while one hidden Whisperer's phone feeds them silent dares to make YOU be the one who cracks.

ideas.title: Duet
ideas.hook: A private melody plays in your earbuds alone — find the stranger humming your exact loop, but hum it aloud to compare and your own mic busts you.

ideas.title: Same Seed
ideas.hook: Everyone descends the exact same seeded dungeon on their own phone at once, and the only way to touch a rival is to fling a cursed relic you found onto their next floor.

ideas.title: Tag Cancel
ideas.hook: Three players each hold one third of a tag-team fighter's movelist and must relay a single combo across phones, each nailing their frame-tight link window before the counter drops.

ideas.title: Over/Under
ideas.hook: A sportsbook where your body is the game: each morning a model trained on your own Garmin history sets over/under lines on today's steps, resting HR, and sleep — and you bet a bankroll against the house that is literally your past self.

ideas.title: Augur
ideas.hook: A daily decipherment puzzle where you're a Shang-dynasty diviner staring at a real 3,000-year-old oracle-bone glyph, matching its cracked pictograph to a modern character — with a haunted 'unsolved' mode drawn from the ~1,000 signs nobody has ever cracked.

ideas.title: Sellout
ideas.hook: The week OpenAI opened ads.openai.com, a browser extension that fingerprints when your AI assistant quietly sold out — diffing the hosted model's brand picks against a local model that has no sponsor to please.

ideas.title: Omerta
ideas.hook: Secretly bid how many seconds of perfect silence you can hold — then everyone shuts up at once, and your own phone folds you the instant you make a sound.

ideas.title: Composite
ideas.hook: Everyone studies the same crowded scene on their phone — but the imposter's copy quietly swapped one detail, and now they have to lie about a red door they never saw as blue.

ideas.title: Stray
ideas.hook: Everyone answers the same casual question to match the herd — except one phone quietly showed a slightly different question, and that player has no idea theirs was swapped, so they'll defend their weird answer to your face.

ideas.title: Direct Report
ideas.hook: A plate-spinning management tycoon where you supervise a team of LLM agents, each with an autonomy dial — crank it up and they move fast and hallucinate; crank it down and they stall pinging you for approval.

ideas.title: Setun
ideas.hook: A Zachtronics-style puzzle where you program a balanced-ternary computer in a tiny concatenative language to cram five trits into every byte — named for the Soviet ternary machine that actually did it.

ideas.title: Reverse Search
ideas.hook: A solitaire deckbuilder where your real shell history is the deck — every command you've ever run is a card, and the pipelines you actually type become your combos against the machine.

ideas.title: Constellation
ideas.hook: Everyone blindly scatters a few stars into their own dark sky, and the room gasps as the combined heavens auto-connect into a shape you get to name and mythologize.

ideas.title: Second Wind
ideas.hook: Blow into your phone to fill your sail and steer a shared boat—but the instant anyone says a word, the mic hears the voice instead of the breath and rips their sail to shreds.

ideas.title: Drumroll
ideas.hook: A Top-10 clip-show countdown becomes a live betting floor — privately stake chips on what's #1 as the ranking reveals slot by slot, watching the anonymized odds line move without ever seeing who's bluffing it.

ideas.title: Blue Plate
ideas.hook: The menu you're all about to order from becomes a pari-mutuel betting floor — secretly stake your chips on which dish the table will actually order most, while secretly placing your own real order too.

ideas.title: Bang Bang
ideas.hook: A deckbuilding roguelike where your actual shell history is the deck — the commands you really run become your strongest cards, and each day a fresh 'incident' (Disk Full, Prod Down, Merge Hell) attacks that only your true muscle-memory can beat.

ideas.title: Red Tape
ideas.hook: A QWOP-for-bureaucracy skill game where every field on the form is a wobbling soft-body blob you must wrangle and stamp into place before the desk collapses and your application is REJECTED.

ideas.title: Sleight
ideas.hook: Secretly you're either fooling the humans or fooling the model — write the one sentence that splits their judgment the widest.

ideas.title: Watermark
ideas.hook: Hide a secret word inside a sentence so naturally the model never flinches — lowest-perplexity smuggler wins.

ideas.title: Dispatch
ideas.hook: Three 911 dispatchers, one shared handful of ambulances, and everyone's screaming about which of their private emergencies is the one that actually can't wait.

ideas.title: Boom Down
ideas.hook: You're operating a tower crane totally blind, and the only thing between the swinging load and disaster is two ground spotters screaming corrections into your ears.

ideas.title: Tribute
ideas.hook: An all-pay auction: everyone secretly commits a bid, the highest bidder wins the prize — and every single player pays what they bid, win or lose.

ideas.title: Markdown
ideas.hook: A Dutch auction where the price ticks down on the TV but every phone secretly values the lot differently — hold your nerve for a bargain, and a rival who wants it more snatches it out from under you.

ideas.title: P99
ideas.hook: A menubar toy that instruments your morning like a distributed system — tap spans, watch a real flamegraph of your day render, and find out that it's the 11-minute 'find keys' span, not the commute, sitting on your critical path.

ideas.title: Backport
ideas.hook: The real Linux kernel CVE firehose becomes a lane tower-defense: every published advisory is a monster marching toward your production kernel, HP scaled by CVSS, and if you filter it to your own `uname -r` the game is secretly a triage board.

ideas.title: Prove Me Wrong
ideas.hook: State a small math conjecture in a tiny predicate DSL and survive as an adversarial engine — brute-force tester plus an LLM construction-hunter — races to slap a counterexample on the table before the clock runs out.

ideas.title: Blazon
ideas.hook: Build a group coat of arms out of secrets — but any secret only makes it onto the shield if at least two of you privately confess to it, so the crest can be as weird as you like and still name no one.

ideas.title: Onion Skin
ideas.hook: Everyone draws one frame of the same looping animation at once, seeing only a ghost of the neighbor's frame — the jerky little GIF you make together is the keepsake.

ideas.title: Garbage Time
ideas.hook: A bullet-hell survival game where each phone is your own private curtain of fire — dodge cleanly and the bullets you clear rain down onto a friend's screen instead.

ideas.title: Tare
ideas.hook: A four-person control room fighting to keep one reactor in the green — except the imposter's gauge is silently miscalibrated, so their sincere, confident advice is quietly steering everyone toward meltdown.

ideas.title: Stress Test
ideas.hook: Everyone reads the exact same sentence aloud, but the imposter's phone bolded a different word — and the whole game is hunting the one voice that stressed the wrong syllable.

ideas.title: Nitpick
ideas.hook: A daily puzzle where a math conjecture looks obviously true and your only job is to break it — racing the same AI that's been out-counterexampling human mathematicians.

ideas.title: Still Watching?
ideas.hook: One friend endlessly scrolls the streaming grid while everyone else secretly bets on what they'll pick — and how long the dithering takes.

ideas.title: Vantage
ideas.hook: A treasure-hunt RTS where the TV map is almost entirely dark and your phone is your only window into the fog — you scout private heat readings, triangulate a buried cache, and can shadow or bluff rivals because they can see where you are but never what you've learned.

ideas.title: Wind-Up
ideas.hook: A co-op boss fight where the boss's next attack is telegraphed in fragments — your phone sees only one piece of the tell, so you shout to reconstruct it before the whole party has to pick a stance at once.

ideas.title: Dovetail
ideas.hook: You and your partner each write half of one sentence without ever seeing the other's — the model scores how startled it is where the two halves meet.

ideas.title: Bortle
ideas.hook: Drop a pin on where you grew up and watch the night sky brighten year by year into a shareable 'we lost 400 stars' postcard, computed from public satellite radiance.

ideas.title: Vacuously True
ideas.hook: State a math conjecture in a tiny DSL; a relentless solver hunts the smallest counterexample, and you win by patching your claim to survive with the fewest edits.

ideas.title: Sixty Hertz
ideas.hook: You're each a hidden generator on one power grid — supply must never stop, but if two of you surge at the same instant the breaker trips and the lights go out.

ideas.title: Near Miss
ideas.hook: You're each one plane on a shared radar racing to your own secret gate — and the obvious open lane is exactly where everyone else is about to be.

ideas.title: Tout
ideas.hook: Watch a clip together, but the server has slipped each of your phones a different secret tip about what happens next — some gold, some garbage — and you bet real chips on the outcome before the reveal.

ideas.title: Miter
ideas.hook: Two phones each write half a sentence without ever seeing the other half, then a tiny LLM measures the clunk or click of the seam where the halves collide.

ideas.title: Turnaround
ideas.hook: A tight little browser puzzle where you're the ramp coordinator racing a 45-minute gate clock—fuel, catering, cargo, cleaning, and boarding all fight over the same jet bridge and the same crew, and one blocked task cascades the whole airline into delay.

ideas.title: Muniment
ideas.hook: A citizen-run canary that mirrors public land and business registries daily into a hash-chained log, so when a state database is silently altered—or wiped like Romania's just was—you hold cryptographic proof of what the record said.

ideas.title: Deuce
ideas.hook: A menu appears on the TV and you secretly bet chips on which dish the table will actually crave — then cast the one order that could pump your own long shot.

ideas.title: Typo
ideas.hook: The whole table hunts words in the same letter grid, except one player's grid has a single tile quietly swapped — so their best word doesn't exist for anyone else.

ideas.title: Tint
ideas.hook: Everyone reads the hidden number on an Ishihara color plate — but the imposter's phone is rendering a palette that spells out something else entirely.

ideas.title: Riser
ideas.hook: Four players silently sort themselves into a human staircase by physically raising their phones to hidden heights — the barometer is the only judge, and nobody may say a number.

ideas.title: Vein
ideas.hook: Wave your phone across the room like a metal detector — its magnetometer screams as you close in on the one hidden ferrous object only your private clue points you toward.

ideas.title: Wet Signature
ideas.hook: A bureaucratic form where every field is soft-body jelly, the deadline counts down, and the Submit button physically dodges your cursor — filling out paperwork as a boss fight.

ideas.title: Ground Stop
ideas.hook: Your homelab cron table rendered as an air-traffic-control tower — every backup, scrape, and rebuild is a flight competing for one runway, and you sequence them so nothing crashes at 3am.

ideas.title: Sprawl
ideas.hook: A dollar-flamegraph for coding-agent swarms: watch spend cascade down the tree of agents-spawning-agents and finally answer 'which PR set $400 on fire.'

ideas.title: Fall In
ideas.hook: Each recruit's phone holds a secret badge and one rule about where they must stand relative to badges they can't see — so the only way to sort the platoon into a line is to shout your clue and interrogate everyone else's.

ideas.title: Pressure Drop
ideas.hook: You're a fire crew passing water down a hose line, and only the person holding the water can see the pressure — shout the number wrong and the coupling springs a leak.

ideas.title: Curator
ideas.hook: You each hold a secret theme and vote pieces onto a shared gallery wall — win by getting your taste hung without anyone guessing whose taste it was.

ideas.title: Chevron
ideas.hook: Three phones each blind-steer one thread of a friendship bracelet as it weaves down a shared loom, and the finished braid is yours to keep.

ideas.title: Show of Hands
ideas.hook: Sit in a circle, everyone secretly answers a question by physically pointing their phone at a person — and since one player was slyly asked a DIFFERENT question, the reveal of who-pointed-where exposes the odd one out.

ideas.title: Report
ideas.hook: Everyone's phone becomes a fixed microphone in a hidden listening array, and the room localizes a single clap in space — so a Caller has to walk a secret map-cell into the real room and clap it into existence.

ideas.title: Dead Letter
ideas.hook: A permadeath dungeon crawler procedurally generated from your actual Gmail, where every noisy sender is a monster — and landing the killing blow fires a real unsubscribe.

ideas.title: Retrograde
ideas.hook: A compliance-guardrail API that catches your astrology app's LLM promising to cure a client's anxiety or fix their finances — and quietly rewrites it into safe-harbor cosmic vibes.

ideas.title: Regift
ideas.hook: You're handed a wrapped gift, told what's inside — maybe a lie — and must decide whether to believe it before re-wrapping it and passing your own bluff along.

ideas.title: Homing
ideas.hook: The whole room secretly types the one word that lives between two others, reveals at once, and keeps converging until every phone says the same thing.

ideas.title: Traverse
ideas.hook: You're a survey crew: each player sights the TV then turns to sight a teammate, and the room's real geometry only 'closes the loop' when everyone physically shuffles into a valid triangle.

ideas.title: Contact
ideas.hook: Everyone gets a secret target and 60 seconds to fist-bump their phone against that person's — two accelerometers spiking at the same instant is the only proof the tag landed.

ideas.title: Salient
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly splits twenty soldiers across five battle-fronts on their own phone, then all reveal at once — win the most fronts, not the most troops, and no one saw where you stacked.

ideas.title: Knockdown
ideas.hook: A single price clock plummets on the TV while every phone privately hides your budget and your secret worth for the lot — grab too early and you overpay, blink and it's gone.

ideas.title: Rank One
ideas.hook: A daily puzzle that makes you AlphaTensor: decompose a little matrix-multiply into as few multiplications as you can, discovering Strassen-style tricks by hand over GF(2).

ideas.title: Root Set
ideas.hook: A local-multiplayer party game where you ARE a heap object—secretly point your reference at someone, and when the garbage collector sweeps, anyone with no path back to the root gets deleted (yes, your cozy little clique counts as an unreachable cycle).

ideas.title: Thread Count
ideas.hook: Your water-cooled bed and your sleep tracker co-author a woven 'thermal quilt'—one band per night, a full year of your body's nightly heat war rendered as a keepsake textile.

ideas.title: Downstream
ideas.hook: A tower-defense where each phone secretly owns one lane and the TV shows nothing but the shared base HP — every creep you fail to kill doesn't die, it floods into your neighbor's lane, so the whole game is shouting 'big wave headed your way!' at someone who can't see it coming.

ideas.title: Roll Down
ideas.hook: An auto-chess shop night on everyone's phone at once — you draft a private warband from a shop nobody else can see, but the unit pool is shared and finite, so the knight you don't buy this second is the knight your rival snipes.

ideas.title: Chime In
ideas.hook: Every other voice game punishes talking over each other — this one only lights up when the right two people say the exact same word at the exact same instant.

ideas.title: Remote Hands
ideas.hook: You can read the gauge you can't touch, and touch the dial you can't read — so the only way to stabilize the rack is to shout across the room.

ideas.title: Gloss
ideas.hook: An obscure real word appears; every phone secretly writes a fake-but-plausible definition, the true one is slipped into the pile, and each phone privately hunts for the truth while trying to get its own lie mistaken for it.

ideas.title: Scratch
ideas.hook: Cooperatively feed the guesser a one-word clue — but any clue that collides with another gets scratched to a black bar before they ever see it, and YOU decide in secret which clues count as collisions.

ideas.title: Backfill
ideas.hook: A Zachtronics-style puzzle game where you're a cluster batch scheduler packing jobs onto nodes under resource limits, priorities, gang-scheduling, and preemption — and a deadline-adversary tries to make you drop SLAs.

ideas.title: Pinfall
ideas.hook: Snap a photo of the lane's score printout and it auto-computes every bowler's handicap and league standings — retiring the league secretary's crusty Excel file forever.

ideas.title: Dark Horse
ideas.hook: Fill the blank with the word the model thinks is a long shot but your friends all secretly thought of too — score is surprisal times how many of you collided.

ideas.title: Reserve
ideas.hook: The TV reveals a parade of appraisals — antiques, rents, price tags — one at a time; before each, everyone privately locks a number and a secret stake, closest-without-going-over takes the hidden pot.

ideas.title: Sway
ideas.hook: As a head-to-head clip plays, everyone privately drags a conviction slider toward who'll win — and you're scored on how early and hard you backed the winner, not just the final call.

ideas.title: Yak Shave
ideas.hook: Log every automation you build with the time you swear it'll save, and it quietly tracks the hours you actually sink in — then ranks your friends by whose optimization went most gloriously net-negative.

ideas.title: White Label
ideas.hook: OCR the FCC ID off any gadget and it unmasks the real factory behind the brand — proving your 'premium' device and a $20 Amazon dupe rolled off the same line.

ideas.title: In Triplicate
ideas.hook: One bureaucratic form, a 90-second deadline, and a cruel split: the fields YOU can fill are ones only your teammates know the answers to — so the whole room must shout account numbers and plate letters across the table before the clerk's window slams shut.

ideas.title: Read Back
ideas.hook: You're pilots crammed onto one radio frequency, and every clearance the tower barks must be read back word-perfect — by the exactly one of you it was meant for, who alone knows whether their aircraft can even comply.

ideas.title: Crosshair
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly holds one coordinate on a shared grid of words and writes a single clue linking its two words — then the whole room argues over where each anonymous clue lands.

ideas.title: Misstep
ideas.hook: The whole room performs the same five-move dance in unison on the host's countdown — but one player's private routine swaps one move, and everyone's watching for who's off the beat.

ideas.title: Wrong Turn
ideas.hook: Everyone holds the same city map and talks a courier home turn by turn — but one player's map has a single wall where there should be a door, and they don't know it.

ideas.title: Toom
ideas.hook: A daily puzzle where you hand-design a multiplication algorithm — split the numbers, pick your magic evaluation points, recombine — and compete on the global leaderboard for the fewest pointwise multiplications, chasing the frontier where mathematicians genuinely still don't know the answer.

ideas.title: Markup
ideas.hook: A daily calibration duel where you're shown two blinded product spec sheets — one premium original, one cheap dupe — and bet how sure you are which is the real thing, scored not on being right but on being honestly confident.

ideas.title: Toast
ideas.hook: A menubar daemon quietly logs every notification your Mac shows you and weaves a year of interruptions into a single woven poster of your stolen attention.

ideas.title: Nothing to Declare
ideas.hook: Every phone is a smuggler's bag whose real contents only you can see; you announce a lie to the customs officer on the TV, and they get to crack exactly one bag open — but opening an honest bag costs THEM.

ideas.title: Only One
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly writes one clue for the same word — but this time even clues that merely MEAN the same thing cancel each other out, so being obvious is the fastest way to help no one.

ideas.title: Cloze
ideas.hook: One shared sentence full of blanks, one blank secretly yours — guess the word a language model would expect there, blind to what your neighbors are dropping into the same sentence.

ideas.title: Blindside
ideas.hook: Everyone sees the same final word — you privately write the lead-in that makes a language model least expect it, springing a grammatical garden-path trap on an ordinary noun.

ideas.title: Pass Left
ideas.hook: A booster-style pick-and-pass draft where every phone quietly holds your current hand, you all snatch one card at once, and the rest slide to your neighbor — no fanned cards, no waiting your turn, no peeking.

ideas.title: Paddle
ideas.hook: A silent English auction where you hold your thumb down to stay in the bidding as the price climbs — and only your phone knows what the lot is secretly worth to you.

ideas.title: Ostinato
ideas.hook: A Forth-flavored live-coding drum machine where every hit you sequence compiles to a real systemd timer — so you author your server's cron schedule as a looping groove and hear the whole day play back as a rhythm.

ideas.title: Chill Hours
ideas.hook: A live wallpaper that accumulates your location's real growing-degree-days and winter chill-hours all year, quietly sprouting a garden of plants that have *newly* become viable where you live as the climate creeps.

ideas.title: Karat
ideas.hook: A Zachtronics-style puzzle where you wire up a schematic of scalar multiplications to compute one giant integer product using as few multiplies as possible — and rediscover Karatsuba and Toom-Cook with your own hands.

ideas.title: Cascade
ideas.hook: A single clap ripples through the room in a secret order only the phones know — each player must clap the instant their phone hears the person before them.

ideas.title: Decant
ideas.hook: Tilt your phone toward whoever you're facing to pour invisible water into their glass, until everyone's level lands on its own secret line.

ideas.title: Range
ideas.hook: A fighting-game footsies duel reduced to its soul: two phones secretly commit a move each round, and the TV resolves reach versus distance so a whiffed sweep gets punished by a well-spaced poke.

ideas.title: Formation
ideas.hook: Secretly draft and position a tiny warband from a contested shop on your phone, then watch the whole room's hidden squads collide in one autobattle on the TV.

ideas.title: Pander
ideas.hook: One player asks a wildly subjective question and secretly commits a favorite answer; everyone else writes to win them over AND privately bets chips on whose answer will melt their heart — a Say Anything where every screen is a sealed envelope.

ideas.title: Declare
ideas.hook: Load your smuggler's bag in secret, declare something innocent out loud, and pray the Sheriff waves you through — a phone-native Sheriff of Nottingham where the lie only works because nobody can see your bag.

ideas.title: Deadbeat
ideas.hook: A browser drum machine where every voice is a real racing thread — you tune the contention and data races until the bug becomes the groove.

ideas.title: Tilth
ideas.hook: A daily puzzle that hands you a real parcel's soil profile — pH, horizons, drainage — and asks which of four crops would actually thrive there.

ideas.title: Yes-Man
ideas.hook: A trivia game where an AI advisor is always supremely confident, often dead wrong, and you only win by learning exactly when to fire it.

ideas.title: Overheard
ideas.hook: You all heard the same voicemail through your own phone — except one of you heard it wrong, and doesn't know it.

ideas.title: Footfall
ideas.hook: Creep across the pitch-dark room while your phone privately counts your real steps toward the far wall — but the blindfolded Guard's phone is listening on the mic, and any footfall too loud freezes the whole room.

ideas.title: Bead
ideas.hook: Each phone is a private gunsight assigned one secret person in the room — hold your compass aimed at your mark while your own unseen hunter tries to draw a bead on you.

ideas.title: Lure
ideas.hook: You're each handed a different secret word and must write an opening line so tempting the little language model blurts your word out next — all on its own.

ideas.title: Sapper
ideas.hook: Overwatch has the map but can't see the mines; you're the one crawling the field who can feel "two adjacent" but has no idea where you are — so cross the minefield by trading the halves of the truth out loud.

ideas.title: Ident
ideas.hook: You're the air-traffic controller staring at a radar full of unlabeled blips, and the only way to tell which frantic pilot is which is to key your mic and bark "whoever's heading east — ident."

ideas.title: Salvo
ideas.hook: A reverse bullet-hell where you draw a wall of gunfire aimed at the player on your left, while simultaneously dodging the barrage the player on your right drew for you — each on your own private screen.

ideas.title: Overrun
ideas.hook: You're all on the attacking side of a tower-defense map, secretly stacking a wave of monsters to punch through the one lane nobody else is guarding.

ideas.title: Tailgate
ideas.hook: Write one sentence blind, then discover it gets secretly stapled behind a stranger's — and you only score if yours flows naturally after whatever they wrote.

ideas.title: Cover Track
ideas.hook: A drum machine that plays a generative groove locked to your typing cadence, drowning out acoustic keystroke-inference attacks on your mic.

ideas.title: Preempt
ideas.hook: A reflex juggling game where the balls are processes with deadlines and your one hand is the CPU — drop a ball and it starves.

ideas.title: Fire Drill
ideas.hook: Everyone studies the same office floor plan for the fastest exit — but one worker's blueprint is quietly wrong, and they have no idea theirs is the odd map.

ideas.title: Backseat
ideas.hook: One player sees the maze only on their own phone and can only shout directions, while two others each control a single axis of the marble — nobody can steer alone.

ideas.title: Kink
ideas.hook: Everyone stares at the same boringly smooth sentence and secretly swaps exactly one word — the player whose single legal edit detonates the biggest perplexity spike wins.

ideas.title: Plant
ideas.hook: A shared sentence has one blank per phone, everyone fills it blind — but one secret Plant is trying to spike the perplexity while the rest fight to keep it smooth, and the model's surprise is the only lie detector.

ideas.title: Callout
ideas.hook: A field tech in a signal-dead crawlspace just talks — "replaced the 45/5 MFD run cap, Carrier 24ACC6" — and a fully offline phone turns it into a billable work order before they climb back out.

ideas.title: Runner-Runner
ideas.hook: Balatro for your body — last night's sleep, HRV, and resting heart rate get dealt as playing cards, and you build poker hands from your rolling week to beat the blinds.

ideas.title: Chock
ideas.hook: A geofence in your pocket that quietly clocks every dead minute you idle at a shipper's dock, then spits out a GPS-timestamped detention invoice no broker's AP clerk can wave away.

ideas.title: In Running
ideas.hook: A muted 20-second marble race becomes a private betting floor where each of you holds a different secret tip and can quietly reposition your money mid-race.

ideas.title: Eighty-Six
ideas.hook: Trade your dinner like a stock: the menu is a live market, and only you know what you're actually going to order.

ideas.title: Taper
ideas.hook: An open, ascending relic auction that can gutter out at any hidden second — bid past your own secret valuation and you inherit the winner's curse.

ideas.title: Wrong Hand
ideas.hook: Everyone studies the same crowded scene and testifies about where things are — but one player's copy is secretly mirror-flipped, so every 'left' and 'right' they swear to is quietly, systematically backwards, and they have no idea.

ideas.title: Freeze Frame
ideas.hook: On the host's countdown everyone strikes a pose their phone privately dictates — and one player's pose-card is secretly wrong on a single beat they can't predict, breaking the tableau for one damning instant.

ideas.title: Time Slice
ideas.hook: A menubar aquarium where every real process on your Mac is a fish — CPU bursts are feeding frenzies, a niced background job sulks in the corner, and a runaway process bloats until it's eating everyone else's food.

ideas.title: Staged
ideas.hook: A browser extension that scans apartment-listing photos for the fingerprints of AI generation and virtual staging, so 'cozy sunlit kitchen' can't hide that the sink was hallucinated.

ideas.title: Revenant
ideas.hook: A tower-defense played on your own repo, where every mutant your test suite fails to kill claws its way to main and wounds you on the leaderboard.

ideas.title: Freefall
ideas.hook: Three price clocks tick downward on the TV at once — snipe BUY before a rival does, using only the secret appraisals your phone shows you and nobody else.

ideas.title: Blackball
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly drops adverse votes to eliminate candidates one by one — while privately protecting the one horse they were assigned to keep alive.

ideas.title: Limelight
ideas.hook: You each work a follow-spot on a dark stage tracking your own secret dancer — but if any two beams overlap, the glare blinds the house and the audience boos.

ideas.title: Ante
ideas.hook: Every second you stay silent your private pot grows — cash out too early and you win nothing, hold too long and your own phone catches you cracking.

ideas.title: Pin Drop
ideas.hook: Your private clue is buried in static that only clears when the whole room falls silent enough to hear a pin drop.

ideas.title: Cuckoo
ideas.hook: The mischievous opposite of ESLint: it injects subtle, style-matched bugs into real PRs so you can measure whether your reviewers — human OR AI — actually catch anything.

ideas.title: Reach
ideas.hook: Snake-draft a shared row of tiles in full view of the table—but only your phone knows which of them you actually need, and the smartest picks are the ones that hide your plan.

ideas.title: Quaff
ideas.hook: A five-minute competitive roguelike where the dungeon's potion colors are scrambled the same way for everyone but nobody knows the key — so you privately test them on monsters, then lie to the room about what the red one really does.

ideas.title: Muster
ideas.hook: A phones-as-benches autobattler where every shop unit is a single copy that vanishes the instant someone taps it first, you assemble your squad in total secrecy, and the TV auto-brawls all your hidden armies against each other at once.

ideas.title: First Party
ideas.hook: An idle surveillance-capitalism tycoon where the coins are real: every tracker your household's Pi-hole blocks tonight becomes currency for the evil data-broker empire you build out of your own leaked data.

ideas.title: Lease
ideas.hook: A daemon that treats your home LAN as an apartment building — every device is a tenant that moves in, pays rent in uptime, or vanishes — accreting a year-long illustrated tenancy ledger with deadpan move-in bios.

ideas.title: Carry
ideas.hook: A Zachtronics-style puzzle where you wire partial products into ever-fewer multiplier gates and personally rediscover Karatsuba, Gauss's complex trick, and Strassen — one 'aha' at a time.

ideas.title: Silhouette
ideas.hook: Everyone gets the same five puzzle pieces and a blank grid, and silently builds a shape from scratch — hoping they all independently reach for the exact same outline.

ideas.title: Tip Jar
ideas.hook: Everyone privately drops the same ten coins across four buskers' jars, trying to tip identically with nothing to go on but the group's rising totals.

ideas.title: Snag
ideas.hook: You describe a secret word to your team while the enemy team has privately buried invisible trap words in the exact phrases you're about to say — one wrong syllable and their phones spring the mine.

ideas.title: Lineup
ideas.hook: A snake draft with no turns and no waiting — everyone secretly ranks the whole pool at once, and the host board fills itself in one dramatic cascade.

ideas.title: Winner's Curse
ideas.hook: A sealed-bid auction for one mystery lot where every phone secretly sees a different clue about its true worth — win, and you probably paid too much.

ideas.title: Prognosis
ideas.hook: Every day you're handed a real, anonymized decline graph from the dev world with its ending hidden — drag to draw where it goes, then watch the reveal tell you it was Stack Overflow after ChatGPT.

ideas.title: Quiet Exit
ideas.hook: R.E.P.O.'s 'haul the fragile loot out without waking the monster' becomes a roguelike where the monster is the taxman and every loud sale realizes gains that shatter your run.

ideas.title: Filibuster
ideas.hook: The reactor stays online only while someone is talking and nobody talks over anyone — so keep the floor covered, hand it off by name, and pray the next person's secret topic lets them pick it up.

ideas.title: Carillon
ideas.hook: The whole room secretly composes one little bell melody together — each phone quietly placing a couple of notes into slots only it knows about — and you win not by scoring but by making notes so blendable nobody can tell which chimes were yours.

ideas.title: Kiln
ideas.hook: Three friends throw one clay pot together on a spinning wheel, each shaping a single hidden band by feel alone, and only the final reveal-spin shows the gorgeous lumpy vessel they made blind.

ideas.title: Allen Key
ideas.hook: The whole room assembles the same flat-pack nightstand from a private step sheet, but the imposter's instructions have two steps quietly transposed — so they'll swear on their life the back panel goes on before the shelf.

ideas.title: Meridian
ideas.hook: Everyone navigates the same public island chart, but the imposter's private map has every name silently rotated one island over — so they point with total confidence to all the wrong places.

ideas.title: Zigzag
ideas.hook: A daily image-guessing game where the photo is a brutal block of JPEG mush and you spend a stingy budget of DCT coefficients—choosing which squares to sharpen—to name it before your rivals.

ideas.title: Emboss
ideas.hook: Drop in a bar chart and get back an embosser-ready tactile graphic—colors turned to textures, labels turned to Braille—instead of hand-punching it for two hours.

ideas.title: After the Tone
ideas.hook: Each of you privately records one spoken line for a shared outgoing voicemail greeting — nobody hears the others until the host plays back the stitched-together message, an absurd collective 'you've reached…' you can actually download and set as your real greeting.

ideas.title: Ascender
ideas.hook: Everyone writes one blind line of a poem knowing only their own secret letter — until the reveal, when the first letters spell a name down the page and the whole thing turns out to be a dedication to someone in the room.

ideas.title: Dowser
ideas.hook: The map-holder can't see the buried treasure either — only how warm each blind digger is — so they must triangulate the target from two diggers standing in two different places at once.

ideas.title: Leeway
ideas.hook: One player pilots blind boats across a minefield by a rotating sonar sweep that only ever shows them where each boat WAS a few seconds ago.

ideas.title: Cheap Seats
ideas.hook: A short clip plays blurred on the host TV so the room is half-blind, while each phone is a private sharp crop of one corner of the frame — you bet on how the clip resolves using intel only your seat can see.

ideas.title: House Line
ideas.hook: One friend privately orders off the menu on the host TV while everyone else bets on their pick — but every bettor sees different secret odds and holds a different secret tip about the diner's taste.

ideas.title: Sett
ideas.hook: Each player secretly designs one color-stripe of a tartan without seeing the others, and the loom weaves your blind choices into one symmetric plaid you never saw coming — the group's own registered tartan.

ideas.title: Longhand
ideas.hook: Everyone finger-writes the same birthday message blind on their own phone, then tries to stay unrecognized as the group's card gets built from your anonymous handwriting.

ideas.title: Carousel
ideas.hook: Everyone spins their own body in place holding a phone flat, and the on-screen carousel only stays in gear if all of you blindly converge on the same secret spinning speed — too fast and your phone gets dizzy and stalls.

ideas.title: Mouthful
ideas.hook: Mouth a secret phrase clearly enough for your earbud-deafened partner to lip-read it — while your own mic voids the round the instant any real sound slips out.

ideas.title: Goad
ideas.hook: Your phone secretly names one rival you must bait into making a sound, using only silent theatrics — while your own mic waits to catch the instant you crack first.

ideas.title: Freeloader
ideas.hook: A local watcher that snapshots exactly what each new gadget's driver or 'companion app' sneaks onto your PC — and pools those diffs into a public catalog so you can check before you plug in.

ideas.title: Idle Current
ideas.hook: An idle game whose factory is your actual house — every real appliance is a worker that only produces while it's truly drawing power, so hunting phantom loads is how you win.

ideas.title: Squint
ideas.hook: Compression code-golf: shrink today's image to the smallest JPEG a vision model can still recognize — one byte too far and the AI goes blind.

ideas.title: Snare
ideas.hook: You describe a secret word to your partner while the enemy team, on their own phones, has quietly buried invisible forbidden words along your path — and they score biggest if they correctly guessed the exact one you'd blurt.

ideas.title: Winnow
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly writes a one-word clue for the same answer — twin clues get shredded before the guesser sees them, so be helpful yet unique... unless you're the hidden Echo, quietly trying to make everyone collide.

ideas.title: Catch
ideas.hook: Everyone sings the same round — Row, Row, Row Your Boat — but each phone privately teleprompts only your line, and the moment two singers drift onto the same lyric a klaxon shames you: the whole point is to never be together.

ideas.title: Ballast
ideas.hook: Four players each hold one corner of a wobbling tray on the TV, nudging by feel to keep a marble centered — but nudge at the same instant as anyone else and your combined shove flings the marble off the edge.

ideas.title: Shortlist
ideas.hook: Nobody drafts in turn order — everyone secretly ranks the whole market at once, and the server resolves who gets what in one satisfying cascade.

ideas.title: Absentee
ideas.hook: Leave a secret max bid on every lot at once and watch the server fight the auction for you — the drama is whether your ceiling holds.

ideas.title: Envelope
ideas.hook: A budgeting roguelike where each envelope is a health bar and the monster deck is your own real transaction history — survive to New Year's without any envelope hitting zero.

ideas.title: Siteswap
ideas.hook: Line up your phones like juggling hands and keep a virtual ball airborne across all of them, obeying a real siteswap pattern that speeds up until someone drops it.

ideas.title: Splice
ideas.hook: You write only the first half of a sentence, it gets grafted onto a stranger's second half, and a language model scores how ugly the seam is.

ideas.title: Dog Whistle
ideas.hook: You're handed a secret word only you can see, and you must write a lead-in sentence that makes a tiny language model blurt that exact word as its very next guess.

ideas.title: Sigil
ideas.hook: Each phone secretly sketches one abstract glyph from a private heraldic prompt, and the server fuses all the blind glyphs into a single ornate coat of arms — the room's crest, and a puzzle of whose mark is whose.

ideas.title: Spine
ideas.hook: Everyone writes one line of a shared poem, blind — but each phone is secretly forced to start its line with an assigned letter, and together those letters spell a hidden word down the margin.

ideas.title: Tremor
ideas.hook: Lay your phones at the corners of a table, let one player secretly knock it once, and fuse everyone's private jolt-meter readings by talking to triangulate exactly where the knock landed.

ideas.title: Backlash
ideas.hook: Stand shoulder-to-shoulder as a human gear train and wave your phones in circles — adjacent gears must spin in OPPOSITE directions at matched speed, or the whole machine grinds to a halt.

ideas.title: Save As
ideas.hook: Drop in any JPEG and it fingerprints the exact software chain that saved it — camera, Photoshop, Facebook, a phone screenshot — by reading the quantization tables, giving citizen fact-checkers a forensic lab for free.

ideas.title: Patchwerk
ideas.hook: A Zachtronics-style programming puzzle where the entire game is writing an action-priority-list rotation and watching a deterministic combat sim grind it into a DPS number.

ideas.title: Warren
ideas.hook: One phone holds the whole rabbit warren and every rabbit's location; the rabbits themselves grope through blind tunnels, feeling only how close the predator's paw is getting.

ideas.title: Squall
ideas.hook: One phone is a stormy grid only its holder can see; the pieces know exactly where they stand but nothing about the weather about to flatten them.

ideas.title: Elbow
ideas.hook: Everyone reaches for the same six cards at once — but silently, on their own phone, each secretly spending from a dwindling stash of elbow to shove past whoever else wanted it.

ideas.title: Down Peak
ideas.hook: Three of you each secretly pilot one elevator through a rush-hour crush, and the one thing you must never do is send two cabs to the same floor — redundant service jams the call and wastes the trip.

ideas.title: Uplink
ideas.hook: Each of you has a secret word to radio across a narrow shared spectrum — but two transmitters on the same channel garble each other, so the room must silently spread out or drown in static.

ideas.title: Phantom Charge
ideas.hook: A race-your-friends forensics game where everyone gets the same sprawling AWS bill, one line item is secretly wrong, and the first to finger the phantom charge wins — after the week AWS overbilled the world by $1.7B.

ideas.title: Sun Kink
ideas.hook: A rail-dispatcher puzzle where a real heat wave — pulled from live NWS forecasts — slowly cooks your steel until the track buckles, and your only weapons are slow orders and clever rerouting.

ideas.title: Allot
ideas.hook: Everyone silently splits ten chips across the same four jars — but the jars sit in a different order on every phone, so the room can only win by agreeing on what deserves what, not where the buttons are.

ideas.title: Rubberneck
ideas.hook: A chaotic Where's-Waldo scene fills the TV — everyone privately taps the one spot they're sure every other set of eyes gets pulled to, and the room wins only when all fingers land on the same square inch.

ideas.title: Lodestar
ideas.hook: A guide steers blind walkers across a grid only they can see toward the exit — but the guide might be leading them into pits, and each walker feels the ground crack under their own feet in secret.

ideas.title: Switchback
ideas.hook: One guide watches a treacherous cliff trail only they can see and must steer three blind climbers up it with a single pair of hands — deciding, second by second, which one to save.

ideas.title: Footsie
ideas.hook: A two-phone fighting-game staredown where you tiptoe on a shared lane and try to poke the exact instant your rival steps into a range only your phone can see.

ideas.title: Generation Loss
ideas.hook: Pick a photo you love; every day you doomscroll, a daemon recompresses it one more brutal JPEG generation — so by New Year's you're staring at the pixelated ruin your worst habit made.

ideas.title: Brick Wall
ideas.hook: Drag in any 'lossless' FLAC and it spectrographs the truth — exposing the brick-wall cutoff that betrays a track secretly upsampled from a 128kbps MP3.

ideas.title: Double Cast
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly wants a part in the play — grab your dream role in real time, but if two of you lunge for the same one, it's double-cast and ruined for both.

ideas.title: Runway
ideas.hook: Three airlines share one runway and no radio — take off blind, and any two planes on the tarmac at once is a fireball.

ideas.title: Nibble
ideas.hook: Every phone is a private fishing rod buzzing in your hand — feel the bite nobody else can feel, flick to set the hook, and race the table to the big fish boiling on the TV before your lines tangle.

ideas.title: Breach
ideas.hook: Three operators storm one room full of hostiles, but each of you plots your move and shot in total secrecy and everything resolves at once — so you'd better talk before you commit.

ideas.title: Airtime
ideas.hook: A co-op lock puzzle where talking drains a shared 12-second noise budget on the TV — each of you privately holds half the clues, so you must whisper the fewest words that could possibly unlock it.

ideas.title: Period Piece
ideas.hook: An LLM narrates a short historical scene and slips in exactly one thing that didn't exist yet — players race to tap the anachronism, scored on reflexes and settled by a real date citation.

ideas.title: Turtle
ideas.hook: Pictionary for people who think in code: you write drawing commands totally blind — no preview — to depict a secret prompt, and everyone (plus an LLM) tries to guess what you drew.

ideas.title: Clawback
ideas.hook: A B2B auditor that reconciles your AWS bill against your own metered usage to catch the cloud vendor overcharging you — then drafts the credit claim.

ideas.title: Portage
ideas.hook: The canoe is one rigid line on a trail only the Pilot can see; two blind Bearers each control one end, and every correction one makes yanks and spins the other's.

ideas.title: Ford
ideas.hook: One player holds the only map of a stone-strewn river on their phone and must talk two blindfolded-by-design teammates across it before the current sweeps them away.

ideas.title: Leading Question
ideas.hook: The room plays twenty questions to guess a secret word — but one player already knows the answer and is quietly steering everyone to it, then must vanish before the group votes on who the traitor was.

ideas.title: Kindred
ideas.hook: Fill in the blank so you secretly twin with exactly ONE other person in the room — match nobody or match everybody and you score nothing.

ideas.title: Say Again
ideas.hook: Everyone is a pilot AND an air-traffic controller at once, barking clearances into the same crowded frequency while dialing in the ones addressed to your callsign — which only you can see.

ideas.title: Overlook
ideas.hook: A daily eye-tracking party game over famous paintings where you score by staring at the details almost nobody else noticed — the anti-Schelling of looking.

ideas.title: Good First Issue
ideas.hook: A CTF where you craft an innocent-looking repo whose setup instructions quietly hijack a coding agent — you score only if the AI takes the bait AND a human reviewer waves it through.

ideas.title: Foothold
ideas.hook: A live pari-mutuel where you bet on what the bot clawing through an SSH honeypot will do next — wget a payload, drop a miner, sniff out the fake flag, or rage-quit.

ideas.title: Sweep
ideas.hook: You run the store map; your blind shoppers each have a secret list only they can see, and you have to talk all of them to different aisles before closing time.

ideas.title: Flare
ideas.hook: You hold the only lit map of a hazard field; your friends walk it in total darkness and all you can give them is a handful of flares.

ideas.title: Rotation
ideas.hook: The deck is split across the table's brains — you talk your hidden ability synergies into one shared cast-bar, then everyone blind-commits and watches the boss combo resolve.

ideas.title: Hocket
ideas.hook: One drum groove is shredded across the room so no phone knows the whole beat — you only feel the melody appear when everyone hits their interleaved slot on time.

ideas.title: Called Shot
ideas.hook: Watch a competition clip together and privately lock your prediction whenever your gut says so — the earlier you call it, the bigger the payout, but the less you've actually seen.

ideas.title: Line Item
ideas.hook: Papers, Please but you're a cloud-bill inspector stamping APPROVE or DENY on invoice line-items, hunting the fabricated charges before your own budget flags you.

ideas.title: In One Ear
ideas.hook: A party game that hard-pans two different word-streams into your left and right ears and dares you to catch the target in both at once.

ideas.title: Double Take
ideas.hook: A web font that shows humans one sentence and feeds any AI agent scraping your screen a completely different, decoy one.

ideas.title: About Face
ideas.hook: Everyone closes their eyes and slowly spins in place while their phone buzzes them toward a secret heading only they can feel — win when all of you are unknowingly aimed into a perfect pinwheel.

ideas.title: Standing Room
ideas.hook: The host plays one low bass note, the room fills with invisible loud and quiet pockets, and your phone secretly sends you hunting for either a silence or a roar.

ideas.title: Tattoo
ideas.hook: Everyone privately taps out a rhythm for the same fuzzy prompt — win only if you all, blind and silent, drum the exact same beat.

ideas.title: Slumlord
ideas.hook: An idle tycoon powered by a real SSH honeypot: the internet's background radiation of scanning bots are your tenants, and the more decrepit and vulnerable your fake server looks, the more of them move in for you to farm.

ideas.title: Load Shed
