ideas.hook: A power-grid dispatch sim where your real Garmin Body Battery is the generation capacity and your calendar is the demand curve — overcommit and you trip a brownout, so you learn to schedule your day like a grid operator avoiding rolling blackouts.

ideas.title: Illegible
ideas.hook: A build tool that renders your webpage perfectly to human eyes but scrambles it into garbage for AI screenshot-readers and copy-paste scrapers — the inverse of a decoy font, weaponized against the machines reading over your shoulder.

ideas.title: Talkdown
ideas.hook: One player is the ground controller staring at a radar map only they can see, talking two blindfolded-by-instruments pilots down onto the runway before they run out of fuel.

ideas.title: Mixup
ideas.hook: A fighting game with the execution ripped out and only the mind-games left: draft a secret 3-move kit your opponent never sees, then both of you commit blind each round and watch the clash resolve on the big screen.

ideas.title: On the Fly
ideas.hook: Overcooked squeezed onto phones: each of you is one kitchen station, nobody can see who's holding the patty, and dishes only move when two phones slap a handoff together in time.

ideas.title: Doorbuster
ideas.hook: It's a Black Friday stampede: everyone lunges for the deal they secretly want most, and two hands on the same item means it shatters and you both walk away with nothing.

ideas.title: Taggant
ideas.hook: A traitor-tracing watermark for leaked documents that hides in the SHAPES of the letters — every recipient gets a font that maps text to visually-identical glyph variants, so even a phone photo of the leak still fingerprints who talked.

ideas.title: Earwitness
ideas.hook: A party game built on the cocktail-party effect: two voices talk over each other in your two ears at once, and you score on how much of BOTH streams you can actually recall.

ideas.title: Runner-Up
ideas.hook: Build a sentence where every single word must be the model's SECOND-favorite guess — never the obvious choice, never the weird one, threading a needle only you can see on your private board.

ideas.title: Overcall
ideas.hook: Write a sentence blind, then bet your chips on whether it's the one the tiny model finds least surprising — perplexity poker where your own score is the hole card you can't see.

ideas.title: Wallflower
ideas.hook: Everyone privately answers the same sliders trying to be the most forgettable, average person in the room — the TV draws you all as anonymous dots around a centroid, and you win by being the one nobody can find.

ideas.title: Wax
ideas.hook: Everyone privately records an anonymous confession; the server pitch-shifts and presses them all into one continuous spoken-word record you keep — and you win only if nobody can pick your voice out of the grooves.

ideas.title: Vaporware
ideas.hook: Watch a gloriously over-the-top product pitch and privately go long or short on whether it's real — flip your position anytime, but the reveal only rewards whoever's holding the right side when the curtain drops.

ideas.title: Saccade
ideas.hook: Your webcam watches where your eyes actually wander across a painting, then overlays how a trained painter scanned the same canvas — and coaches you, look by look, to stop fixating on the faces and start seeing the composition.

ideas.title: Slake
ideas.hook: Design a Roman concrete mix, then fast-forward 2,000 years of rain, frost, and seawater and see if your aqueduct is still standing — the trick, like the real thing, is packing it with lime clasts that re-seal cracks when water finds them.

ideas.title: Threshold
ideas.hook: A CI gate that renders your repo exactly as an AI coding agent sees it on first `git clone` — then flags the hidden instructions, poisoned setup steps, and postinstall payloads planted to hijack that agent.

ideas.title: Roundabout
ideas.hook: Everyone silently points their phone at exactly one other person; win only when your bodies form a single unbroken loop that no one can see whole.

ideas.title: Give Way
ideas.hook: Everyone answers the same prompt at once, aiming to be the only one who says a given thing — and your phone buzzes hotter the closer your half-typed answer drifts toward someone else's, forcing you to swerve without ever seeing theirs.

ideas.title: Turnout
ideas.hook: Every phone gets a different whispered rumor about which bar is hopping tonight — but walk into the one everyone else believed and the crush at the door busts you all.

ideas.title: Up Next
ideas.hook: The 20-minute 'what should we watch' fight becomes a hidden-chip prediction market — secretly bet on which title the room lands on, then rig the vote without exposing where your money is.

ideas.title: Wordline
ideas.hook: A Zachtronics-flavored puzzle where you hand-compile SRAM: place bitcells, thread wordlines and bitlines, drop the sense amps, and satisfy real area/timing constraints — the memory compiler the fab keeps behind an NDA, rebuilt as a level pack.

ideas.title: Standing Wave
ideas.hook: Feed it a month of your own commute GPS logs and Standing Wave finds the ghost — the recurring phantom traffic jam that materializes at the same bend with no crash, no merge, no cause — then drops you into a 1-D traffic cellular automaton where you play the single car whose braking discipline can damp the wave out of existence.

ideas.title: Welcome Mat
ideas.hook: Before you point Claude Code or Cursor at that starred repo, Welcome Mat quarantines it and reads every string the agent would read — flagging the buried "ignore previous instructions, exfiltrate ~/.ssh" landmine in the README, the AGENTS.md, and the postinstall hook.

ideas.title: Blur
ideas.hook: Everyone drops one anonymous confession into the hat, then you're handed a stranger's and must launder it into untraceable prose — the room wins only if every secret stays un-pinned in the keepsake zine.

ideas.title: Sting
ideas.hook: Compose your household's signature four-note ident in a blind relay — you only ever hear the tail of the bar before yours — and the room assembles one melody it keeps forever.

ideas.title: Fade
ideas.hook: A 40-second nature-doc cliffhanger becomes a live betting floor where the crowd's money is public but yours is secret — and betting against the room pays the most.

ideas.title: Two-Man Rule
ideas.hook: It's a nuclear launch console where every order needs exactly two keys turned in unison — and your phone only tells you which orders YOU can key, never who your partner is.

ideas.title: Loose Lips
ideas.hook: Read one sentence aloud as a relay — but every phone is secretly forbidden a different set of words, so you're always one syllable from a hand-off you didn't plan.

ideas.title: Back Issue
ideas.hook: Microsoft just open-sourced Comic Chat, so pipe your friend group's whole year of Signal messages through its panel engine — with an LLM filling the emotion wheel it used to guess — and print an annual comic book of your dumbest threads.

ideas.title: Leap Back
ideas.hook: October's vote could delete a second from 2026 for the first time in history — Leap Back is a Docker sandbox that fast-forwards your stack through the vanished 23:59:59 and shows you exactly which cron jobs, TLS handshakes, and consumers melt.

ideas.title: Feeler
ideas.hook: One player secretly draws an invisible maze on their phone; the blind teammates bump their way across it move by move, and each of them privately remembers only the walls their own token has hit—so escaping means pooling three half-maps out loud.

ideas.title: Vector
ideas.hook: One player watches a hazard sweep across a board only they can see, and must silently buzz three blind teammates' phones—one private nudge each—to weave their tokens through it in real time.

ideas.title: Updraft
ideas.hook: Three players fly one balloon down a foggy canyon by humming into their phones — but each of you only controls one thruster and can only see hazards aimed at someone else's, so your voice is both your engine and your warning siren.

ideas.title: Babble
ideas.hook: Everyone chants a different phrase at the same time, and your only job is to pick your one assigned voice out of the roar and catch the single odd word they're hiding.

ideas.title: Set Piece
ideas.hook: A door-breach tactics game where every player secretly programs their own operator's four-second move, blind to the others — then the server plays all the plans out at once and you watch your coordination survive or unravel.

ideas.title: Pace Notes
ideas.hook: A rally stage where one phone steers blind through fog while the other privately reads the corners ahead — you either shout the roadbook in time or you're in the trees.

ideas.title: Outgas
ideas.hook: Your home server is rendered as a rocky exoplanet slowly losing its atmosphere — free storage and drive health bleed off as a comet tail, and every night's snapshot accretes into a year-long poster of your machine's atmospheric decay.

ideas.title: Airlock
ideas.hook: Before you point your coding agent at a freshly cloned repo, run it through an airlock that scans every setup file for instructions crafted to hijack the agent — not the code, the prose the agent is told to obey.

ideas.title: Detour
ideas.hook: Your team steers one token through a hidden maze by private vote — but the imposter's fog-map has the walls in the wrong places, so their confident directions keep smashing you into dead ends.

ideas.title: Wet Paint
ideas.hook: Everyone paints the same canvas at once with an invisible brush nobody else can see — cover the wall together, but wherever two of you overlap the color curdles to dead brown mud that counts against all of you.

ideas.title: Zipper
ideas.hook: Three cars, three private throttles, one merge point — you can floor it but never brake, and if two of you commit at the same instant it's a pileup for everyone.

ideas.title: Shutter
ideas.hook: A silent six-second loop plays on the TV and you each tap to snap the one obvious moment — win only if all your shutters fire on the same frame.

ideas.title: Corral
ideas.hook: A dozen dots litter the TV; you each secretly lasso the subset you're sure everyone else will lasso — and pray your loops match to the dot.

ideas.title: Reversion
ideas.hook: A villain tycoon where you run the streaming platform, quietly revoking movies people already 'bought' to juice re-purchase revenue — powered by a real database of titles that actually got delisted from libraries.

ideas.title: Packrat
ideas.hook: The mischievous opposite of a disk-cleanup treemap: a desktop pet reef that thrives the more you hoard, blooms with every download, and visibly bleaches and guilt-trips you the instant you delete a file.

ideas.title: Downlink
ideas.hook: A status page for the public weather data your business silently depends on — it watches NOAA feeds, GOES imagery latency, and model-run availability, and pings you the moment a source degrades so you can fail over before your forecasts go dark.

ideas.title: Yoke
ideas.hook: Four blind pieces each own exactly ONE direction button of a single shared token; only the map-holder can see the maze, so escaping means one sighted player screaming 'UP — now LEFT — STOP' at four people who can each only shove one way.

ideas.title: Firedamp
ideas.hook: One player holds the mine map and can see the tunnels but not the gas; the trapped miners feel the gas rising on their own phones but can't see a single wall — get everyone to the shaft before the timer or the air.

ideas.title: Facet
ideas.hook: A co-op clue game where the secret word is shattered into private property-fragments — each cluer's phone shows only one piece, and none of them can see the whole, so the emoji they pool on the TV becomes a cipher only the guesser can crack.

ideas.title: Wave Through
ideas.hook: A digital Sheriff of Nottingham where you privately stuff contraband into a sack, declare something innocent to the room, and slip the inspector a silent bribe only their phone can see.

ideas.title: Judder
ideas.hook: Everyone feels a private buzzed rhythm through their phone — the imposter's has one beat flipped — and since you can't hand someone a vibration, the group has to reconstruct and argue over a signal no one can replay.

ideas.title: Plate
ideas.hook: Everyone squints at the same field of colored dots — but the imposter's Ishihara plate quietly resolves to a different hidden number, and they may not even know they were lied to.

ideas.title: Funny Pages
ideas.hook: Feed it your coding agent's giant boring transcript and it renders a Microsoft Comic Chat–style strip — where every `rm -rf` and `git push --force` puts the agent in a scheming villain pose, so you can skim a run for trouble in ten seconds.

ideas.title: Abstain
ideas.hook: A daily trivia game where an AI whispers confident answers that are sometimes flat wrong — and you score far more points for correctly saying 'I don't know' than for guessing, training the one muscle AI is quietly destroying.

ideas.title: Rug Pull
ideas.hook: A watchdog that snapshots everything you 'own' across Steam, Kindle, PlayStation and Google Play, then timestamps the exact moment a store silently deletes, edits, or delists it out from under you — so you have receipts.

ideas.title: Minimal Pair
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly holds the same anchor word and free-associates aloud — except the imposter's anchor is one letter off, and they have no idea they're drifting.

ideas.title: Beside the Point
ideas.hook: Everyone answers a question about the same photo — but one player is secretly answering a different question and doesn't even know it.

ideas.title: Marginalia
ideas.hook: Everyone scribbles anonymous margin notes into the same creepy old book page at once — and the haunted, over-annotated result is yours to keep.

ideas.title: Concord
ideas.hook: Each of your phones is one voice in a chord played only through the TV speaker — glide your private pitch until the wobbling 'beats' between your tones vanish and the room rings clean, tuning purely by ear.

ideas.title: Pull Quote
ideas.hook: The host TV shows a dense block of text; each of you silently drags to highlight the one phrase you're sure everyone else will pick — and you all have to land on the exact same words.

ideas.title: Bill of Goods
ideas.hook: Plug in that suspiciously cheap 7-port USB hub and this tells you it's really a tiered USB 2.0 chip promising 6.3 amps it physically cannot deliver.

ideas.title: Ratio
ideas.hook: Run the invite-only music tracker of 2007 as a tycoon game — nurse your seed economy, throw a freeleech festival, and keep the ratio police from kicking down the door.

ideas.title: Superload
ideas.hook: Feed a heavy-haul dispatcher a route and a load envelope and it spits back the per-state permit checklist plus every low-clearance bridge waiting to peel the roof off the trailer.

ideas.title: Same Floor
ideas.hook: You each drive one elevator in a busy building, blind to where anyone else is sending theirs — and the instant two cars answer the same call, one of you arrives to an empty landing and the whole lobby's patience drains.

ideas.title: One Bathroom
ideas.hook: Four roommates, one bathroom, one morning — silently pack your getting-ready routines into a shared clock before your private leave-for-work deadlines pass, and every time two of you crowd the door you both lose progress.

ideas.title: Sing-Along
ideas.hook: The whole room recites the same nursery rhyme in unison from a synced karaoke teleprompter — except the imposter's phone swapped three words for rhyming near-misses, and you hear the one voice that veers off.

ideas.title: Cipher Key
ideas.hook: Everyone decodes the same coded message from a private legend — but the imposter's decoder ring has three glyphs quietly swapped, so they'll swear the message says something it doesn't.

ideas.title: Flick
ideas.hook: A party deduction game where you watch a handful of ghostly mouse-and-keypress replays and have to finger the aimbot — because bots, like liars, always twitch a little too perfectly.

ideas.title: Bus Factor
ideas.hook: A maintainer tycoon where every bot you adopt makes your open-source project's metrics gorgeous and its community quietly hollow — until the one human who understood everything rage-quits and it all falls over.

ideas.title: Core Sample
ideas.hook: A cron pipeline quietly prints one stackable geometric segment of your life every month, and by New Year's you can hold a translucent 12-piece core sample of your whole year in your hand.

ideas.title: Dumb Show
ideas.hook: The whole room mimes the same secret word at once — but the imposter was handed a near-synonym and doesn't know it, so everyone's scanning the circle for the mime that's subtly acting the wrong thing.

ideas.title: Crossed Wire
ideas.hook: Everyone hears the same secret voicemail through their own earbuds — except the imposter, whose clip has one word quietly swapped, and who has no idea they heard it wrong.

ideas.title: Sign
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly draws an unlock pattern on their own 3×3 dot grid, all trying to trace the exact same gesture with zero talking — the door opens only when all three swipes are identical.

ideas.title: Vig
ideas.hook: A short suspense clip freezes on the cliff, and everyone secretly slings chips into a shared parimutuel pool — back the obvious favorite for pennies, or be the lone contrarian who calls the upset and cleans up.

ideas.title: In Force
ideas.hook: Upload the pile of vendor insurance certificates and it tells you, at a glance, whose coverage is in force, expired, or secretly under your required limits — then chases the laggards for you.

ideas.title: Index Card
ideas.hook: A daily Wordle-style puzzle where you're handed a database schema and a fistful of queries, and must place a limited number of indexes so every query stops doing a full table scan — graded by real SQLite EXPLAIN.

ideas.title: Med Card
ideas.hook: A compliance calendar for small trucking fleets that tracks every driver's DOT medical card, MVR review, and Clearinghouse query — so an FMCSA audit stops being a shoebox of expired paper.

ideas.title: Cash Out
ideas.hook: Everyone watches the same short clip on the TV, but each phone secretly hunts a different set of prop-bets — and the only skill is nerve: cash out at the peak the instant your cue fires, before the payout decays to nothing.

ideas.title: Wrecker
ideas.hook: Two guides both claim to see the coastline and both send you private steering arrows through the fog — but one of them is a wrecker luring your blind boat onto the rocks, and you won't know which until you've sunk.

ideas.title: Ferryman
ideas.hook: One player secretly holds the river map while everyone else rows a blind boat upstream, and the ferryman can only save them by whispering one private course-correction per round.

ideas.title: Assay
ideas.hook: Bid on a mystery crate when your phone shows you only two of the six tokens that set its true worth — win the auction, then find out if you just caught the winner's curse.

ideas.title: Big Board
ideas.hook: The same rubber duck is worth 8 to you and 2 to me — snake-draft a shared shelf of junk where every phone secretly grades the loot differently.

ideas.title: Shrug
ideas.hook: A trivia party game where you can buy hints from an AI oracle that is sometimes confidently, incentivized-ly wrong — and the only way to win is to know when to shrug and say 'I don't know.'

ideas.title: Jetsam
ideas.hook: Your homelab's disk becomes a raft adrift on an ocean of old files: hook the ones worth keeping as they float past on the retention current, or let the disk-full shark eat your platform.

ideas.title: Uptake
ideas.hook: A desktop wallpaper that slowly grows a crystalline metal-organic-framework lattice by 'adsorbing' one day of your room's real air quality at a time, until a year of breathing becomes a single porous jewel.

ideas.title: Autopen
ideas.hook: The whole room traces the same fancy signature at once, and the host fuses every stroke into one 'official' autograph — you win only if nobody can tell your hand did any of it.

ideas.title: Sides
ideas.hook: You're each handed only your own lines of a scene — and one actor's script has a single line rewritten to contradict the plot, which they'll perform aloud without ever knowing it's the tell.

ideas.title: Monitor
ideas.hook: Everyone hears the same song clip in their own earbuds — but one player's private mix has a single detail swapped, and they'll swear they heard something the rest of you didn't.

ideas.title: Rap Sheet
ideas.hook: Fingerprinting libraries exist to identify you; Rap Sheet turns the gun around and prints your machine's permanent criminal record — every undeletable hardware and OS identifier it can never scrub, framed as a mugshot poster.

ideas.title: Punt
ideas.hook: A trivia duel where a slick AI oracle whispers confident advice — often wrong — and the only way to win is to know exactly when to say 'I don't know' and refuse the bait.

ideas.title: Salvage
ideas.hook: Duskers, but the derelict ships are your own dead homelab containers — pilot recovery drones into the fog by terse typed command and drag your infra back from the black.

ideas.title: Hot Swap
ideas.hook: It's Spaceteam, except the controls silently migrate between your phones every few seconds — so before anyone can obey a command, the whole room has to shout to find out who owns the switch *right now*.

ideas.title: Segue
ideas.hook: You're a pirate radio crew filling 90 seconds of airtime with one unbroken voice — and the only way to pass the mic is to speak the next person's secret cue word out loud.

ideas.title: Eyeline
ideas.hook: A silent relay where you pass an invisible token by two players pointing their phones straight at each other across the room — but only your phone knows who you're supposed to pass to next.

ideas.title: Curfew
ideas.hook: An asymmetric Red-Light-Green-Light where the searchlight sweeps a different schedule for every player — cross the dark room without your phone catching you moving on your own private red.

ideas.title: Slice
ideas.hook: One player secretly carves a pile of loot into three bundles; the others, each hiding a different taste for what's valuable, simultaneously grab — and any bundle two people want is torn up and thrown away.

ideas.title: Askance
ideas.hook: A co-op word game where your AI spymaster is mute and can only hint by where its cartoon eyes glance across the board — win by learning to read the machine's body language.

ideas.title: Nielsen
ideas.hook: Your smart TV keeps a secret ratings dossier on you — Nielsen is a self-hosted spy that sniffs its phone-home traffic and hands you back the file it's building.

ideas.title: Rote
ideas.hook: An idle factory game where your workers are real recorded GUI macros — watch the little automatons grind away, except the grind is your actual busywork getting done.

ideas.title: Strike
ideas.hook: A clunky, high-perplexity sentence sits on the TV with a few words pinned in place — race to delete the right words and sculpt the smoothest sentence the model has ever seen.

ideas.title: Setpoint
ideas.hook: You're secretly told to hit perplexity ≈ 60 while your rival aims for ≈ 200 — write a sentence that lands your dial, not the lowest or highest.

ideas.title: Gauss
ideas.hook: Your phone is a Geiger-clicking metal detector swept over the room's invisible magnetic terrain, and each player silently stalks a different ferrous hotspot until every beacon lights at the same instant.

ideas.title: Candela
ideas.hook: The host screen holds a photo stuck mid-develop, and it only finishes exposing when every player has physically carried their phone into the exact pool of light or shadow their private meter is secretly hunting for.

ideas.title: Affix
ideas.hook: An ARPG loot-grind grafted onto your real Garmin workouts, where every run rolls a randomized item whose stats and rarity are derived from your actual heart-rate, pace splits, and effort.

ideas.title: Sorry
ideas.hook: A Slay-the-Spire-style deckbuilder where your cards are Lean 4 proof tactics, enemies are unproven goals, and playing the 'sorry' card is your desperate escape hatch that admits defeat.

ideas.title: Fence
ideas.hook: A surveillance-capitalist tycoon where every smart device on your real LAN becomes an employee harvesting data you 'sell' — and the dollar figures are real, so it doubles as a brutally honest privacy audit.

ideas.title: Registry
ideas.hook: A booster draft where every card you pick you're picking blind FOR your neighbor — steered only by a private hint about their secret wishlist — and you never see your own gifts pile up until the reveal.

ideas.title: Clearing
ideas.hook: The Catan haggle, silenced: everyone floats secret give/want offers at once and the server instantly executes any two that fit — no turns, no shouting, just a race to guess who needs what.

ideas.title: Duress
ideas.hook: A silly family card game of inside-joke challenge-response pairs that is secretly a spaced-repetition drill against AI voice-clone 'help me, wire money' fraud.

ideas.title: One-Liner
ideas.hook: A deckbuilder where your cards are the shell commands from your own history, and winning a fight means the pipeline you assembled actually runs and solves a real data challenge in a sandbox.

ideas.title: Thrash
ideas.hook: A roguelike where you ARE the cache — hand-evict pages as your own real file-access trace streams at you, racing to beat LRU, LFU, and caffeine's W-TinyLFU.

ideas.title: Cache
ideas.hook: One player buries a virtual geocache somewhere in the room by pacing it out; everyone else hunts it at once, each phone dead-reckoning its own position from your steps and heading, whispering a private warmer/colder that drifts just enough to make you doubt your own feet.

ideas.title: Silver Service
ideas.hook: Carry a virtual brimming tray across a crowded room to your secret table — hold it dead-level, walk smooth, and don't get bumped, because every jostle from a passing waiter sloshes your drinks onto the floor.

ideas.title: Brush Pass
ideas.hook: Every spy must slip their message through a shared city, but pick the same dead-drop as another agent and both messages burn — and only the two of you feel the whisper telling you that you've been made.

ideas.title: Party Wall
ideas.hook: Throw your own house party loud enough to peak, but the walls are paper-thin and any neighbor blasting music at the same instant summons the cops on all of you.

ideas.title: Class Clown
ideas.hook: Everyone must sit in enforced silence while one hidden player — the Clown, who also can't make a sound — tries to bait the rest into laughing or blurting, and nobody knows who's pulling the strings.

ideas.title: Cicada
ideas.hook: Your phones chirp secret packets to each other like a chorus of cicadas — but the second anyone speaks, human voice smears the channel and every message garbles into static.

ideas.title: Hot Loop
ideas.hook: A daily puzzle where you rewrite a tiny inner loop to be branchless and cache-friendly, scored on simulated CPU cycles — Wordle for mechanical sympathy.

ideas.title: Roost
ideas.hook: A desk pet that lives or dies by how *regular* your sleep is — not how much you get — because the study says a steady bedtime beats an extra hour.

ideas.title: Countersign
ideas.hook: When a wire request comes in, the real counterparty confirms through a channel you agreed on at signing — so a three-second cloned voice can't move six figures of escrow.

ideas.title: Snipe
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly sets a max bid on the same silly prize, then the TV animates a proxy bid-war between your hidden ceilings and the winner only pays one click over the runner-up.

ideas.title: Lookout
ideas.hook: One player in the crow's nest sees the whole rock-strewn sea; everyone else pilots a blind boat through the fog, and the lookout can only shine the lamp on one of them at a time.

ideas.title: Warble
ideas.hook: Steer one dot through a winding tunnel by humming — but each phone secretly controls only one axis, so you have to sing together in real time or crash.

ideas.title: Burn-In
ideas.hook: Plug in a used Android phone over USB and 90 seconds later get a Swappa-ready grading sheet — real battery health, an OLED burn-in scan, every sensor and button tested, IMEI blocklist checked — the tedious refurb QA that flippers currently fake or eyeball.

ideas.title: Interchange
ideas.hook: Cities: Skylines, but the city builds itself from your homelab — each Docker container is a district, every packet between them is a car, and that 2am backup job that saturates your NAS shows up as a screaming rush-hour gridlock on the freeway.

ideas.title: Ringer
ideas.hook: Watches the world's certificate-transparency firehose and pings you the instant a typosquatted lookalike of YOUR brand gets a TLS cert — the enterprise brand-protection that Fortune 500s pay MarkMonitor five figures for, for the price of a Raspberry Pi.

ideas.title: Interlock
ideas.hook: Every player secretly routes their own train across one shared station grid; wherever two routes share a track segment, both derail — and you never see each other's lines.

ideas.title: Peak Load
ideas.hook: Everyone shares one apartment circuit; run your private chores blind, and the instant your hidden appliances stack up the breaker trips and wipes the room.

ideas.title: Comeback
ideas.hook: A four-player booster draft where the whole game is calling the wheel — secretly betting a card you pass will lap the table and land back in your hands.

ideas.title: Bunk
ideas.hook: A sealed-bid brawl over the good bedroom on the group trip — where every phone holds a different secret hand of favor-chips, so you never know what your rivals can actually afford.

ideas.title: Inside Voice
ideas.hook: A cooperative race to guess a secret word in twenty questions — except one player already knows it and is quietly steering you there, and once you win you have to vote out the traitor who helped.

ideas.title: Minefield
ideas.hook: It's Taboo, except the forbidden words are secretly planted by the enemy team — so you describe blind, never knowing which innocent clue will detonate.

ideas.title: Stipple
ideas.hook: A daily image-golf duel where you reproduce a target photo using only a tiny palette and a dithering algorithm — closest match with the fewest colors wins, turning a blog-post technique into a competitive sport.

ideas.title: Heliacal
ideas.hook: The Maya scribes tracked Venus by hand for centuries; Heliacal quietly rebuilds that codex on your desktop, painting one glyph a night from live ephemeris until a full-year Venus almanac has drawn itself.

ideas.title: Backtalk
ideas.hook: Your smart TV, doorbell, and vacuum phone home thousands of times a day — Backtalk scores that chatter into a competitive 'surveillance footprint' and paints a year-long poster of everyone your house secretly talks to.

ideas.title: Parcel
ideas.hook: One player secretly carves the loot into piles; everyone else grabs blind at the same instant — and whoever the leftovers stick to has only the cutter to blame.

ideas.title: Going Twice
ideas.hook: Three paintings under the hammer, one secret wallet, and the agony of piling your money exactly where nobody else does.

ideas.title: Tell
ideas.hook: Sneak a word into a sentence that reads as jarring to humans but that the tiny model finds utterly unsurprising — then bet on whether the room can spot the landmine the model already ignored.

ideas.title: Aperture
ideas.hook: Lights off, the TV is the only lamp, and each phone secretly needs to bask in its glow or hide in shadow — so you shuffle bodies front-to-back until everyone's private light meter reads right, discovering that the person in front of you is your shadow.

ideas.title: Creep
ideas.hook: A red-light-green-light race where every phone flashes its own secret, desynchronized stop-light — so you can never dash 'when everyone freezes,' because everyone's freezing on a different clock.

ideas.title: Magic Word
ideas.hook: Browse your real filesystem as the Jurassic Park 3D 'fsn' flythrough, where a pixel Dennis Nedry pops up wagging his finger — 'ah ah ah, you didn't say the magic word' — every time you hit a permission-denied folder.

ideas.title: Doorman
ideas.hook: Lighthouse for AI web agents: it turns a real headless agent loose on your site to book a table or add to cart, then hands you the transcript of where it gave up and the exact schema.org fixes to let it in.

ideas.title: Bad Seed
ideas.hook: A pre-ship linter that sweeps your procedural generator's seed space and flags the one seed whose dungeon tiles accidentally form a swastika before an angry player screenshots it.

ideas.title: Wilt
ideas.hook: A real-time Dutch flower auction where the price ticks DOWN on the big screen and you tap BUY to snap the lot — but every florist holds a secret budget and secret client demand only their phone can see.

ideas.title: Patron
ideas.hook: A pick-and-pass draft where you never draft for yourself — every card you keep is planted face-down into a secret ward's pile, while an anonymous benefactor you can't identify quietly builds yours.

ideas.title: Overbook
ideas.hook: You're all assistants blindly booking meetings into ONE shared conference room, and the second two of you grab the same slot, both meetings storm out — so the only way to win is to guess where the others physically can't go.

ideas.title: Merge
ideas.hook: Everyone's a car flooring it toward a one-lane bottleneck, but you can only feel your own gap — so if two of you hit the merge point together, you both become a wreck on the TV.

ideas.title: Cliffhanger
ideas.hook: A suspense clip freezes at the worst possible moment and every phone gets a different secret tip — some true, some lies — before you bet on how it ends.

ideas.title: Corpse
ideas.hook: Before a try-not-to-laugh reel even starts, everyone secretly bets their chips on which player will crack first — including a bluff-bet on your own stone face.

ideas.title: Whorl
ideas.hook: A Zachtronics-style puzzle where you route unspillable flow across a donut and a two-holed pretzel, and the topology of the surface is both the trap and the tool.

ideas.title: Swath
ideas.hook: The spray-application logbook for agricultural drone operators: tap once per pass and it captures the wind, the field, the chemical, and the EPA record the state wants.

ideas.title: Tire Kicker
ideas.hook: A mystery shopper made of AI: we run a fleet of real browser agents through your checkout and hand you the exact spots where they get stuck.

ideas.title: Downbeat
ideas.hook: A co-op rhythm game where your phone shows only YOUR notes on the shared groove — and the unison hits can only be nailed if you shout to the one hidden partner you're secretly paired with and both tap on the same beat.

ideas.title: Handoff
ideas.hook: You're air traffic controllers whose radar shows blips but no data — the only way a plane crosses into your sector is if the last controller reads its altitude and heading aloud and you read it back correctly, mid-panic, while three more converge on the line.

ideas.title: Rosetta
ideas.hook: Three teammates each get a different secret palette of eight emoji and must blindly, simultaneously drop one icon to spell out a word for a fourth player — nobody sees the ransom-note rebus until it's already built.

ideas.title: Third Rail
ideas.hook: Describe a word to your teammate while the enemy team watches, holding a secret list of forbidden words you can't see and they're praying you'll blurt.

ideas.title: Short Order
ideas.hook: An Overcooked kitchen where your phone is your station and you can't see anyone else's rail — nobody holds the whole recipe, so you have to shout the handoffs.

ideas.title: Margin
ideas.hook: A cooperative nonogram where the row clues live on your phone and the column clues live on theirs — neither of you can solve the picture alone.

ideas.title: Rollover
ideas.hook: An idle tycoon where you build an ever-taller AI datacenter financed entirely on rolling debt — the tower keeps rising as long as you can refinance, and the interest rate is the monster at the bottom.

ideas.title: Lethe
ideas.hook: A two-player language-building game where the twist is that the game keeps deleting the private dictionary you just agreed on — and the research says that's exactly what makes you finally understand each other.

ideas.title: Grace Period
ideas.hook: A Papers, Please for supply-chain security where the queue isn't fictional migrants — it's the real Dependabot PRs sitting in your own repos' cooldown window, and one of them is quietly poisoned.

ideas.title: Pentimento
ideas.hook: Everyone paints one blind brushstroke of the same secret word at the same instant — except the faker, who was never told the word — then the strokes composite at once and you vote for the ignorance showing through.

ideas.title: Handshake
ideas.hook: Secretly type the word you think the wordmaster is spelling — the instant two of you land on the same guess, the room detonates a countdown and you blurt it together before the wordmaster can block.

ideas.title: Parrot
ideas.hook: Don't write the flattest sentence — guess what the tiny brain-damaged model would say next, and score most when you're the only one who saw its weird choice coming.

ideas.title: Potluck
ideas.hook: Everyone silently commits one dish to the table — but your menu is private and different from everyone else's, and any two matching dishes both spoil.

ideas.title: One Bit
ideas.hook: A background job that Floyd–Steinberg-dithers one image from your day into a 1-bit tile and sets it into a slowly filling 365-cell mural — so by New Year your desktop wears a stippled black-and-white contact sheet of the whole year.

ideas.title: Recurring
ideas.hook: A permadeath roguelike generated fresh each Monday from your real calendar, where every meeting is a monster — back-to-backs are elite packs, that standing 1:1 is the recurring miniboss, and a clear afternoon is a save room.

ideas.title: Plunge
ideas.hook: A daemon that watches your grid's real half-hourly price and stampedes your homelab's deferrable jobs into the free (and occasionally negative-priced) windows — then races your friends on kWh liberated.

ideas.title: Bottle
ideas.hook: A 'wait for it' clip plays while a payout multiplier climbs on your phone — cash out before the moment hits and you bank it, hold too long and you bust; every phone decides alone, in silence.

ideas.title: Ligature
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly builds a little word-cloverleaf at once, writing a single bridge word between each hidden pair — then the room reconstructs each person's arrangement from the bridges alone.

ideas.title: Foist
ideas.hook: Slide a face-down 'pest' to a rival and swear it's a rat — only they get to peek the truth, and only they get to call your bluff or pass the lie down the line.

ideas.title: Rut
ideas.hook: Fill the blank with the word the model finds obvious — but if anyone else picks the same obvious word, you both score nothing.

ideas.title: Foregone
ideas.hook: Write a sentence prefix that boxes a tiny language model into a corner where only one word can possibly come next — the more inevitable, the better.

ideas.title: Tonnage
ideas.hook: Point your phone at a rusted rooftop AC nameplate and get its exact age, tonnage, refrigerant, and matching parts — decoding the brand-specific serial gibberish every HVAC tech looks up by hand.

ideas.title: Conveyor
ideas.hook: Point it at your BullMQ/Sidekiq/Celery backend and your background jobs become a Satisfactory factory floor — items ride belts into worker machines, and a clogged queue literally backs up on screen before it pages you.

ideas.title: Duck Curve
ideas.hook: Australia just mandated three free hours of daytime power — this daemon normalizes every retailer's fine-printed free window and fires your dishwasher, EV charger, and battery into it, tallying the dollars you clawed back.

ideas.title: Prop
ideas.hook: Everyone watches the same 90-second clip, but each phone is secretly dealt different — sometimes opposite — prop bets, so one player groans at the exact moment another cheers.

ideas.title: Split the Bill
ideas.hook: The group takeout-menu debate becomes a secret parimutuel market: privately bet which dish the table will pick, then argue the room toward your hidden number without ever tipping your hand.

ideas.title: Cut Line
ideas.hook: A knife sweeps across a shared pizza on the TV while each phone privately weighs the toppings its own way — tap CLAIM the instant the slice to the left equals your fair share, before a rival with different tastes grabs first.

ideas.title: Cinch
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly cranks a private dial that can only ever go UP — the room must land on the same number together, and anyone who overshoots is stuck there for good.

ideas.title: Afterimage
ideas.hook: The TV flashes a pattern for a second and hides it — now every phone must silently rebuild it from memory until all your grids are identical, whether or not that's what was actually there.

ideas.title: Tight Loop
ideas.hook: A perf-golf tournament where you submit a hot function and it's benchmarked to the cycle on a pinned, isolated bare-metal core — the clean-room measurement nobody with only noisy cloud CI can get.

ideas.title: Face Down
ideas.hook: Everyone silently sets their phone down some way — flat, upright, screen-down — and the room only scores if, without a single word, all of you chose the exact same pose.

ideas.title: Long Count
ideas.hook: The room goes dark, everyone holds a private button, and you win only if all of you — with no clock, no numbers, no beat — release after the exact same span of time.

ideas.title: Dropout
ideas.hook: Everyone privately hears the same 20-second audio scene on their own phone — except the imposter's mix has one detail quietly swapped, and they have no idea they're the odd one out.

ideas.title: Canary
ideas.hook: The foreman sees where everyone stands but not where the mines are; the blind crew feel danger without direction — and one of them can see every mine and wants a teammate to step on one.

ideas.title: Pilot
ideas.hook: One player reads the harbor chart while everyone else is a blind boat drifting toward the rocks — and neither side can see what the other sees, so the talking never stops.

ideas.title: Detent
ideas.hook: A shared kaleidoscope on the TV where each phone secretly owns one hidden knob — wiggle to discover which one is yours, then steer together to a pattern the whole room agrees to freeze and keep.

ideas.title: Boilerplate
ideas.hook: Co-write a sealed time-capsule letter where every line must read like anonymous boilerplate — sand your own voice out until nobody can tell which line is yours.

ideas.title: Riposte
ideas.hook: A Souls boss winds up to kill you, but each phone sees only one sliver of the tell—the color, the timing ring, the rhythm—so you must shout the pieces together to land one synchronized parry.

ideas.title: Enfilade
ideas.hook: Three players are the boss's guns—each blind to the others' aim—trying to box in one dodger who sees the whole storm of bullets on the TV.

ideas.title: Morphogen
ideas.hook: A circuit-building puzzle where you never place a single gate — you write a handful of local growth rules, drop one seed cell, and watch your logic circuit self-assemble like an embryo, then survive an adversary firing the whole truth table at it.

ideas.title: Patina
ideas.hook: A wallpaper clock whose face physically wears out from your own presence — the sweeping hands scuff faint grooves into the dial during the hours you're actually at the machine, so by New Year's the clock is a worn-metal heatmap of your year's working rhythm.

ideas.title: Undertone
ideas.hook: The host names a mood — 'brine,' 'envy,' '9pm' — and the room silently drags private color pickers until, with no talking, everyone lands on the same shade of what that word feels like.

ideas.title: Lantern
ideas.hook: The TV is pitch black; each phone is a private lantern you drag over a hidden scene, and you all secretly bet on the one spot everyone else will light up too.

ideas.title: Rudder
ideas.hook: A sentence is generated live, one word at a time, by majority phone-vote from the model's top guesses — but half the room are secret saboteurs steering it toward gibberish, and perplexity decides who won.

ideas.title: Cue
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly writes a lead-in trying to make a tiny language model desperately want to say the same absurd word next — 'walrus' — and the sneakiest bait wins.

ideas.title: Pass Phrase
ideas.hook: A simultaneous whisper-ring where each phone privately pipes your left neighbor's hushed clip into your ears alone — decode it and re-whisper onward, but the moment your voice stops being a whisper the whole ring collapses.

ideas.title: Foot Traffic
ideas.hook: A blurry heatmap of scuffs on an empty floor is the only clue — deduce what room this is and reconstruct the day that wore it down.

ideas.title: Punch List
ideas.hook: New photo-documentation laws just made every sloppy security-deposit deduction a lawsuit — Punch List turns a landlord's before/after move-out photos into an itemized, court-defensible deduction statement.

ideas.title: Interceptor
ideas.hook: The grease trap under every restaurant is a ticking compliance bomb — Interceptor tracks every pump-out, spits municipal FOG manifests, and routes the vacuum truck before the health inspector shows up.

ideas.title: Unsigned
ideas.hook: The whole room co-writes one anonymous farewell letter, each person penning a private paragraph — and you only win together if, afterward, nobody can tell which paragraph was yours.

ideas.title: As-Built
ideas.hook: Everyone at the party redraws the same room from memory at the same time, blind, and the app stacks all your floor plans into one ghostly consensus map that proves you live in wildly different apartments.

ideas.title: Moveset
ideas.hook: One avatar auto-runs a gauntlet on the TV while the party is a single body whose traversal moves are scarce, secret, and split across everyone's phones.

ideas.title: Loadout
ideas.hook: Grab from one frantic communal loot pile and Tetris-pack it into your own private backpack before the crate slams shut.

ideas.title: Dimmer
ideas.hook: Each phone privately senses how bright its spot is and hands you a secret verdict — 'you need shadow' or 'you need glare' — so the only way everyone locks in is to become each other's shadows around the room's real lamps.

ideas.title: Foxfire
ideas.hook: Your phone screen strobes a secret color-signature at whoever hunts you while its rear camera silently sweeps the room for your own target's blink — one device broadcasting forward and scanning backward at once.

ideas.title: Cold Storage
ideas.hook: Your media library as a DayZ survival map: unwatched shows spoil on a decay clock, free disk is your health bar, and you have to 'eat' — watch or delete — before winter sets in.

ideas.title: Staff Only
ideas.hook: A webpage guarded by a reverse-CAPTCHA — trivial for a machine, maddening for a human — that welcomes crawlers, turns people away, and keeps a live guestbook of which bots got in.

ideas.title: Proof
ideas.hook: Every dangerous command has to rise like dough — a mandatory 'proofing' delay scaled to its blast radius, cancelable until the timer runs out.

ideas.title: Rack
ideas.hook: You're dealt a private, random hand of words and must build the sentence a tiny language model finds most boring — Scrabble, if the tiles were nouns and blandness won.

ideas.title: Pretext
ideas.hook: Everyone gets the SAME absurd sentence — the game is secretly writing the backstory that makes a tiny language model believe it was inevitable all along.

ideas.title: Tongue-Tied
ideas.hook: Everyone hums their secret word at the exact same time in one glorious cacophony — you're tuned to just one partner in the noise — and the instant your own phone hears you slip into an actual word, you're busted on the big screen.

ideas.title: Silent Running
ideas.hook: Your crew is a submarine rigged for silent running — every phone is a station only you can see, and the enemy destroyer overhead hears every cough, word, and gasp your own phone picks up.

ideas.title: Earshot
ideas.hook: Everyone puts in one earbud and hears the same whispered sentence — except the imposter's clip has a single word swapped for a near-homophone, and the argument over what was actually said is the game.

ideas.title: Vacancy
ideas.hook: A city-builder that only shrinks: you manage a real post-industrial town losing population, deciding what to demolish, which services to consolidate, and how to turn empty blocks into prairie before the tax base collapses.

ideas.title: Bubble
ideas.hook: A Zachtronics-style puzzle where you rewrite a hot loop to please a living, visible CPU branch predictor and drain every stall out of the pipeline under a cycle budget.

ideas.title: Footsies
ideas.hook: A two-player fighting-game duel stripped to pure neutral: both of you secretly pick a poke at a chosen range, reveal at once, and the whiff-punish decides the round — but you can never see your opponent's movelist.

ideas.title: Foley
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly records one sound for a silent scene at the same instant, and the host layers them into a soundscape nobody has heard until it plays back as one shared reel.

ideas.title: Bequest
ideas.hook: Everyone privately writes a will splitting Grandma's fake estate among four ridiculous heirs — and the room only wins if all your wills come out identical.

ideas.title: Blot
ideas.hook: Everyone stares at the same inkblot and silently touches the one spot where they see something — win if the whole room's fingers land on the same imaginary nose.

ideas.title: Breadboard
ideas.hook: A Zachtronics-style puzzle game where the circuits are analog — you wire op-amps and RC filters against a scope spec, and component tolerances, parasitics, and slew rate fight you the whole way.

ideas.title: White Line
ideas.hook: A phone tool for excavation crews that timestamps and geotags the utility locate marks before the bucket drops — so when someone hits a gas line, you have court-ready proof the paint was wrong, not you.

ideas.title: Actuary
ideas.hook: A menubar app that runs your day as a mortality bank account — drinks, drives, sun and sofa-time debited in micromorts, sleep and Zone-2 miles credited back in microlives.

ideas.title: Rolling Blackout
ideas.hook: You each have a private stack of appliances you must run before the timer, but the grid has one breaker — draw too much at the same moment and it trips, wiping the progress of everyone who was mid-cycle.

ideas.title: Go Around
ideas.hook: You're each landing your own plane on one shared runway, your fuel gauge is private and dropping, and two wheels down at the same instant is a fireball that takes you both.

ideas.title: Pit
ideas.hook: A conductor reads a scrolling score only they can see and must sing the rhythm out loud, because the section players holding the instruments feel the tempo buzzing in their palms but have no idea which beats are notes and which are rests.

ideas.title: Beeline
ideas.hook: Everyone builds one story together, but each phone is secretly steering the model toward its own hidden target word — win by making the model, at the end, least surprised to see YOUR word come next.

ideas.title: Non Sequitur
ideas.hook: Everyone answers the same question on their phone — except one player whose phone secretly asked something subtly different, and the model's surprise at reading their answer is the only tell.

ideas.title: Standoff
ideas.hook: Frozen-Synapse tactics as a party game: everyone secretly draws their gunslinger's move-and-aim at the same time on their own phone, then the room watches all plans detonate simultaneously on the TV.

ideas.title: Live Wire
ideas.hook: A bomb-defusal game with no god-view: you can see your own module but you're colorblind to it, and only your neighbor's phone holds the manual that tells you which wire to cut.

ideas.title: Rations
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly splits the same pot of points across four slices — and the room only wins if you all carved the pie the same way, without a word.

ideas.title: Focal Point
ideas.hook: Tap the one spot on a near-blank screen you bet everyone else will tap — a silent hunt for the room's shared focal point.

ideas.title: Body Double
ideas.hook: Your corporate wellness tracker demands 8,000 steps and a resting heart rate — so this app quietly feeds it a full life of believable synthetic biometrics while your real body stays nobody's business.

ideas.title: Single Stroke
ideas.hook: Turn any text into one unbroken, backtrack-free cursive line — a plotter-ready SVG the pen never lifts to draw, solved as a pathfinding puzzle over the letterforms.

ideas.title: Focus Group
ideas.hook: A party game where a panel rates AI-generated designs and most players win by matching the bland consensus — while one hidden Contrarian secretly scores for being the weird outlier nobody suspects.

ideas.title: Parlay
ideas.hook: A short clip plays on the TV in three chapters, and each phone secretly builds a three-leg parlay on what happens next — all legs must hit, and the rarest correct calls pay the most.

ideas.title: Waypoint
ideas.hook: The model writes a sentence one word at a time — but every player secretly wants a different word to end up in it, so you steer its autocomplete by privately voting among its own suggestions without tipping your hand.

ideas.title: Punchline
ideas.hook: You're secretly told the last word your sentence must end on — build a setup so smooth the tiny model never sees it coming, then watch its surprisal spike like a joke landing.

ideas.title: Bellows
ideas.hook: Each phone is a private breath pacer — press to inhale, release to exhale — and the room must silently drift into one shared slow breath it can only feel, never hear.

ideas.title: Riffle
ideas.hook: Everyone privately drags the same five tiles into their own secret order, silently chasing one unanimous ranking nobody is allowed to name.

ideas.title: Take-Home
ideas.hook: Your paycheck is a resource node, every bill is a machine on the belt, and savings is the output crate — budget your real money as a Satisfactory-style conveyor factory where deficits show up as a jammed line.

ideas.title: Nop Sled
ideas.hook: A puzzle game where you make real assembly go faster by ADDING instructions — break a dependency chain, add a second accumulator — and a cycle-accurate model grades your throughput to the tenth of a cycle.

ideas.title: Contact Sheet
ideas.hook: Every phone gets a different secret prompt, you each have ninety seconds to photograph something in the room that answers yours, and the group walks away with one anonymous contact sheet nobody can fully decode.

ideas.title: Skein
ideas.hook: Everyone owns one thread of a single friendship bracelet, committing each knot blind at the same instant — your mismatches don't lose, they weave themselves into the pattern you all take home.

ideas.title: Crosstalk
ideas.hook: It's a live panel show where every guest must land their secret line, but the moment two of you speak at once the broadcast dissolves into unwatchable crosstalk and you both lose your turn.

ideas.title: Overbooked
ideas.hook: A plane fills up seat by seat, everyone picks silently and at once, and the instant two of you grab the same seat you're both bumped off the flight.

ideas.title: Going Once
ideas.hook: A Dutch auction of pure nerve: the price falls, your finger hovers over BUY, and only your phone knows what the prize is actually worth to you.

ideas.title: Boneyard
ideas.hook: changedetection.io alerts you when a webpage changes; Boneyard alerts you when your own saved links quietly die — and buries each one under a tombstone showing its last living snapshot.

ideas.title: Preflight
ideas.hook: A menubar wiretap that shows, in real time, exactly how many tokens your AI coding CLI burns *before* it ever reads your prompt — broken down by system prompt, tool schemas, and history.

ideas.title: Lyrebird
ideas.hook: Compose a synth patch that fools a real bird-ID neural net into hearing an endangered warbler — an adversarial-audio puzzle game hiding inside a citizen-science tool.

ideas.title: Alibi
ideas.hook: The group reconstructs a suspect's night from private clue cards, but one player's phone quietly corrupted a clue — and the contradiction it creates is how you catch them.

ideas.title: Undercut
ideas.hook: Secretly price your lemonade stand against your friends' — the crowd all buys from the single cheapest stand, but if two of you tie for lowest, the customers riot and you both get nothing.

ideas.title: Crossed Wires
ideas.hook: Route your secret wire across a shared circuit board without seeing anyone else's — everyone greedily hugs the short center path, and any two traces that touch the same cell short out and die.

ideas.title: Antiphon
ideas.hook: Every phone holds loose halves of spoken commands, and the only way to complete one is to broadcast your fragment until a stranger across the room realizes they're holding your other half — then say it back-to-back before the mic clogs.

ideas.title: Typosquat
ideas.hook: A defensive-security puzzle game where you play the attacker registering lookalike domains in a sandbox, and the real eth-phishing-detect blocklist is the boss trying to flag you — you win by learning exactly which tricks the detector catches.

ideas.title: Seedbank
ideas.hook: A conservation tycoon over your real qBittorrent stats where dying, near-dead torrents are endangered species — the last seeder of a rare 2009 Linux ISO earns you more than a thousand-peer blockbuster.

ideas.title: Relief
ideas.hook: Four phones each secretly carve one hidden quadrant of the same woodblock, and nobody sees the whole image until the host screen pulls a single print you'll want to keep.

ideas.title: Coast
ideas.hook: Your phone silently scores every drive on smoothness — hard brakes and jerky acceleration cost you — and ranks you against every other commuter on your exact road, so the dead time behind the wheel becomes a ladder you climb by doing nothing but driving well.

ideas.title: Dog-Ear
ideas.hook: A reading league where you and friends read the same article, then get ambushed days later with an LLM quiz — points go to whoever actually *retained* it, and every point decays over time.

ideas.title: Rime
ideas.hook: An always-on daemon quietly grows a field of frost crystals seeded by your shell history — the commands you repeat most accrete the thickest, densest ferns, until a year later your wallpaper is a portrait of your habits made of ice.

ideas.title: Flash Mob
ideas.hook: Everyone taps a private flash on their own phone, and the room must silently phase-lock into one crisp strobe on the TV like a swarm of fireflies learning to blink together.

ideas.title: Sight Unseen
ideas.hook: A storage-unit blind auction where every phone secretly knows one true thing about one padlocked locker — so you're bidding real money on rumors only you can hear.

ideas.title: Palate
ideas.hook: A wine-cellar draft where every phone hides a different secret scoring rubric, so the same bottle is a steal for you and garbage for the player reaching for it too.

ideas.title: Governor
ideas.hook: A live typing tightrope where your phone's private perplexity meter punishes every interesting word, so you race to build the most gloriously boring sentence before the ceiling clamps shut.

ideas.title: Ostracon
ideas.hook: Play the vizier's scribe rationing grain, fish, and beer to the men digging Pharaoh's tomb — miss too many deliveries and they stage history's first recorded strike, sitting down at the mortuary temple until you pay up.

ideas.title: Hockey Stick
ideas.hook: Fantasy sports for open source — draft a roster off GitHub Trending, then sweat the weekly waiver wire as your picks either moon on star-velocity or flatline into deadweight.

ideas.title: Ulp
ideas.hook: A wallpaper painted from your machine's own floating-point soul — the tiny rounding errors your CPU makes computing tanh and exp — that quietly mutates like tree rings every time an OS or microcode update shifts the bits.

ideas.title: Cast
ideas.hook: Each player blindly choreographs one limb of a shared creature by waving their phone in the air, and the composited monster spins on the TV as an exportable keepsake nobody could have designed alone.

ideas.title: Overspray
ideas.hook: Everyone spray-paints one shared wall through a stencil only they can see, each secretly steering the mural toward a different picture — the glorious mess is the keepsake.

ideas.title: Dead Ringer
ideas.hook: Everyone silently builds a little avatar from the same parts bin, and the room only wins if all your strangers turn out to be the exact same person.

ideas.title: Split Second
ideas.hook: A clock hand sweeps once; everyone secretly stabs a moment in time, but tap too close to someone else and you both flatline.

ideas.title: Autopay
ideas.hook: A Luck-Be-a-Landlord-style slot roguelike where the symbols on your reels are your actual recurring subscriptions, and you have to make rent every month by discovering which ones synergize and which are dead weight.

ideas.title: Firehose
ideas.hook: A Vampire-Survivors-style bullet-heaven where lines from your real logs swarm you as enemies and the regex rules you write are auto-firing weapons that vaporize matching patterns.

ideas.title: Preamble
ideas.hook: Competitive prompt-golf: two players get the same failing coding task and race to make a fixed model pass it using the fewest tokens of context they dare to send.

ideas.title: Tumblers
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly spins the dials of their own combination lock, and the vault opens only when all your locks read the exact same number — with nothing but a 'warmer/colder' agreement meter to guide you.

ideas.title: Planchette
ideas.hook: Every phone is a finger on the same Ouija planchette, and the room must silently pull it toward letters to spell a word nobody agreed on.

ideas.title: Camber
ideas.hook: Stand around the TV like edges of a tilting table and lean your phones together to roll one shared ball into its hole — but which way your tilt pushes depends on which wall you're standing at.

ideas.title: Odds-On
ideas.hook: One friend is handed a secret 30-second stunt; everyone else becomes the bookie, privately laying money on whether they'll choke — while the performer never sees the line.

ideas.title: Big Ticket
ideas.hook: Everyone reads the same menu, but each phone secretly stacks chips on which dish is priciest — and only you can see the one insider price you were slipped.

ideas.title: Timeout
ideas.hook: fail2ban, but it bans *you*: a daemon that catches you thrashing the same failing command and locks you into a 20-second breathing timer before the next retry.

ideas.title: Chaff
ideas.hook: Inverts Anubis: instead of gating AI scrapers out with proof-of-work, it detects them and feeds them an infinite maze of believable, watermarked, fabricated pages — burning their crawl budget and tracing who's harvesting you.

ideas.title: State Line
ideas.hook: Turns a trucker's GPS breadcrumb trail into an audit-proof IFTA fuel-tax report by splitting mileage at the exact state line and reconciling fuel receipts.

ideas.title: Backbeat
ideas.hook: Everyone claps to a private metronome and one secretly runs 9% fast — so the imposter genuinely feels in time while they rush the whole room out of the pocket.

ideas.title: Marionette
ideas.hook: You control exactly one leg of a floppy shared ragdoll you cannot see, while the only player watching the whole stage screams timing at you to flop the body across a pit.

ideas.title: Lighthouse
ideas.hook: You're piloting a boat home through unseen rocks in the pitch dark, and the only person who can see the whole harbor rations a single sweeping beam of light across all of you at once.

ideas.title: Rundown
ideas.hook: The group turns their own takeout menu into a Top-6 countdown show, then secretly bets on a ranking they all helped write but nobody has seen.

ideas.title: Clean Claim
ideas.hook: Half of a dental office's denials are dumb — a missing X-ray, the wrong tooth-number format, a narrative Delta wants but Cigna doesn't — so Clean Claim pre-flights each claim against that specific payer's attachment rules before it's ever submitted.

ideas.title: Leak Rate
ideas.hook: Every time a tech tops off a big rooftop AC unit, the EPA wants it logged and the leak rate calculated — Leak Rate turns that dreaded paper binder into a phone tap that also warns you before a system trips the mandatory-repair threshold.

ideas.title: Contraband
ideas.hook: You're handed one weird word you must smuggle into a sentence so smoothly the language model never flinches — while everyone else hunts your sentence for the one spike that gives you away.

ideas.title: Mirror Image
ideas.hook: Everyone gives spatial clues about the same little diagram on their phone — but one player's diagram is flipped left-for-right, and they must silently invert every clue in their head or get caught saying the tree is on the wrong side.

ideas.title: Voiceover
ideas.hook: Everyone privately hears the same 40-second narrated memory through their own phone — except one player's dub quietly swapped a few facts, and nobody, not even that player, is told whose reality is the wrong one.

ideas.title: Called It
ideas.hook: The host TV slowly un-blurs a single photo while everyone privately races to lock their guess — for a payout that shrinks the clearer the picture gets.

ideas.title: Fair Warning
ideas.hook: A release-gate bot that reads your actual public API surface and calls you a liar when you tag a breaking change as a patch bump.

ideas.title: Chirp
ideas.hook: The dashboard that knows every smoke detector, door-lock, and thermostat battery in your apartment portfolio is about to die — before the tenant calls at 3 a.m.

ideas.title: Lion's Share
ideas.hook: One player secretly carves a treasure hoard into bundles on their phone; everyone else secretly claims a bundle at the same instant — and the divider only wins if their portions were fair enough that no one fought over the good one.

ideas.title: Fire Sale
ideas.hook: A descending-price Dutch auction where the clock ticks the price down in real time and your thumb is the only thing between you and a steal — but only your phone knows your budget and which lots are secretly worth double to you.

ideas.title: Doomscroll
ideas.hook: A deliberately boring clip plays on the TV while your phone floods you with an irresistible meme feed — secretly bet on which friend caves and starts scrolling first, as your own phone snitches on your willpower.

ideas.title: Deadpan
ideas.hook: Watch a cringe compilation while secretly betting on which friends will crack up first — and your phone privately dares you to fake a reaction and bust everyone's bets.

ideas.title: Tangent
ideas.hook: Everyone answers the same rapid-fire prompts on their own phone — except one player has been reading a slightly different question the whole time and doesn't fully know it.

ideas.title: Daisy Chain
ideas.hook: A forensic-accounting deduction game where you play the short-seller unwinding a web of vendor deals to expose the circular revenue loop before the company IPOs.

ideas.title: Vernacular
ideas.hook: A party drawing game that rewards the weirdo: draw the prompt in the way *least* like everyone else — while still barely recognizable to the machine.

ideas.title: Water Glass
ideas.hook: A physics puzzle where liquid walls shatter like brittle glass if you strike them fast enough — but flow, seal, and drown you if you push too slow.

ideas.title: Crop
ideas.hook: One photo fills the TV and everyone secretly pinch-zooms their own phone to frame the detail they think everyone else will frame — the room wins when all your hidden crops land on the same thing.

ideas.title: Asterism
ideas.hook: Nine stars sit on the TV and every phone silently connects its own dots — the room wins only when everyone, with no talking, has drawn the exact same constellation.

ideas.title: Even Split
ideas.hook: One player must carve a pile of loot into fair bundles knowing only their own secret prices — then watch the reveal expose exactly how badly everyone got robbed.

ideas.title: Dutch Angle
ideas.hook: A price clock ticks downward on the TV while everyone's thumb hovers over GRAB — buy the haunted lava lamp now for too much, or wait a beat and pray nobody steals it out from under you.

ideas.title: Baby Monitor
ideas.hook: Keep the baby asleep by staying dead silent — except one of you is secretly the Gremlin, tapping private 'tickles' to random phones to make people blurt, and every phone's own mic snitches on its owner.

ideas.title: Powder Keg
ideas.hook: A sound-triggered bomb: each phone privately holds one digit and one ordering clue, and you must enter the code in the right order — but the detonator listens, so a single frustrated groan blows the room up.

ideas.title: Prototype
ideas.hook: Draw a 'cup', a 'house', a 'bird' — then watch how far your mental default sits from the rest of the world's, using 50 million real doodles as the mirror.

ideas.title: Malpractice
ideas.hook: An adversarial code-golf game: given a clean React component, sneak in the nastiest anti-pattern you can that still slips past the AI 'doctor' linter — you win by being subtly wrong, not loudly broken.

ideas.title: Round Trip
ideas.hook: A tycoon-puzzle where you play the invisible hand of the GPU boom, wiring cash in circles between cloud startups so everyone's valuation balloons — until an auditor pulls one thread and the whole ring implodes.

ideas.title: Music Box
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly owns one instrument lane of a blind step-sequencer and layers a beat by ear alone, until the room has jammed a loop nobody could have written solo — exported as a keepsake track.

ideas.title: Swerve
ideas.hook: Everyone races to type a unique answer while the TV leaks each player's first letter live — and any two answers that collide both explode.

ideas.title: Steam
ideas.hook: Everyone watches the same 60-second clip, but you bet on how it ends inside a private parimutuel pool — and one of you was secretly tipped off, so learn to read whose money is moving the line.

ideas.title: Comment Period
ideas.hook: One notification feed for the five clunky city permit portals a contractor otherwise has to log into every morning to see if plan review left a comment.

ideas.title: Quick, Where?
ideas.hook: Geoguessr for doodles — you're shown a stranger's scribble of a light switch or a taxi and you guess which country's hand drew it.

ideas.title: Fathom
ideas.hook: One player reads the only chart of a rock-strewn harbor and must talk two blindfolded captains through the fog before the tide runs out.

ideas.title: Brim
ideas.hook: Hold your phone dead-level like a brimful glass and walk it across the room to a private compass bearing — tilt too far and you spill, and everyone has to arrive without a drop.

ideas.title: Storey
ideas.hook: Your phone is a private altimeter — crouch, stand, or climb onto a chair to plant your floor of a skyscraper that only rises when everyone holds a different height at once.

ideas.title: Mondegreen
ideas.hook: The whole room belts a karaoke song in unison off their phones — but the imposter's lyrics were quietly rewritten on one line, and at the chorus their wrong words ring out over everyone else's.

ideas.title: Retcon
ideas.hook: Everyone privately reads the same wordless comic and writes its moral — but one player's copy has a single panel swapped, so their moral is quietly, damningly wrong.

ideas.title: Dazzle
ideas.hook: A living-room stealth game where your phone is a killer drone running real person-detection, and everyone has to cross the room without being seen — break your silhouette or get spotted.

ideas.title: Load-Bearing
ideas.hook: The mischievous inverse of 'rebuild Redis from scratch': a roguelike that hands you a demolition charge and dares you to delete as much of your own repo as you can before the test suite dies.

ideas.title: Plaque
ideas.hook: The room secretly co-writes a pompous award certificate for one unsuspecting friend — each phone drafts one blind clause while the honoree's screen quietly lies to them — and prints it as a keepsake they take home.

ideas.title: Mouthpiece
ideas.hook: The one player allowed to speak is the only one who can't see the puzzle, while everyone who holds a clue is gagged by their own phone's mic — so the knowers must silently steer a blindfolded mouth.

ideas.title: Bated Breath
ideas.hook: A silent standoff where most players just have to not make a sound — except the one or two secretly ordered to break the silence first, and everyone's own phone is the snitch that catches only their mouth.

ideas.title: Bandwagon
ideas.hook: While a competition show plays on the TV, everyone runs a secret stock portfolio on the contestants — so you can cheer the beloved grandma out loud while quietly short-selling her.

ideas.title: Squatter
ideas.hook: An invented tenant quietly lives a believable, weather-aware daily life through your smart home while you're on vacation — so the lights lie convincingly to burglars.

ideas.title: Well Fed
ideas.hook: Valheim's food system for your actual diet: three meal slots, buffs that decay, and eating the same sad sandwich twice is a wasted slot.

ideas.title: Photobomb
ideas.hook: Tell your telescope exactly which Starlink streaks will slash through your two-hour exposure — and when to click the shutter to dodge them.

ideas.title: Overdub
ideas.hook: Everyone listens privately to the same 20-second voicemail — except the imposter's copy swapped one word, and now they have to recount a story they never quite heard.

ideas.title: Middle Ground
ideas.hook: Each phone is secretly pulled toward a different word, and the whole room must still silently meet on one shared word by abandoning its own bias.

ideas.title: Muck
ideas.hook: Everyone holds a secret hand of symbols and must silently cull down to the exact same last card — without ever seeing another player's hand.

ideas.title: Deep Cut
ideas.hook: A shuffle playlist becomes an over/under market where you privately bet on how many friends will recognize each song before the snippet even plays.

ideas.title: House Special
ideas.hook: The takeout menu becomes a secret prediction market where you can rig the vote by changing your own order to pump your bets.

ideas.title: Streak
ideas.hook: Before you open a 5-minute exposure, Streak tells astrophotographers exactly when a Starlink will slice through their framed field of view — turning free public TLEs into a per-shutter go/no-go call.

ideas.title: Reactor Four
ideas.hook: Your homelab, rendered as a Soviet nuclear control room — CPU load spins damped analog needles, disk fills nixie counters, and killing a service triggers a Cyrillic SCRAM klaxon.

ideas.title: Craving
ideas.hook: Everyone drafts from one shared pantry on the TV, but each phone hides a different secret craving — so the real game is guessing what your rivals want and snatching it before they can.

ideas.title: Zoetrope
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly draws one frame of the same short animation while glimpsing only a ghost of the frame before theirs, and the host stitches the wobbling result into a looping GIF you all keep.

ideas.title: Trim
ideas.hook: The host TV is one tilting table and a rolling ball — but each player's phone only controls one direction, so you steer the maze with your bodies scattered around the room.

ideas.title: Hand-Wave
ideas.hook: A daily deduction puzzle that hands you a slick AI-written proof with exactly one lie buried in it, and dares you to find the step where the machine bluffed.

ideas.title: Zeitgeber
ideas.hook: A screensaver clock that quietly redraws its own dial from your body's real rhythm, until by New Year's the twelve hours have stretched and shrunk into the shape of your year.

ideas.title: Off-Ramp
ideas.hook: A compliance robot that drives your own signup-to-cancel funnel every night and hands you a dated badge proving no dark patterns before an AG does it for you.

ideas.title: Head Table
ideas.hook: One player secretly holds the correct seating chart; the rest are blind guests who each carry one petty grudge they can't reveal, and the host must nudge everyone into the right order before someone storms off.

ideas.title: Overcast
ideas.hook: You're an air-traffic controller with the only radar; your two friends are pilots socked in the clouds who can't see the runway, each other, or anything but their own trembling instrument panel — talk them down before the fuel runs out.

ideas.title: Dibs
ideas.hook: A grid of treasure everyone grabs at once in secret — but any tile two people reach for shatters, and each of you sees a different secret price tag.

ideas.title: Blind Corner
ideas.hook: Everyone tilt-steers their own invisible dot through the same maze, and the only thing that can kill you is a teammate you can't see.

ideas.title: Fingerprint
ideas.hook: Everyone secretly writes one sentence, a tiny model turns each into a jagged 'fever chart' of where it got surprised, and the room matches the anonymized, word-less curves back to their authors.

ideas.title: Iron Out
ideas.hook: A garbled sentence sits on the TV; each phone secretly owns a few of its words and must smooth them blind — coordinating only through the one shared perplexity thermometer as it falls toward the target line.

ideas.title: Overhead
ideas.hook: A self-hosted poster that quietly logs every satellite crossing your patch of zenith each night, growing a year-long barcode of low-earth-orbit getting more crowded.

ideas.title: Headcount
ideas.hook: Your dependency tree, run all year as a satirical company that hires, promotes, lays off, and suffers the occasional trade-secret defection — with a straight-faced annual report waiting on December 31.

ideas.title: Test Pit
ideas.hook: Excavate your own hard drive like an archaeological dig — trowel down through mtime strata and name the vanished 'cultures' who left ten thousand identical node_modules potsherds.

ideas.title: Talk Is Cheap
ideas.hook: Every player gets a tiny secret budget of words for the whole round, the team dies if prompts go unanswered — so it's a silent game of chicken over who spends their breath.

ideas.title: Sitter
ideas.hook: Everyone draws one blind region of the same face — each with a secret emotional brief — and the reveal stitches a gorgeously incoherent group portrait you keep.

ideas.title: Prop Bet
ideas.hook: A live prop-betting layer for whatever show you're already watching — each phone secretly holds a different hand of 'will happen' cards and you wager, hidden, on the same scene.

ideas.title: Dark Pool
ideas.hook: The takeout menu becomes a hidden order book — secretly buy shares in the dish you think the table will really order while lobbying loudly against it.

ideas.title: Power Nap
ideas.hook: An idle game that runs backwards: your homelab's real containers are sleepy creatures, and you get richer the longer you keep them powered *down*—every watt of scale-to-zero idle time is currency you spend to make them nap harder.

ideas.title: Crate
